A user leaves a hidden area only by removing it themselves. If you need people off an area, tell them; see Hiding an area from your users.

docs.title: "You can select at most N areas"
docs.text:
Problem: Saving areas, switching on a geofence, or saving an alarm limited to specific areas answers "You can select at most N areas" or "An alarm can be limited to at most N areas", and a bulk Change radius stores less than was asked for.

Solution: That's PoracleNG's [tracking] max_areas and max_distance, which PoracleWeb.NET applies itself because the writes it sends skip PoracleNG's own check. Raise or remove the settings in PoracleNG's config (0 or absent means no limit) and restart PoracleNG; PoracleWeb.NET reads the values on every save, so nothing on its side needs restarting. A list stored before the limit was lowered can still be saved again or made shorter. PoracleNG's admins and destinations that aren't people are not limited. See PoracleNG compatibility.

docs.title: A geofence saved but not switched on
docs.text:
Problem: After drawing a geofence the user sees "Saved, but it couldn't be switched on yet. Use the toggle to retry."

Solution: The geofence row is saved and PoracleNG then refused or missed the name on the user's profile, most often because PoracleNG was unreachable or hadn't reloaded its geofences yet, or because the profile was already at PoracleNG's max_areas (see above). The user flips the toggle on the Geofences page to retry (it reloads PoracleNG's geofences and retries once; a second failure answers a 409). Check that PoracleNG is up and that geofence.path points at /api/geofence-feed. See also Custom geofences troubleshooting.

docs.title: Geofence names not matching in Poracle
docs.text:
Problem: Custom geofences don't trigger alerts even though they're in the user's area list.

Solution: Poracle does case-sensitive area matching. Geofence names must always be lowercase. The kojiName field in user_geofences and entries in a profile's area list must match exactly. UserGeofenceService.CreateAsync() enforces this with ToLowerInvariant().

docs.title: Koji displayInMatches not working
docs.text:
Problem: User geofence names appear in DMs even though displayInMatches is set to false.

Solution: Koji's displayInMatches custom property is not reliably honored by all Poracle format serializers. Serve user geofences from the PoracleWeb.NET feed endpoint (/api/geofence-feed) instead of pushing them to Koji. Only promote to Koji when an admin approves a geofence for public use.

docs.title: Rate limiting locking out all users
docs.text:
Problem: Multiple users report being unable to log in simultaneously.

Solution: Auth rate limiting must be per-IP (partitioned), not global. Check that Program.cs uses RateLimitPartition.GetFixedWindowLimiter keyed by RemoteIpAddress, not AddFixedWindowLimiter.

docs.title: Gym, raid or egg alarms never fire
docs.text:
Problem: Gym alarms match nothing, even though no specific gym was selected.

Solution: gym_id is nullable, and PoracleNG reads any non-NULL value — including '' — as "only this gym", which an empty string matches nowhere. Alarms created through the PoracleNG API proxy get this right; the rows that need fixing were written directly to the database by PoracleWeb.NET before v2.0.0.

Old gym rows can also carry team = 0, which means Neutral only rather than any team.

-- Diagnose
SELECT uid, id, gym_id, team FROM gym WHERE gym_id = '' OR team = 0;

-- Fix
UPDATE gym SET gym_id = NULL WHERE gym_id = '';
UPDATE egg SET gym_id = NULL WHERE gym_id = '';
UPDATE raid SET gym_id = NULL WHERE gym_id = '';
UPDATE gym SET team = 4 WHERE team = 0;

docs.title: Profile switches at wrong time
docs.text:
Problem: Auto-profile switches happen hours earlier or later than the configured active hours schedule.

Solution: The profile has 0,0 coordinates, so PoracleNG's scheduler falls back to UTC instead of the user's local timezone. Set the pin on the affected profile via the Dashboard or the Areas & places page. The Profiles page shows a red location warning banner on profiles that have no coordinates set.

docs.title: Active hours not showing on profiles
docs.text:
Problem: All profiles display "Manual only" even though active hours were configured via the Discord bot.

Solution: PoracleWeb.NET reads active hours from PoracleNG's profile API responses — they should appear automatically. If they don't:

  1. Verify PoracleNG is reachable (Poracle:ApiAddress)
  2. Check that PoracleNG is returning active_hours in profile responses (GET /api/v2/humans/{id}/profiles should list each profile with its active_hours)
  3. If active hours were set via $!profile bot commands, they are stored in the same place PoracleWeb.NET reads from — no separate sync is needed

docs.title: Schedule changes don't take effect
docs.text:
Problem: After saving active hours in PoracleWeb.NET, the profile doesn't auto-switch at the expected time.

Solution: PoracleNG's profile scheduler checks on a periodic cycle (every few minutes) with a 10-minute matching window. Changes saved in PoracleWeb.NET are written to PoracleNG immediately, but the scheduler picks them up on its next cycle. Wait up to 10 minutes for changes to take effect.

PoracleNG owns the scheduler

PoracleWeb.NET only manages the active hours data. The actual profile switching logic runs in PoracleNG's processor. If auto-switching isn't working at all, check PoracleNG's logs for scheduler errors.

docs.title: Maps are watermarked, blocked, blank, or ignoring the setting
docs.text:
Symptom: Every map on the site — areas, the location picker, geofence thumbnails — shows one of: diagonal API KEY REQUIRED text, black-and-yellow 403 Access blocked tiles, nothing at all, or a basemap that is not the one configured.

A tile provider refusing you still answers HTTP 200

Both CARTO and OpenStreetMap draw their refusal into the image and return success. Nothing appears in the container logs, no health check fails, and the browser's network tab shows 200s. The only place these faults are visible is on the map itself, so do not go looking for an error.

Causes and fixes:

  1. API KEY REQUIRED across the tiles. A CARTO or Stadia basemap is being requested without a key. Set Basemap API key in Admin > Server settings > Maps. Takes effect on the next page load, no restart.

  2. Still watermarked after setting a key. The key is wrong, not missing. The site can detect an absent key and avoid the request; it cannot detect an invalid one, because the response is identical. Check the key itself, and — for a custom tile URL — check the parameter name. CARTO's is key, not api_key; the wrong name also returns 200 and also watermarks.

  3. 403 Access blocked — App is not following the tile usage policy. OpenStreetMap refuses requests it cannot identify. The built-in OpenStreetMap entry handles this by sending the site's origin on its tile images. If you see this, you are on a custom tile URL pointing at tile.openstreetmap.org rather than the built-in entry — switch the provider to OpenStreetMap, which carries the required behaviour.

  4. Blank map, no tiles, no message. A custom tile URL over plain http://. The site's Content-Security-Policy allows images from https: only, so the browser blocks them silently. Serve your tiles over HTTPS.

  5. Blank map with a custom URL over HTTPS. Check the template. It must be an absolute URL containing Leaflet's {z}, {x} and {y} placeholders. A URL that is not a tile template is never requested at all, and the site falls back to OpenStreetMap and says so in the Maps section.

  6. The basemap is not the one you configured. You have picked a different one for yourself. Each viewer's choice is stored per-browser and outranks the site setting, so an admin who clicked the layers button once while testing will see every later change to the setting do nothing. Open the layers button on any map and choose Site default. The Maps section says so when it applies to the admin reading it.

  7. The Maps section shows a key field on an install you never configured. You are running a build older than the fix that made "not set" mean OpenStreetMap. Older builds resolved an unset provider to CARTO, then fell back, so they asked for a key nobody had chosen. Update.

Diagnostic:

# Fetch a tile the way the browser does and look at the bytes.
# A refusal tile is small (~7 KB); a real one is much larger.
curl -s -o /tmp/tile.png -w '%{http_code} %{size_download} bytes\n' \
  'https://tile.openstreetmap.org/11/582/792.png'

# Same tile, identified. If this one is large and the first was small,
# the provider is refusing anonymous requests rather than failing.
curl -s -o /tmp/tile-ref.png -w '%{http_code} %{size_download} bytes\n' \
  -H 'Referer: https://your-site.example/' \
  'https://tile.openstreetmap.org/11/582/792.png'

# Then open both images. The refusal is legible.

In the browser, the active basemap and why it was chosen are visible without any tooling: open the layers button on a map. The entry marked active is what you are looking at, and a line beneath the list names the problem when the configured basemap could not be drawn.

See Site Settings > Maps for the full setting reference.

docs.title: Pokemon availability not showing
docs.text:
Symptom: The "Live > Spawning" filter doesn't appear in the Pokemon selector.

Causes and fixes:

  1. Golbat not configured. Set GOLBAT_API_ADDRESS and GOLBAT_API_SECRET in .env and restart the container. The feature is only enabled when both are set.

  2. Env vars not reaching the container. The compose file loads configuration via env_file: .env, so any var defined in .env is automatically passed in — no per-key entries in docker-compose.yml are needed. If you've customized your docker-compose.yml (a local copy of docker-compose.yml.example), confirm the env_file: .env line is still present under the app service.

  3. Golbat API unreachable from container. Verify connectivity from inside the container. Check the app logs for Failed to fetch available Pokemon from Golbat API warnings.

  4. Wrong API secret. The GOLBAT_API_SECRET must match Golbat's api_secret value in its config.toml. An incorrect secret results in 401 Unauthorised responses.

  5. Browser cache. Hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R) after deploying a new build. The old JavaScript bundle won't have the availability code.

Diagnostic: 

# Test Golbat API from host
curl -H "X-Golbat-Secret: YOUR_SECRET" http://GOLBAT_HOST:9001/api/pokemon/available

# Check if env vars reached the container
docker exec poracleweb.net printenv | grep -i golbat

# Check app logs for Golbat activity
docker logs poracleweb.net 2>&1 | grep -i golbat

docs.title: Quest summary delivery menu is missing
docs.text:
Problem: The Quest summary delivery item does not appear in the Quests page ⋮ menu.

Solution: The menu is shown only when the connected PoracleNG instance reports quest summaries as enabled. PoracleWeb.NET reads the effective tracking.quest_summary_enabled flag from PoracleNG's /api/config/values endpoint (cached for five minutes). If the menu is missing:

  1. Enable the feature on the bot. Set quest_summary_enabled = true under [tracking] in PoracleNG's config.toml and restart the processor.
  2. Make sure the processor API is reachable. PoracleWeb.NET must be able to reach PoracleNG over HTTP. If they run on different machines or in separate containers, set host = "0.0.0.0" (or the LAN IP) under [processor] in PoracleNG's config — the 127.0.0.1 default refuses off-box connections.
  3. Wait out the cache / hard refresh. The capability is cached for five minutes; reload the Quests page (Ctrl+Shift+R) after enabling.

Note

A transient 503 from PoracleNG's summary endpoints is treated as a temporary backend fault, not as "feature off." The feature flag is read from the config endpoint, not inferred from a 503.

docs.title: Send summary now delivers nothing
docs.text:
Problem: Pressing Send summary now succeeds but no summary DM arrives.

Solution: Send summary now flushes only the quests PoracleNG has buffered since your last summary. An empty buffer delivers nothing — which is expected, not an error. To buffer quests:

  1. Enable Daily summary on at least one quest alarm (the per-alarm toggle in the quest add/edit dialog). Only alarms with this toggle are buffered; the rest deliver immediately.
  2. Confirm the feature is enabled on the bot (tracking.quest_summary_enabled = true) — when it is off, PoracleNG's matcher does not buffer at all, so the buffer stays empty.
  3. Give it time. Quests are buffered as they match. Right after enabling the feature, or after a summary fires, the buffer starts empty and fills as matching quests come in. PoracleNG's status log shows the current count (Summary: N buffered).

docs.title: External SSO / OIDC login
docs.text: The issues below cover the generic external OIDC/OAuth2 login provider. For the full settings reference, see External SSO; for the silent-refresh feature, see OIDC Refresh Tokens.

docs.title: "External login failed" / 405 on the token or userinfo call
docs.text:
Problem: The OIDC login starts, the user authenticates at the provider, but the callback redirects to /login#error=oidc_token_exchange_failed (or oidc_userinfo_failed). The provider's logs show a 405 Method Not Allowed on the token or userinfo request.

Solution: Some providers are split-host — the browser-facing authorize endpoint lives on one host (the frontend/login host) while the token and userinfo endpoints live on a separate API host. Pointing OIDC_TOKEN_URL / OIDC_USERINFO_URL at the frontend host hits a static site with no POST handler, which returns 405.

Set each endpoint to its correct host:

OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_URL=https://login.provider.example/oauth2/authorize
OIDC_TOKEN_URL=https://api.provider.example/oauth2/token
OIDC_USERINFO_URL=https://api.provider.example/oauth2/userinfo

Only OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_URL belongs on the frontend host; OIDC_TOKEN_URL and OIDC_USERINFO_URL go to the API host.

docs.title: redirect_uri mismatch / invalid redirect
docs.text:
Problem: The provider rejects the login with an "invalid redirect URI" or "redirect_uri mismatch" error before the user ever reaches PoracleWeb.NET's callback.

Solution: PoracleWeb.NET builds the callback URL as {scheme}://{Host}/api/auth/oidc/callback from the incoming request Host header, and that exact URL must be registered at the IdP. In local development the Angular dev-server proxy preserves Host = localhost:4201, so the callback becomes :4201, not the API's :5048. Register every host that can originate the request as an allowed redirect URI at the provider:

http://localhost:5048/api/auth/oidc/callback
http://localhost:4201/api/auth/oidc/callback
https://poracle.example.com/api/auth/oidc/callback

Include your real production host alongside the two local-dev URIs.

docs.title: 404 after OIDC login in local dev (standalone ng serve)
docs.text:
Problem: Running the Angular dev server standalone, OIDC login completes at the provider but the browser lands on a 404 instead of the dashboard.

Solution: The callback issues a 302 to the Angular client route /auth/oidc/callback#token=…. The committed proxy.conf.json proxies /auth to the API, so the dev server forwards that client route to the API (which has no such route) → 404. Run the dev server with an /api-only proxy so Angular serves /auth/* itself:

{
  "/api": { "target": "http://localhost:5048", "secure": false }
}

A ready-made proxy.local.json is provided for this; start the dev server with ng serve --proxy-config proxy.local.json.

Only affects standalone ng serve

When the API serves the built SPA (Docker, production), there is no separate dev-server proxy and Angular's router handles /auth/oidc/callback directly — this issue does not occur.

docs.title: #error=user_not_registered at the callback
docs.text:
Problem: Login succeeds at the provider but the browser returns to /login#error=user_not_registered.

Solution: The value carried by the configured identity claim has no matching row in the Poracle human table — the SSO user has no Poracle account. PoracleWeb.NET reads OIDC_IDENTITY_CLAIM (default discord_id), then OIDC_SECONDARY_IDENTITY_CLAIM when set, falling back to the standard sub claim only when neither is present, and looks that value up as the Poracle human id. To fix:

  1. Ensure the claim carries the user's Poracle id — a linked Discord or Telegram id, not an internal SSO/email id.
  2. Confirm a matching user actually exists in Poracle (they must have registered with the bot).

PogoAlerts users must link Discord

At PogoAlerts the user must have Discord linked to their account so the provider emits the discord_id claim. Without a linked Discord, no discord_id is sent and the lookup fails.

docs.title: Silent refresh not happening / no refresh token issued
docs.text:
Problem: Sessions still expire at the full JWT lifetime instead of refreshing silently. The app logs "OIDC refresh tokens are enabled but the provider returned no refresh token (offline_access not granted?); falling back to a standard session."

Solution: Standards-compliant providers only issue a refresh token when the offline_access scope is requested and granted. If OIDC_OFFLINE_ACCESS_SCOPE is blanked (or the provider declined to grant it), the token response carries no refresh token, and PoracleWeb.NET gracefully falls back to a normal full-lifetime session — no error is shown to the user.

  1. Set OIDC_USE_REFRESH_TOKENS=true.
  2. Ensure the provider actually issues refresh tokens: leave OIDC_OFFLINE_ACCESS_SCOPE=offline_access (the default) so the scope is requested, or use the provider's own mechanism (e.g. Google's ?access_type=offline).

See OIDC Refresh Tokens for the full setup.

docs.title: Token endpoint returns 400/401 invalid_client
docs.text:
Problem: The token exchange fails with the provider returning 400/401 and an invalid_client error, so the callback redirects to /login#error=oidc_token_exchange_failed.

Solution: OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH_METHOD must match how the provider expects client credentials presented:

  • client_secret_post — credentials sent in the request body.
  • client_secret_basic — credentials sent in the HTTP Basic Authorization header.

Match the provider's expectation: Keycloak and Okta default to client_secret_basic; Auth0, Azure, and PogoAlerts use client_secret_post.

docs.title: Locked out after switching to SSO (provider down / misconfigured)
docs.text:
Problem: An admin set enable_oidc to SSO mode, the login page now auto-redirects to the provider, and the provider is down or misconfigured — nobody can sign in to fix it.

Solution: This is the break-glass scenario. Set the env flag and restart:

AUTH_FORCE_LOCAL=true

This forces the local login page regardless of the enable_oidc mode, so an admin can sign in and disable or repair the OIDC configuration. Once fixed, remove the flag and restart.

Admins can always reach local login

Even when enable_oidc is off (or a provider is broken), admins can always reach the local login page — the enable_oidc gate is enforced after authentication so an admin is never locked out of re-enabling or fixing the setting.

docs.title: "Sign out everywhere" 404s / single logout doesn't end the provider session
docs.text:
Problem: The "Sign out everywhere" option is missing, returns a 404, or signs the user out of PoracleWeb.NET but leaves the provider session active (so the next login skips re-authentication).

Solution: RP-initiated single logout requires all three of:

  1. OIDC_END_SESSION_URL configured. Without it, logout falls back to a plain local sign-out.
  2. enable_oidc_slo not set to false. This admin runtime toggle defaults to on once the end-session URL is wired; an explicit false disables single logout.
  3. The post_logout_redirect_uri registered at the IdP. PoracleWeb.NET sends {origin}/login?loggedout=1. If that URL isn't in the provider's allow-list, the provider rejects the logout redirect.

Configure the end-session URL, leave enable_oidc_slo unset (or true), and register the post-logout redirect URI at the IdP.

docs.title: Pokemon names and types stay English with the site set to another language
docs.text:
Symptom: The interface is translated, but the species picker still lists Bulbasaur, Blastoise and Butterfree, and the type chips read Bug, Dark, Dragon.

Cause: Those names come from Poracle, which translates them from its own bundle. If it cannot serve them, the site falls back to the English WatWowMap masterfile rather than showing nothing.

Checks, in order:

  1. Poracle is too old for the endpoint. GET /api/masterdata/monsters?locale=de on your Poracle should answer with a map of "{pokemonId}_{formId}" entries. A 404 means the fallback is doing its job and only an upgrade will change it.

    curl -s -H "X-Poracle-Secret: $SECRET"       "http://poracle-host:3030/api/masterdata/monsters?locale=de" | head -c 200

  2. Poracle has no translation for that language. It ships de, en, es, fr, it, ja, nb-no, pl, ru, sv and zh-cn. For nl, pt, pt-BR and da it returns English, and there is nothing to configure — the interface around the names is still translated.

  3. Poracle's game-data locale files are missing. If names come back as their own keys (poke_25 rather than Pikachu), Poracle's resource download has failed. The site ignores such values and keeps the English name, so the symptom is English names rather than visible keys. Check Poracle's startup log for its resource fetch.

  4. Move and item names are meant to be English. Poracle serves no translated equivalent, so those pickers are unaffected by the display language.

Note: this follows the display language, not the alert language. The alert language decides what your DMs say. See Internationalization.

docs.title: An alarm type has disappeared and its admin toggle will not switch on
docs.text:
Symptom: A type is gone from the sidebar and the dashboard, its page redirects away, and on Admin > Server settings its toggle is off, greyed out and refuses to move.

Cause: Poracle has that type disabled in its own config. Its processor drops the webhook and its bot refuses the command, so alarms of that type could never fire — this site honours that rather than offering a feature the server will not deliver. Rules users already had are not deleted; they lie dormant and come back if the type is switched on again.

Fix: change it in Poracle's config.toml, not here. The flags are disable_pokemon, disable_raid, disable_quest, disable_invasion, disable_lure, disable_nest, disable_gym, disable_max_battle, disable_fort_update and disable_showcase. Restart Poracle afterwards; this site re-reads them within five minutes, or immediately on restart.

Pokéstop Events is read from a different place

You do not need to write disable_showcase into your config.toml to switch it on. GET /api/config/values reflects over the config Poracle actually loaded and reports the effective value, and the option is declared with a default of false, so a supported server answers false whether or not the line is present. Set it only when you want the feature off.

Only an explicit true hides the page. A Poracle whose config this site cannot read, or one that answers without the option, leaves Pokéstop Events on, because every supported PoracleNG serves the incident route. If the page is missing, Poracle is reporting disable_showcase = true; check GET /api/config/values and the flag in config.toml.

Unlike the others it does not travel in disabledHooks; it is read separately from GET /api/config/values, so the jq .disabledHooks check below will not show it.

Diagnostic:

# What Poracle reports as disabled
curl -s -H "X-Poracle-Secret: $SECRET"   http://poracle-host:3030/api/config/poracleWeb | jq .disabledHooks

# Pokéstop Events travels separately. `false` means available, `null` means
# the server did not report the option.
curl -s -H "X-Poracle-Secret: $SECRET"   http://poracle-host:3030/api/config/values | jq .values.general.disable_showcase

# What this site resolved that into (any signed-in user)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT"   https://your-site/api/settings/upstream-disabled

An empty array on the first call, with the type still locked, means the local disable_* site setting is the one doing it — that one is yours to change on Admin > Server settings. The page names which side it came from, so you should not have to run either command to find out.

docs.title: A feature is missing and nothing says why
docs.text:
Symptom: A page or control the docs mention isn't there, with no error, toast or empty state.

Cause: Every supported PoracleNG (5.4.0 and later) has the quiet chip, Pokécoin quest rewards, the costume filter and the button that moves a saved place, so PoracleWeb.NET always offers them. What can hide something without a word is configuration:

Missing Hidden by An alarm type's page and sidebar item Its disable_* site setting on Admin > Server settings, or the type in Poracle's own disabledHooks (see the section above) Pokéstop Events Poracle's general.disable_showcase = true, or the disable_showcase site setting Quest summary delivery Poracle's tracking.quest_summary_enabled not true The Pokemon edit-in-place toggle Poracle's tracking.pokemon_edit not true Areas & places, Profiles, Geofences and similar pages Their disable_* site settings

The two tracking.* values are read from GET /api/config/values and cached for five minutes, and read as off when PoracleNG can't be asked.

Fix: check the setting on Admin > Server settings, then Poracle's config.toml. The Versions card on the same page shows which PoracleNG the deployment is talking to; below 5.4.0 these features fail with a message naming the version rather than hiding.

PoracleUnsupportedException is what a request gets when it reaches a route the server doesn't have: a human, profile, area, place or geocode call on PoracleNG below 5.4.0 answers 409 Conflict naming what is missing. When PoracleNG can't be reached at all, the mute and location endpoints and every alarm endpoint answer 503.

{
  "error": "This PoracleNG does not support listing areas. It requires PoracleNG 5.4.0.",
  "feature": "listing areas",
  "requires": "PoracleNG 5.4.0"
}

409 and not 403 on purpose: 403 is what a disable_* site setting answers, which is an operator's switch and a different conversation. A 409 carries the one detail worth reading, so the SPA shows it beside the control rather than bouncing you to the dashboard.

docs.title: A delegate cannot see "My Destinations"
docs.text:
Symptom: You granted someone a destination on Admin > Destinations, and they report no My Destinations item in the sidebar.

Checks, in order:

  1. Did the grant land? Reopen the destination's delegates dialog. A removable chip with their name means it exists. A grant naming an account that does not exist is refused rather than stored, so an absent chip usually means they had never signed in when you added them — they must register with the Poracle bot and sign in once before they can be granted.

  2. Give it a minute. Delegation is resolved live but cached for about a minute per person.

  3. Are they an administrator? Admins can manage any destination and are never listed as a delegate of a particular one, so they never see the item. It is for delegates only.

  4. Are you thinking of the bot? discord.webhook_admins in Poracle's config grants access through the Discord bot, not here. The reverse also holds: a row added here grants nothing to the bot. A Poracle-side grant does work here, but not the other way round.

  5. Expecting a PoracleNG channel admin? Someone PoracleNG lists in [[discord.delegated_admins]] or [[telegram.delegated_admins]] appears only when Admin → Settings → Administration → Let Poracle's channel admins manage here (delegation_poracle_channels) is on, and only for channels registered as destinations on this site. It is off by default.

Note: before v2.17 the item came from a claim stamped into the sign-in token, so a new delegate waited up to 24 hours or had to sign out and back in. If you are running an older build, that is the explanation — see Destinations & Delegates.

docs.title: Telegram and linked accounts
docs.text: Setup is in Telegram and behaviour in Linked accounts.

docs.title: The Telegram button doesn't appear
docs.text:
Symptom: No Telegram button on the login page, or none on the Telegram card of Linked accounts.

Cause: The button is drawn only when Telegram sign-in is enabled (set automatically when TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME are both set, unless TELEGRAM_ENABLED=false), a bot username is known (TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME, or the telegram_bot setting when that's empty), and Enable Telegram login isn't switched off. A button that appears but says "Bot domain invalid" means the bot's domain in @BotFather isn't this site's. A sign-in that completes in the widget and is then refused with "Telegram login is currently disabled." (telegram_disabled) means Enable Telegram login was switched off while the page was open; admins can still sign in that way.

Fix: Set the three values and restart after .env changes. In @BotFather, /setdomain with the exact hostname people use. The widget works on one domain only.

docs.title: Telegram says the account isn't registered
docs.text:
Symptom: Telegram sign-in answers "Your account is not registered" (user_not_registered), or a linked Telegram card reads "Waiting to register".

Cause: PoracleNG has no telegram:user for that id. It registers only members of a registration group ([telegram] channels, or each community's telegram.channels with area security).

Fix: Join the registration group and send /poracle there. Set telegram_registration_url so the Linked accounts page shows a Join the Telegram group button. Or set link_register_missing to when-qualified so linking creates the account for people who are already in a registration group (the bot must be in the group), or to always to skip the group rule.

docs.title: /start does nothing
docs.text:
Cause: register_on_start = true and the person isn't in any registration group. PoracleNG doesn't reply in that case (jfberry/PoracleNG#335). With register_on_start off it answers "You are not registered. Please register first."

Fix: Join the group and send /poracle there.

docs.title: Registered on Telegram but no alerts arrive
docs.text:
Cause: Telegram lets a bot DM only someone who has started a chat with it.

Fix: Press Start in the bot's chat. Allowing the bot to message you in the site's login widget also counts.

docs.title: Discord and Telegram show different settings
docs.text:
Cause: A bot command (!location, /profile, /area add) changed one account only, or a save reached one app and not the other.

Fix: Open Linked accounts and pick Use Discord's or Use Telegram's on each line. The site never picks for the person.

docs.title: A difference won't go away
docs.text:
Checks:

  1. Profile 0. An older account may have a profile 0, which the other app can't have. It's left out of the comparison on purpose, and the page says which account has one. That note isn't a difference to fix.
  2. "That changed in the meantime". Something changed one app while the list was open. Choose again from the refreshed list.
  3. A profile or place in use. A profile that still holds alarms on the other app, or a place alarms there still use, isn't deleted. Move or change those alarms, or keep that app's side instead.
  4. Active profile. It can only be matched once the other app has that profile. Fix the Profiles line first.

docs.title: An alarm can't be moved to the other app
docs.text: Message Fix Discord and Telegram are on different profiles Match the active profile on Linked accounts, then move again The place isn't saved on the other app Match saved places, or save that place on the other app It's limited to an area the other app can't use Change the alarm's areas Alerts can't be moved while inspecting another account Admins viewing as someone can't move their alarms. The person has to do it "…but the Discord copy is still there" The move worked and the delete didn't. Delete the leftover copy from the list

docs.title: People are never removed after leaving the group
docs.text:
Cause: [general] role_check_mode is ignore, PoracleNG's default, or [telegram] check_role is off. The check never creates anyone, only disables or deletes.

Fix: Set role_check_mode = "disable-user" (or "delete") and check_role = true. See Removing people who leave.

docs.title: Alarm services (PoracleNG API proxy)
docs.text:
Ten alarm tracking services (MonsterService, RaidService, EggService, QuestService, InvasionService, LureService, NestService, GymService, FortChangeService, MaxBattleService) use IPoracleTrackingProxy to proxy CRUD operations through the PoracleNG REST API. They do not use repositories or direct database access.

PokestopEventService is the eleventh, and the exception: Pokéstop Events have no v1 route, so it uses IPoracleIncidentProxy against /api/v2/humans/{id}/tracking/incident instead. It never touches IPoracleTrackingProxy.

See PoracleNG API Proxy for the full architecture, request flow, and how to add new alarm types.

docs.title: JSON serialization
docs.text:
Alarm data is serialized/deserialized with JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower to match PoracleNG's snake_case field names:

private static readonly JsonSerializerOptions SnakeCaseOptions = new()
{
    PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower,
    PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true,
};

docs.title: Update pattern
docs.text:
Creates and edits both go to PoracleNG's /api/v2 and nowhere else. There is no v1 fallback: a route that answers gin's plaintext 404 page not found raises PoracleUnsupportedException, and a row the translator can't express is refused with "PoracleNG can't store this alarm as it is: ... Nothing was changed." rather than sent through the older surface. Bulk distance and the cleaning toggle are the exception to the full replace: each is one PATCH /api/v2/humans/{id}/tracking/{type} naming the uids and the one setting, so nothing else a rule holds is re-sent.

An edit is PUT /api/v2/humans/{id}/tracking/{type}/{uid}, a full replace: a field left out of the body is reset to its default. The body is built by serializing the typed model, so every column PoracleWeb.NET has no property for would arrive absent. TrackingFieldPreserver.PreserveStoredFieldsAsync runs first on every update: it re-reads the stored row and copies across any property the submitted body lacks. Before it existed, editing an alarm on the web reset override_location_label, override_areas and pvp_ranking_evolution set from the bot (#730). A read failure returns the body untouched rather than failing the edit.

PoracleNG answers 409 for an edit that would duplicate another rule or change exactly one updatable field of it, and the proxy turns that into the takeover message. Services keep no copy of PoracleNG's diff any more. The PUT keeps the rule's uid on 5.4.0 (jfberry/PoracleNG #303) unless the server's reassignment fails, so the response is always read, and ITrackedUidRemapper moves quick-pick applied state to the new uid whenever it does change. See The v2 write path.

sequenceDiagram
    participant SPA
    participant API as PoracleWeb.NET
    participant NG as PoracleNG
    SPA->>API: PUT /api/{type}/{uid}
    API->>NG: GET .../tracking/{type}
    alt uid not on the active profile
        API-->>SPA: 404
    end
    alt the edit changes nothing
        API-->>SPA: 200, nothing sent to PoracleNG
    end
    API->>API: ApplyUpdate, nulls skipped
    alt a min above its max (range validator)
        API-->>SPA: 400 naming the field
    end
    API->>API: TrackingFieldPreserver carries stored fields across
    API->>API: translate to a V2 rule
    API->>NG: PUT .../tracking/{type}/{uid}?silent=true, trusted if override areas allowed
    alt 409
        API-->>SPA: 409 takeover message, nothing changed
    else 422
        API-->>SPA: 400 with PoracleNG's reason
    else 200 with uid
        opt uid changed
            API->>API: ITrackedUidRemapper moves quick-pick state
        end
        API-->>SPA: 200
    end

The ... is /api/v2/humans/{id}. TrackingFieldPreserver reads the same list again rather than trusting the first read. trusted=true is added only when the rule names override areas that IUserAreaPolicy allowed.

docs.title: Repository layer (non-alarm entities)
docs.text:
There is no repository for humans, profiles or alarms. Every human and profile read and write, the admin user list, the webhook list, the batch read that resolves geofence owners' names and account deletion go through IPoracleHumanProxy and PoracleNG's /api/v2 routes. The poracle_web tables have one repository each: OidcSessionRepository, QuickPickAppliedStateRepository, QuickPickDefinitionRepository, SiteSettingRepository, UserGeofenceRepository and WebhookDelegateRepository.

BaseRepository removed

The generic BaseRepository<TEntity, TModel> and all alarm repository classes have been removed. EnsureNotNullDefaults() went with them; the remaining repositories normalise nulls where they need to.

docs.title: Mapping extensions
docs.text:
Mapping is done with static extension methods in Core.Mappings/. There is no AutoMapper dependency.

AlarmMappingExtensions covers the alarm DTOs: To*() builds a model from a *Create DTO (create.ToMonster()), and ApplyUpdate() merges a *Update DTO onto an existing model (update.ApplyUpdate(existing)).

EntityMappingExtensions covers the poracle_web entities (user geofences, site settings, webhook delegates, quick-pick definitions and applied state) with ToModel(), ToEntity(), and ApplyTo().

All *Update models use nullable properties so partial updates don't zero out unset fields. ApplyUpdate skips nulls explicitly:

public static void ApplyUpdate(this MonsterUpdate src, Monster dest)
{
    if (src.Ping != null) dest.Ping = src.Ping;
    if (src.Distance != null) dest.Distance = src.Distance.Value;
    // ... one guarded assignment per field
}

docs.title: Monster filter defaults
docs.text:
PoracleNG fills a field only when it's absent from the write. A non-nullable int on a *Create model is never absent: it serialises as whatever it defaults to, and that value is stored. So every default on a *Create model is authoritative, and getting one wrong writes it into every rule. Believing PoracleNG would supply them is how 15,383 production rules ended up with pvp_ranking_best = 0 (#895).

A bound's "no filter" value is the column's default, which isn't always zero:

Property Default Notes max_iv 100 max_cp 9000 max_level 55 max_weight 9000000 max_atk, max_def, max_sta 15 pvp_ranking_best 1 Ranks are 1-based. [Range] still admits 0 so stored legacy rules stay editable pvp_ranking_worst 4096 costume 9000 Any costume. 0 means no costume size -1 Any size max_size 5 team (Raid, Egg, Gym) 4 Any team move, evolution (Raid) 9000 Any

When adding a field, ask what the column stores for "no filter", and check its pair: the bug in #895 was one half of a best/worst pair left without an initializer. Every write goes through TrackingV2Translator, which turns the v1-shaped row into a V2*Rule body. A rule read back with a legacy zero (pvp_ranking_best 0, size 0) shows the default, and the next write saves it.

docs.title: Raid level service
docs.text:
IRaidLevelService / RaidLevelService is a singleton that serves the canonical Pokémon GO raid-type vocabulary to the frontend, mirroring the WatWowMap masterfile without the locale-blind English strings leaking into the UI. The implementation returns a baked-in snapshot of 19 levels (1-Star through Coordinated 2) via GET /api/masterdata/raid-levels, with each entry exposing { value, category, name, namePlural }. A TODO in GetAllAsync documents the upgrade path to a live masterfile fetch with on-disk caching under DATA_DIR; the wire contract will not change. The frontend RaidLevelService caches the response in a signal and falls back to a baked-in KNOWN_LEVELS constant on fetch error so the level picker always works, even offline.

PoracleNG accepts any positive integer as a raid/egg level, so the picker's + Add affordance lets users alarm on levels that haven't been added to the canonical list yet. The [Range(0, int.MaxValue)] attribute on the alarm Create/Update DTOs ensures custom integers and the 9000 "any" sentinel pass server-side validation.

docs.title: Test alert service
docs.text: TestAlertService lets users trigger a sample notification for an alarm of one of the eight types TestAlertController.ValidTypes names: pokemon, raid, egg, quest, invasion, lure, nest, gym. Fort Changes, Max Battles and Pokéstop Events have no test alert, and the controller answers 400 for any other type. It uses Task.WhenAll to fetch the alarm (via IPoracleTrackingProxy) and the human record (via IPoracleHumanProxy) in parallel. It then constructs a realistic mock webhook payload based on the alarm's filter fields (e.g., pokemon_id, raid_level, quest_reward) using the user's location as the event coordinates. The payload is sent to PoracleNG's POST /api/test endpoint, which formats and delivers the notification. Once PoracleNG accepts it (2xx), the service sends one plain-text note (TestAlertService.TestNote, English only, because the backend has no message localisation) to the same target, same id and type including webhooks and Telegram, through IPoracleApiProxy.DeliverTextAsync, which posts one job to PoracleNG's POST /api/deliverMessages. The note says the alert is a sample and not a live one, so a member who pressed the button by accident doesn't go looking for a spawn (#1097). A refused or unreachable /api/test sends no note, and a failed note never fails the test: the service logs a warning with the alarm type, the uid and the target type, never the target id (it can be a webhook URL), and still returns success. Rate-limited at 5 requests per 60s per user (falling back to the IP) via the test-alert policy.

docs.title: Fort change and Max Battle services
docs.text: FortChangeService and MaxBattleService follow the same IPoracleTrackingProxy pattern as all other alarm services. They proxy CRUD operations through PoracleNG's tracking endpoints. Each has the standard three distance endpoints (PUT /{uid}, PUT /distance, PUT /distance/bulk).

docs.title: Grunt type checks
docs.text:
InvasionService runs RequireGruntType before every create and edit. It rewrites the legacy metal to steel (InvasionGruntTypes.Normalise), because PoracleNG's game data has no metal and v2 refuses it. It then refuses a blank value, control characters, or anything longer than the 255-character column. It deliberately doesn't check against a list: production holds grunt types this code doesn't model (blanche, candela, spark, npc 0 to npc 10, player team leader), and those must stay editable. Case is left as sent, and PoracleNG normalises a spaced name such as player team leader to player_team_leader on write.

A Pokéstop event grunt (Kecleon, Gold Stop, Showcase) picked on the invasion page is saved as a Pokéstop event rule instead, through IPoracleIncidentProxy.

docs.title: Bulk operations
docs.text:
Each alarm controller has three distance endpoints:

Endpoint Purpose PUT /{uid} Update a single alarm (full object) PUT /distance Update ALL alarms' distance for the current user/profile PUT /distance/bulk Update distance for specific UIDs: { uids: number[], distance: number }

The two distance endpoints send one PATCH /api/v2/humans/{id}/tracking/{type}?silent=true&trusted=true with {"uids": [...], "set": {"distance": n}}, so nothing else a rule holds is re-sent and each rule keeps its uid. DistanceRewrite.Plan first sets aside the rules a radius can't apply to: one limited to areas can't take a radius above zero, and one measured from a saved place can't take zero. PoracleNG answers per uid, and DistanceRewrite.Report turns that into { updated, skippedAreaScoped, skippedPlaceScoped, skippedConflict }. A rule PoracleNG refuses because it would clash with another is reported as a conflict, and the rest still go through. The cleaning toggle is the same PATCH with {"set": {"clean": n}}.

flowchart TD
    A["PUT /api/{type}/distance/bulk<br/>uids, distance"] --> P["DistanceRewrite.Plan"]
    P -->|"limited to areas, distance above 0"| SA["skippedAreaScoped"]
    P -->|"measured from a place, distance 0"| SP["skippedPlaceScoped"]
    P -->|"the rest"| W["PATCH /api/v2/humans/{id}/tracking/{type}<br/>silent, trusted"]
    W --> R{"answer per uid"}
    R -->|"updated or unchanged"| U["updated, uid kept"]
    R -->|"conflict, or invalid for another reason"| C["skippedConflict"]
    R -->|"not_found"| L["logged only"]

docs.title: IPoracleTrackingProxy (alarm tracking)
docs.text:
Proxies alarm reads, creates, edits and deletes to PoracleNG's /api/v2/humans/{id}/tracking/* routes. Authenticated via the X-Poracle-Secret header. No v1 tracking route is called. See PoracleNG API Proxy for full details.

  • Registered as AddHttpClient<IPoracleTrackingProxy, PoracleTrackingProxy>(); there is no decorator
  • Used by: all alarm services, DashboardService, CleaningService, ProfileOverviewService, TestAlertService, RuleRepairJob, UserAreaWriter

docs.title: IPoracleHumanProxy (human/profile management)
docs.text:
Proxies human and profile operations to PoracleNG's /api/v2/humans/... routes: user reads and creation, location, areas, profile switching and profile CRUD, plus the admin user list and delete and the admin-roles read.

  • Registered via AddHttpClient<IPoracleHumanProxy, PoracleHumanProxy>()
  • Used by: HumanService, ProfileService, ProfileOverviewService, UserGeofenceService, UserAreaPolicy, UserAreaWriter, UserRoleResolver, TestAlertService, RuleRepairJob, and the Admin, Area, Auth, Location, Profile and ProfileOverview controllers
  • URL-encodes user IDs with Uri.EscapeDataString() -- critical for webhook IDs that contain slashes

docs.title: IPoracleApiProxy (config, areas, templates)
docs.text:
Wraps HttpClient calls for non-tracking Poracle API operations.

  • Used for: config and config values, templates, masterdata (grunts, localized monsters), geofence maps and hashes, asking PoracleNG to reload geofences, test alerts (POST /api/test, then the one-line note after it through POST /api/deliverMessages) and geocoding (/api/geocode/forward and /reverse)
  • Registered via AddHttpClient<IPoracleApiProxy, PoracleApiProxy>()

docs.title: IPoracleMuteProxy (quiet periods)
docs.text: Proxies the mute store at /api/v2/humans/{id}/mutes. v2 only, with no v1 equivalent and no capability check: every supported PoracleNG has the routes. MuteController answers { mutes }, and all three actions answer 503 through PoracleUnreachableExceptionFilter when PoracleNG cannot be reached.

docs.title: IPoracleIncidentProxy (Pokéstop Events)
docs.text: Proxies Pokéstop-event alarm CRUD at /api/v2/humans/{id}/tracking/incident. Both proxies now speak v2, but IPoracleTrackingProxy hands its callers the v1 row shape every service is built on, and Pokéstop events never had one, so the incident proxy keeps its own model rather than adding a second shape to every tracking method. The tracking proxy folds event rules into the invasion list for the reads that show them there.

docs.title: IPoracleSummaryProxy (quest summary delivery)
docs.text:
Reads and writes the quest summary schedule for SummaryScheduleController. See Quest Summary Delivery.

That makes six Poracle proxies in total: tracking, incident, human, mute, summary and api.

docs.title: Config parsing
docs.text: PoracleConfig is parsed from Poracle's JSON configuration. The defaultTemplateName field can be a number or string — deserialization handles both via JsonElement.

docs.title: Server capability probe
docs.text:
IPoracleServerProfileService / PoracleServerProfileService asks the PoracleNG instance what it is. One read: GET {Poracle:ApiAddress}/health, which carries the release number and PoracleNG's own capability map. It is unauthenticated, so the probe carries no secret and still works when the API key is wrong, which is itself worth knowing: "reachable but every write 401s" and "not running" look identical otherwise. The map is read key-by-key rather than into a fixed type, because it is upstream's and it grows. It covers bot and template-editor features and says nothing about alarms.

There used to be a second read, schema_migrations and information_schema straight out of PoracleNG's database, for the costume columns and the lure and invasion unique keys. Every supported release answers those the same way, so it went when 5.2.1 became the minimum, and Poracle:TrackingApiVersion went with 5.4.0.

PoracleServerProfile.MinimumSupported is 5.4.0. IsBelowMinimum is true only when the server is known to be older: unreachable, unparseable, or the 0.0.0 a locally built binary reports are all unknown rather than too old, so the banner is not shown on a guess. IsSupported is the rule every version-decided feature shares: reachable and not known to be older, so a local build counts as current and an unreachable server does not. Supports(capability) defaults a missing key to false, per PoracleNG's map contract.

Against a server below the minimum PoracleWeb.NET keeps running. PoracleCompatibilityStartupService logs an error at startup naming what breaks, and the Versions card on the admin settings page shows the same thing. Refusing to start would take the whole site down over something an operator can fix.

The profile is cached in IMemoryCache for five minutes and the HttpClient's timeout is five seconds, so an unreachable server answers "unknown" quickly instead of stalling the admin page. GET /api/admin/server-profile serves it (admin only); ?refresh=true invalidates the cache and the GitHub update check first.

docs.title: Per-feature capability services
docs.text:
Two services answer a question from Poracle's own configuration: SummaryCapabilityService reads tracking.quest_summary_enabled and PokemonEditCapabilityService reads tracking.pokemon_edit, both from GET /api/config/values, caching for five minutes. They exist because both are deployment settings an operator can switch off on a server that supports the feature, not because of the server's version.

The services that used to answer "is this server new enough" (QuestPokecoinCapabilityService, PlaceUpdateCapabilityService, CostumeCapabilityService, MuteCapabilityService) are gone with the fallbacks they guarded: every supported release has the feature, so its control is always shown and the endpoints that only reported them (GET /api/settings/costume-capability, GET /api/quests/capability) no longer exist.

There is deliberately no central registry. A user-facing control cannot ask the admin-only GET /api/admin/server-profile, so an ordinary authenticated endpoint answers instead, like GET /api/summary-schedules/capability.

See Version compatibility for how to choose a signal and what each feature needs.

docs.title: Areas
docs.text:
Every area write goes to PoracleNG's /api/v2 area routes, and PoracleNG keeps humans.area and profiles.area in step. PoracleWeb.NET writes neither table.

User-drawn geofences are why there is more than a plain SetAreasAsync. PoracleWeb.NET serves them with userSelectable=false to keep them off the bot's area picker, and PoracleNG's setAreas drops any name whose fence is not user-selectable. IUserAreaWriter gets round that with the v2 trusted flag (PoracleNG 5.4.0) and does its own authorising first, because trusted skips PoracleNG's check. A name is allowed when it is in the union of:

  • the names PoracleNG lists as userSelectable for this user;
  • the user's own drawn geofences;
  • the names already on the profile being written.
Operation What it does SaveSelectionAsync (Areas page) One trusted POST /api/v2/humans/{id}/areas. A name outside the union answers 400 { error, areas } before anything is sent. Names PoracleNG has no fence for are dropped by PoracleNG and reported back, not treated as an error. FilterAllowedAsync (new profile) The same union, but a disallowed name is dropped with a warning instead of refused. Used by profile create only. Both duplicates copy the caller's own source profile's list trusted and unfiltered (the source may be a non-active profile); import writes no areas. AddToActiveProfileAsync / RemoveFromActiveProfileAsync The geofence toggle, and create. Read the active profile's list, change it, post it trusted. PreviewRemovalAsync / RemoveEverywhereAsync Delete. A dry run reports the alarms that would widen; the real call removes the name from every profile. RenameEverywhereAsync Rename and approval. PoracleNG's geofences are reloaded first, because the new name has to be loaded.

The geofence service orders these so a failure leaves something retryable. Create reloads PoracleNG's fences before it adds the name, and if the add fails the fence is kept and flagged activationFailed. Delete removes the name from the profiles first and deletes the row last, so a failed removal keeps the fence. A user rename that PoracleNG refuses puts the old name back.

trusted also lifts PoracleNG's [tracking] max_areas (jfberry/PoracleNG#346), so IUserAreaPolicy applies that limit itself, read from maxAreas on /api/config/poracleWeb. It follows PoracleNG's rule: a new list must fit, a list already over the limit can be saved again or made shorter but not longer, and PoracleNG's admins and destinations that aren't people (channels, threads, webhooks, groups) are exempt. It covers the Areas page, the geofence toggle and create, new profiles, and alarm override areas on create, edit and linked-account move. A refusal answers 400 with the limit in the message. Copying a linked account's list to fix a difference isn't limited. The same upstream change lifts [tracking] max_distance for trusted writes, and every v2 PATCH is trusted, so both PatchAsync methods (tracking and Pokéstop events) pass a distance through ClampDistanceAsync first. It clamps rather than refuses, as PoracleNG does, with the same exemptions. Creates and edits don't need it: a trusted one carries override areas, and those can't carry a radius (#1122).

Geofence polygons come from the Poracle API (via the unified feed), not the database.

docs.title: Per-alarm areas
docs.text:
An alarm can confine itself to named areas of its own, stored in the row's override_areas. That is the userSelectable problem one layer down: PoracleNG's tracking write checks every entry against its allowed areas and answers 400 "area not permitted" for a user-drawn fence, failing the whole request.

PoracleTrackingProxy handles it in three steps, with no write to PoracleNG's database:

  1. OverrideScope refuses an incoherent scope before anything is sent. A row cannot carry both a place and a set of areas; areas cannot coexist with a radius; a place needs one.
  2. IUserAreaPolicy authorises each name: selectable for the user, one of the user's own drawn geofences, on the active profile, or already on the rule being edited. A name that passes none of those is refused.
  3. The write is sent with ?trusted=true, so PoracleNG stores the list as given.

The Pokéstop event proxy (PoracleIncidentProxy) does the same for its own routes. A write that names no override area sends no trusted flag.

docs.title: Location
docs.text: LocationController uses IPoracleHumanProxy.SetLocationAsync() to set the user's location. PoracleNG handles the write and state reload atomically, so there's no transaction to manage here.

docs.title: Saved places
docs.text:
The same controller owns the places an alarm can be anchored to instead of the profile pin. PoracleNG stores them in user_locations, keyed by (human, label), and they are reached only through IPoracleHumanProxy.

Endpoint Behaviour GET /api/location/places Returns SavedPlaces { Default, Named }. Default is the profile pin every alarm falls back to, null when the user has never set one. POST /api/location/places Saves a place, then returns the updated set. PoracleNG reports a rejected label inside a 200 because its endpoint answers per row, so the refusal is unwrapped and returned as a 400 the SPA can show against the field. DELETE /api/location/places/{label} 204 on success. 409 with referencingRules when alarms still point at the label — PoracleNG refuses rather than orphaning it, and naming the alarms is the difference between "could not delete" and knowing what to repoint. Carried as PlaceInUseException.

A label is what an alarm's override_location_label refers to. The whole controller carries [RequireFeatureEnabled(DisableFeatureKeys.Location)], so disable_location takes the pin, the places API, the static and distance maps and weather with it.

docs.title: Service lifetimes
docs.text:
Service Lifetime Reason Most services Scoped Per-request MasterDataService Singleton Cached game data. Serves move and item names from the WatWowMap masterfile, and the English monster map as the fallback for GET /api/masterdata/monsters, which normally proxies Poracle's translated one RaidLevelService Singleton Stateless canonical-list provider; future live masterfile fetch will cache here UpstreamFeatureFlagService Scoped Resolves Poracle's own per-type disable flags into disable_* keys, cached 5 min; fails open

DashboardService uses the proxy

DashboardService calls IPoracleTrackingProxy.GetAllTrackingAsync() to fetch all alarm types in a single API call, then counts each type from the response.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
• humans.current_profile_no (not profile_no) tracks the active profile
  • All alarm tables reference profile_no to filter by active profile

docs.title: Active hours
docs.text:
The Profile model includes an ActiveHours (string?) property representing a JSON array of time-window rules stored in the active_hours column of the profiles table. ProfileService.DeserializeProfiles() extracts active_hours from the PoracleNG proxy's JsonElement response and maps it onto the model.

ProfileController includes active_hours in the proxy payload for Create, Update, and Duplicate endpoints. Validation lives in Core.Models/ActiveHoursValidator, shared with SummaryScheduleController so the two cannot drift:

  • Each entry must specify day (1--7), hours (0--23), mins (0--59)
  • Maximum 28 entries per profile (four per day across seven days)
  • Returns a 400 Bad Request with details on validation failure

It accepts hours and mins as either numbers or strings, because PoracleNG stores them inconsistently.

docs.title: Repeating entries
docs.text:
An entry can also fire repeatedly across a window, which adds three snake_case fields to the stored JSON:

{"day": 1, "hours": 9, "mins": 0, "end_hours": 17, "end_mins": 0, "step": 2}

That fires at 09:00 and every two hours up to and including 17:00. A single fire omits all three fields entirely.

step must be a whole number of hours no greater than 23, and when it is positive the end time must be strictly later than the start — a window spanning midnight is not supported. A step of zero or less is a single fire, and any end fields beside it are ignored rather than refused, matching what ActiveHourEntry.Fires() does upstream. The end fields carry omitempty in PoracleNG, so a window ending on the hour arrives with end_mins missing: a missing end field reads as 0 and is never an error.

docs.title: Scanner service
docs.text: The scanner DB (ScannerDb connection string) is optional. When not configured, IScannerService is not registered and scanner endpoints return appropriate fallback responses.

docs.title: Gym search endpoints
docs.text:
ScannerController exposes two gym endpoints backed by ScannerService:

Endpoint Purpose GET /api/scanner/gyms?search=term&limit=20 Search gyms by name prefix (term%, index-sargable). User input is escaped for LIKE wildcards (%, _, \). Search length 2--100 chars; limit clamped to [1, 50]. GET /api/scanner/gyms/{id} Return a single gym by its ID (max 128 chars).

Both endpoints are rate-limited under the scanner-search policy (60 requests/min per user, falling back to the IP).

Both endpoints resolve the gym's area name by running point-in-polygon checks against cached Koji admin geofences (via IKojiService.GetAdminGeofencesAsync()). The first matching fence name is set on the result's Area property.

Graceful fallback: if the scanner DB is unreachable or the query fails, the search endpoint returns an empty array and the single-gym endpoint returns 404. If IKojiService is unavailable, area resolution is skipped (gym is returned without an area name).

docs.title: GymSearchResult model
docs.text:
GymSearchResult in Core.Models carries the gym data returned by both endpoints:

Property Type Notes Id string Scanner gym ID Name string? Gym name from scanner DB Url string? Photo thumbnail URL from scanner DB Lat double Latitude Lon double Longitude TeamId int? Controlling team (0 = neutral) Area string? Resolved at request time via point-in-polygon, not stored

docs.title: ScannerGymEntity.Url
docs.text: The ScannerGymEntity in the scanner context maps the url column from the gym table, providing gym photo thumbnail URLs to GymSearchResult.

docs.title: PointInPolygon
docs.text: IScannerService declares a static PointInPolygon(double lat, double lon, double[][] polygon) method using the ray-casting algorithm. The method tests if a point lies inside a polygon (where each entry is [lat, lon]) and returns false for degenerate polygons with fewer than 3 vertices. Used by ScannerController to determine which Koji geofence area a gym belongs to.

docs.title: GeoMath
docs.text:
Core.Services/GeoMath.cs holds the polygon maths used outside the scanner path: AreaSqKm (spherical excess / Girard's theorem, R = 6371 km), Centroid (vertex mean), Contains (ray casting), and DescribeArea (plain-language size band). It backs the geofence review card's size, location and overlap fields.

Keep in sync with the frontend

GeoMath is a hand-port of the frontend's shared/utils/geo.utils.ts. If the two drift, the area a user sees while drawing a geofence stops matching the one an admin sees in the review thread. The tests derive their expected values from the sphere's radius (2πR/360) rather than from the implementation, so a port mistake fails rather than being enshrined.

docs.title: Discord notifications
docs.text:
IDiscordNotificationService opens and maintains the geofence review thread. Two mechanics are easy to get wrong:

  • The map must be uploaded, not linked. Poracle's GET /api/geofence/{area}/map returns a pregenerated tileserver-cache URL that the cache evicts, so an embed linking it goes blank within hours. The bytes are downloaded (via a separate unauthenticated named HttpClient, so the bot token never reaches the tileserver) and posted as a message attachment.
  • Editing the card re-uploads the map. Discord folds an attachment:// attachment into the embed, so the message reports an empty attachments array — there is no ID to carry forward, and the embed's resolved cdn.discordapp.com URL is a signed link that expires. A forum post's starter message shares the thread's ID, so the opening embed is edited with PATCH /channels/{threadId}/messages/{threadId}.

One BuildEmbed produces the pending, approved and rejected cards so they cannot drift apart, and each piece degrades on its own: a failed download links the URL, a failed card rewrite still posts the verdict reply, and a Koji outage just omits the overlap line.

docs.title: IGolbatApiProxy (Pokemon availability)
docs.text:
Proxies requests to Golbat's GET /api/pokemon/available endpoint, which returns currently spawning species with per-species/form counts. Authentication uses the X-Golbat-Secret header (per-request, not on DefaultRequestHeaders).

  • Registered conditionally via AddHttpClient<IGolbatApiProxy, GolbatApiProxy>() — only when Golbat:ApiAddress is configured
  • Response parsing handles both flat arrays [1,2,3] and object arrays [{"id":1,"form":0,"count":100}], deduplicating by Pokemon ID
  • On error: returns empty list (never throws), logs warning

docs.title: IPokemonAvailabilityService (caching layer)
docs.text:
Caches Golbat availability data in IMemoryCache with a 5-minute absolute expiration. Maintains a _lastKnownGood fallback — if Golbat goes down after a successful fetch, the stale data is served rather than returning empty.

  • Registered as singleton (only when Golbat is configured)
  • Cache key: golbat_available_pokemon
  • PokemonAvailabilityController uses nullable DI injection (IPokemonAvailabilityService? = null) — when Golbat is not configured, the endpoint returns { available: [], enabled: false }

docs.title: Weather data
docs.text: Weather data is served via IScannerService from the scanner DB (ScannerWeatherEntity). ScannerService fetches weather cells using S2 cell geometry (S2CellHelper) and returns WeatherData models with cell polygons and gameplay weather conditions. The LocationController exposes weather data alongside the user's location. Weather is optional -- when the scanner DB is not configured, weather endpoints return empty results.

docs.title: Rate limiting
docs.text:
Sensitive endpoints use partitioned rate limiting, never one global bucket:

Policy Limit Window Applied to auth 30 requests 60 seconds Login / callback / token exchange auth-read 120 requests 60 seconds Current user, profile switch test-alert 5 requests 60 seconds Test-alert sends mutes 60 requests 60 seconds Quiet-period reads and writes geojson-import 5 requests 60 seconds A user's own GeoJSON import scanner-search 60 requests 60 seconds Scanner gym search / lookup geofence-feed-refresh 20 requests 60 seconds The anonymous feed-refresh POST

Configured in Program.cs using RateLimitPartition.GetFixedWindowLimiter. auth and geofence-feed-refresh key on RemoteIpAddress because neither caller is signed in; the other five key on the authenticated user, falling back to the IP. The mutes limit is set for reads — the quiet chip is read on every alarm page, and the store is written a few times a day at most. geofence-feed-refresh bounds guessing at the shared secret rather than load: the work per call is one cache eviction.

Never use global rate limiting for auth

Global (non-partitioned) AddFixedWindowLimiter for auth causes cascading login failures — multiple users share one bucket.

docs.title: Database
docs.text: PoracleWeb.NET owns one MySQL database, poracle_web, and optionally reads a second, scanner database. It does not connect to Poracle's database. Everything Poracle stores (users, profiles, alarms, saved places) is reached through PoracleNG's REST API.

docs.title: Poracle's data (not connected)
docs.text:
PoracleNG keeps users, profiles and alarms in its own database. PoracleWeb.NET has no connection string for it and no DbContext mapping it, so a direct write to an alarm table isn't possible from this application. The older DB_* variables are ignored (see Configuration).

The rest of this section describes what PoracleNG stores, because the shapes explain what the API returns. Treat it as a reference to PoracleNG's schema, not as something PoracleWeb.NET reads.

Area writes for user geofences (Areas save, create, toggle, delete, rename, approval) go through PoracleNG's /api/v2 area routes. Saved places live in PoracleNG too, keyed by (human, label), and are written only through IPoracleHumanProxy.

Eleven tracking types, ten alarm tables

Ten is the table count and it is right. The eleventh type, Pokéstop Events (incident), stores its rows in the existing invasion table. No table arrived with it, and nothing marks the row apart except grunt_type, which holds an event name (gold-stop, kecleon, showcase) rather than a grunt name — the same discriminator PoracleNG's own isEventGruntType uses to split its two v2 endpoints.

v1's invasion read returned both kinds, and the application was built on that list. The tracking proxy now reads incident through v2 and folds those rules into the invasion list itself, and InvasionService splits them out again, but only when the Pokéstop Events page exists. Where it doesn't (Poracle reports disable_showcase = true, or an admin has switched the page off), the event rules stay in the invasion list, because filtering them out of the only page that can show them would leave alarms that fire and can't be deleted.

docs.title: Notable columns in profiles
Notable columns on the alarm tables
docs.text:
Per-alarm delivery scope rests on two columns, present on all ten tables (monsters, raid, egg, quest, invasion, lures, nests, gym, forts, maxbattle). Both arrived in PoracleNG 5.1.0.

Column Type Description override_location_label string, nullable Saved-place label the alarm measures its radius from, instead of the profile pin. A label that no longer exists is not an error — PoracleNG falls through to the pin, so deleting a place widens its alarms rather than breaking them. override_areas JSON array, nullable Areas the alarm is confined to, lowercase with spaces. Replaces the profile's area list outright rather than intersecting with it. NULL when unset, never [] — parseOverrideAreas reads an empty value back as no override, while [] is a list that matches nothing.

The two are mutually exclusive, areas cannot coexist with a radius, and a place requires one. PoracleNG refuses all three combinations, and so does PoracleWeb.NET before the write (see Backend).

Two more columns on monsters alone, also 5.1.0:

Column Type Description pvp_ranking_evolution int, default 0 Which form the PVP ranks are read from: 0 base, 1 any mega, 2 Mega X, 3 Mega Y. Only consulted when a league is set. min_time int, default 0 Seconds a spawn must still have left when it is found, or the alert is skipped. 0 means any.

docs.title: Costume
docs.text:
costume arrived after 5.1.0 and on two tables at different times: monsters.costume at PoracleNG database migration 6, raid.costume at migration 7. Both are in every supported release (5.2.1 and later).

Value Meaning 9000 Any costume 0 No costume n That costume

The filter is always offered: every supported PoracleNG stores it. It used to be gated on the applied migration number, read straight from schema_migrations, and later on a capability endpoint; neither exists any more. See Version compatibility.

docs.title: user_locations
docs.text: PoracleNG stores saved places here, keyed by (human, label). PoracleWeb.NET reads and writes them only through IPoracleHumanProxy. See Backend.

docs.title: PoracleWebContext
docs.text:
A separate EF Core context for application-owned data.

MySQL provider

This project uses MySql.EntityFrameworkCore (Oracle's official provider), not Pomelo (Pomelo.EntityFrameworkCore.MySql), which is incompatible with EF Core 10. Connection setup uses options.UseMySQL(connectionString) (capital SQL).

  • Connection string: ConnectionStrings:PoracleWebDb
  • Database: poracle_web
  • Schema managed by EF Core migrations (Database.MigrateAsync() on startup)
  • PoracleWeb.NET's only database; Poracle's is never touched
  • Contains:
Table Purpose user_geofences User-drawn custom geofence polygons site_settings Typed admin-configurable settings with categories webhook_delegates Relational webhook-to-user delegation mappings quick_pick_definitions Quick pick alarm presets (global and user-scoped) quick_pick_applied_states Tracks which quick picks users have applied per profile oidc_sessions Refresh-token families for OIDC silent refresh, with rotation and replay detection account_links Pairs one person's Discord and Telegram humans

MariaDB compatibility

MySql.EntityFrameworkCore's MigrateAsync() uses GET_LOCK(-1) which returns NULL on MariaDB. The MariaDbHistoryRepository class overrides the lock to use GET_LOCK(3600) instead. This is registered via ReplaceService<IHistoryRepository, MariaDbHistoryRepository>() on PoracleWebContext.

docs.title: ScannerContext (optional)
docs.text:
Connects to a Golbat scanner database. ScannerService reads it directly, with no repository in between.

  • Connection string: ConnectionStrings:ScannerDb
  • If not configured, IScannerService is not registered and scanner endpoints return appropriate responses
  • Maps four scanner tables: gym (the gym picker, see Scanner entities below), pokestop (active quests), station (the Pokemon seen in max battles, for the max battle picker) and weather (the dashboard weather)

docs.title: EF Core migrations
docs.text: The poracle_web database uses EF Core migrations for schema management. Tables and indexes are created automatically on startup.

docs.title: Adding a new migration
docs.text:
dotnet ef migrations add <MigrationName> \
  --context PoracleWebContext \
  --project Data/Pgan.PoracleWebNet.Data \
  --startup-project Applications/Pgan.PoracleWebNet.Api \
  --output-dir Migrations/PoracleWeb

Migrations are stored in Data/Pgan.PoracleWebNet.Data/Migrations/PoracleWeb/.

A design-time factory (PoracleWebContextDesignTimeFactory) provides the context for tooling without requiring a running app.

docs.title: Automatic application
docs.text: On startup, Program.cs calls webDb.Database.MigrateAsync() which applies any pending migrations. New tables and indexes are created automatically — no manual SQL required.

docs.title: ScannerGymEntity
docs.text:
Maps to the gym table in the Golbat scanner database.

Property Column Type Description Id id varchar (PK) Gym fort ID Name name varchar, nullable Gym display name Url url varchar, nullable Gym photo thumbnail URL Lat lat double Latitude Lon lon double Longitude TeamId team_id int, nullable Controlling team (0 = neutral, 1 = Mystic, 2 = Valor, 3 = Instinct)

docs.title: GymSearchResult
docs.text:
DTO model in Core.Models used by scanner gym search endpoints. Projected from ScannerGymEntity with an additional computed Area field.

Property Type Description Id string Gym fort ID Name string? Gym display name Url string? Gym photo thumbnail URL Lat double Latitude Lon double Longitude TeamId int? Controlling team ID Area string? Geofence area the gym belongs to (resolved at query time)

docs.title: gym_id semantics
docs.text:
The gym_id column on alarm entities (raid, egg, gym) uses NULL vs non-NULL to distinguish general alarms from gym-specific alarms:

  • gym_id = NULL — general alarm, matches all gyms
  • gym_id = '<id>' — gym-specific alarm, matches only the gym with that ID

The column is nullable with a NULL default. PoracleNG's matcher treats any non-NULL value as "only this gym", so a stored empty string ('') matches nothing. Writes through the API can't produce one: PoracleNG stores an empty gym_id as NULL, and the v2 read reports a general alarm's gym_id as null. Rows that hold '' were written straight to the database by older releases; see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Site settings table
docs.text:
The site_settings table holds the admin-configurable settings. They're typed and categorized:

Column Type Description id int (PK) Auto-increment ID category varchar(50) Setting group — branding, features, alarms, icons, admin, api, discord, oidc, telegram, maps, commands, analytics, debug, plus system for a legacy sentinel older versions wrote key varchar(100) Unique setting key (e.g., custom_title, disable_mons) value text Setting value value_type varchar(20) Type hint: string, boolean, url, csv

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text:
At startup SettingsMigrationService.SeedDefaultsAsync inserts any missing default setting and repoints the retired icon packs. It only adds rows that don't exist, so running it again changes nothing.

The pweb_settings table that early versions kept in Poracle's database is no longer read, and the app never alters or drops it. An admin can drop it.

docs.title: Webhook delegates table
docs.text:
Relational table for webhook delegation:

Column Type Description id int (PK) Auto-increment ID webhook_id varchar(500) Webhook URL/identifier user_id varchar(100) Delegated user ID created_at datetime When the delegation was created

Unique composite index on (webhook_id, user_id). Additional index on user_id for login-flow lookups.

docs.title: Account links table
docs.text:
Pairs a discord:user human with a telegram:user human. See Linked Accounts.

Column Type Description id int (PK) Auto-increment ID discord_id varchar(64) The Discord human's id. Unique telegram_id varchar(64) The Telegram human's id. Unique default_destination varchar(16) discord or telegram: where a new alarm goes when no app is named discord_verified_at datetime, nullable When the Discord identity was last proven telegram_verified_at datetime, nullable When the Telegram identity was last proven created_at datetime When the link was made

The unique index on each id column is what limits an account to one link. Rows join to PoracleNG by id only, and nothing about the link is written to PoracleNG. A side that isn't registered yet, a paused side and the differences between the two are all computed from PoracleNG on each request, never stored. Deleting a user removes their link, and unlinking deletes only the row.

docs.title: quick_pick_definitions
docs.text:
Stores alarm presets (both admin-global and user-scoped):

Column Type Description id varchar(50) (PK) Unique pick ID name varchar(200) Display name alarm_type varchar(20) monster, raid, egg, quest, invasion, lure, nest, gym, maxbattle scope varchar(10) global (admin) or user owner_user_id varchar(100) NULL for global, user ID for user-scoped filters_json JSON Alarm filter parameters sort_order int Display ordering enabled bool Whether the pick is active

Composite index on (scope, owner_user_id) for efficient filtering.

docs.title: quick_pick_applied_states
docs.text:
Tracks which picks users have applied:

Column Type Description id int (PK) Auto-increment ID user_id varchar(100) User who applied the pick profile_no int Profile the pick was applied to quick_pick_id varchar(50) The applied pick alarm_type varchar(20) Alarm type stored at apply time (for safe removal even if definition is deleted) tracked_uids_json JSON UIDs of created alarm rows exclude_pokemon_ids_json JSON Pokemon IDs excluded at apply time

Unique composite index on (user_id, profile_no, quick_pick_id).

docs.title: User geofences table
docs.text:
The user_geofences table stores user-drawn polygon geofences:

Column Type Description id int (PK) Auto-increment ID human_id string Owner's Discord/Telegram ID display_name string User-provided name koji_name string Lowercase Poracle-compatible name polygon_json text Array of lat/lng coordinates status string active, pending_review, approved, rejected group_name string Region/group name parent_id int Koji id of the region the fence was drawn in submitted_at datetime, nullable When it was submitted for review reviewed_by string, nullable The admin who approved or rejected it reviewed_at datetime, nullable When it was reviewed review_notes string, nullable Admin notes on approval/rejection promoted_name string, nullable The public area name it was promoted to in Koji, once approved discord_thread_id string, nullable Discord forum thread ID created_at datetime Creation timestamp updated_at datetime Last update timestamp

docs.title: Angular conventions
docs.text:
• All components are standalone (no NgModules)
  • Uses inject() function instead of constructor injection
  • Uses Angular signals for reactive state where applicable
  • Lazy-loaded routes in app.routes.ts
  • Services in core/services/ use HttpClient to call the .NET API

docs.title: Project structure
docs.text:
src/app/
├── core/
│   ├── guards/          Auth guard, admin guard
│   ├── services/        HTTP services for each API resource
