│   ├── interceptors/    JWT token interceptor
│   └── models/          TypeScript interfaces
├── modules/
│   ├── auth/            Login page
│   ├── dashboard/       Dashboard with onboarding
│   ├── pokemon/         Pokemon alarm management
│   ├── raids/           Raid alarm management
│   ├── quests/          Quest alarm management
│   ├── invasions/       Invasion alarm management
│   ├── lures/           Lure alarm management
│   ├── nests/           Nest alarm management
│   ├── gyms/            Gym alarm management
│   ├── fort-changes/    Fort change alarm management
│   ├── max-battles/     Max Battle (Dynamax) alarm management
│   ├── pokestop-events/ Pokéstop Event alarm management
│   ├── areas/           Areas, the home pin, and saved places on one page
│   ├── geofences/       Custom geofence drawing
│   ├── profiles-overview/  Profile cards, the routed /profiles page
│   ├── profiles/        Profile add / edit / duplicate dialogs
│   ├── cleaning/        Alarm cleanup tools
│   ├── quick-picks/     Quick pick alarm templates
│   ├── help/            In-app help page
│   └── admin/           Admin panel (users, destinations, settings, geofence submissions)
└── shared/
    ├── components/      Reusable UI components
    └── utils/           Utility functions (geo.utils, alarm-scope, etc.)

/places is a redirect to /areas — places were folded into the Areas & places page, beside the pin they belong with. /admin redirects to /admin/users.

docs.title: ScannerService
docs.text:
ScannerService (core/services/scanner.service.ts) provides access to the optional scanner database for gym lookups. Both methods use catchError for graceful degradation when the scanner DB is unavailable (returns of(null) or of([])).

  • searchGyms(search, limit) — Searches gyms by name. Returns an empty array if the search term is less than 2 characters.
  • getGymById(id) — Fetches a single gym by ID. Returns null on error.

The GymSearchResult interface defines the shape: id, name, url, lat, lon, teamId, and area.

docs.title: TestAlertService
docs.text: TestAlertService (core/services/test-alert.service.ts) manages test alert requests from alarm list cards. It tracks per-UID cooldowns (15-second TTL via a Map) and deduplicates in-flight requests to prevent duplicate API calls. After sending, it displays success/error/cooldown feedback via Material snackbar. The seven lists that can send one (the raid list covers both raid and egg cards) put it behind AlarmMoreMenuComponent, on eight of the eleven alarm types: Pokemon, Raids, Eggs, Quests, Invasions, Lures, Nests and Gyms. Fort Changes, Max Battles and Pokéstop Events have no test alert: TestAlertController.ValidTypes does not carry them, and a request naming one answers 400.

docs.title: MuteService
docs.text:
MuteService (core/services/mute.service.ts) holds the user's quiet periods as a live signal, read from and written to /api/mutes. The list response carries capable alongside the rules, so one call answers both whether this PoracleNG has the mute store (every supported release does; an unreachable or too-old server does not) and what is currently muted. When it does not, the quiet surface is not rendered at all.

Two things about the upstream store shape the service. Mutes are keyed by (scope, value) with no id, so that pair is the key here too. And the store lives in the processor's memory, so a restart wipes it with no notification: nothing here trusts a fetched list for longer than a page view, and the countdown ticks rather than resolving to a clock time. PoracleNG holds seven scopes; the SPA writes four — gym, pokemon, area, station.

docs.title: PokestopEventService
docs.text: PokestopEventService (core/services/pokestop-event.service.ts) backs the Pokéstop Events module. The type is v2-only, and the page exists only where Poracle's config carries general.disable_showcase = false; elsewhere it is not reachable.

docs.title: ProfileService — active hours
docs.text:
ProfileService (core/services/profile.service.ts) parses the activeHours field from the API response in getAll(), mapping the snake_case active_hours JSON string to a typed ActiveHoursEntry[] on each profile model.

  • updateActiveHours(profileNo, entries) — sends the active hours array to the API for the given profile

The active-hours.models.ts file (core/models/) defines the ActiveHoursEntry interface and utility functions for working with time-window rules (serialization, display formatting, validation).

docs.title: PlacesService
docs.text:
PlacesService (core/services/places.service.ts) holds the places an alarm can be aimed at: the named ones, plus the profile pin under pin (null when it is the 0,0 Poracle stores for "not set"). It is a signal rather than a per-caller fetch because the Where sheet, the Places section and every card carrying a where chip read the same list, and a place added in one has to appear in the others without a reload.

  • load() / add(place) / move(label, lat, lon) — each sets the signal from the response
  • remove(label) — answers 409 with referencingRules when alarms still point at the place; the caller should name them rather than reporting a bare failure

There is no canEdit flag: the move control is always rendered, because every supported PoracleNG has the route, and a failed move shows an error. See Version compatibility.

docs.title: AlertLanguageService
docs.text: AlertLanguageService (core/services/alert-language.service.ts) owns the language Poracle writes alerts in — DM text and Pokemon names in your notifications — which is a different setting from the display language. It writes optimistically to localStorage('poracle-language') and rolls back if the API call fails, and reconciles against the authoritative human.Language, since the bot can change it out of band. Its selected value is a computed: a language the user has actually been given, falling back to Poracle's configured locale, then en.

docs.title: MasterDataService
docs.text:
MasterDataService (core/services/masterdata.service.ts) holds the game data the pickers render: Pokemon names, types, form names, evolution chains, plus move and item names.

Names, types and forms are fetched from GET /api/masterdata/monsters?locale={display language} — Poracle owns those translations — while moves and items come from /api/masterdata/{moves,items} in English. All four load in one forkJoin; only the monster call is wrapped in catchError, so a Poracle that cannot serve it leaves the English names in place instead of cancelling the rest.

An effect on I18nService.currentLang re-fetches when the display language changes and re-emits on ready$, so a species picker that is already open updates in place rather than needing a reload.

Type names are the subtlety. Poracle returns them translated, but the uicons file names and the type filter chips both key on the English name, so the English name is kept as the value — resolved from the stable type id via shared/utils/pokemon-types.ts — and the translated string is stored alongside as a display label, read through getTypeLabel(). Only the chip's text is localized; everything that identifies a type is not.

docs.title: AlertDefaultsService
docs.text: AlertDefaultsService (core/services/alert-defaults.service.ts) remembers what scope a new alarm should open with: mode, default radius in km (clamped 0.1–100), and a default saved place. Stored in localStorage under poracle-default-alert-mode, poracle-default-alert-distance-km and poracle-default-alert-place. Client-side only — existing alarms are untouched. Edited from AlertDefaultsDialogComponent in the user menu.

docs.title: PokemonAvailabilityService
docs.text:
PokemonAvailabilityService (core/services/pokemon-availability.service.ts) provides Pokemon spawn availability data from the Golbat scanner API. It is a providedIn: 'root' singleton.

  • enabled signal — true when Golbat is configured on the backend
  • availableIds signal — Set<number> of currently spawning Pokemon IDs for O(1) lookups
  • isAvailable(id) — returns whether a Pokemon is currently spawning
  • load() — idempotent initial fetch + 5-minute auto-refresh via setInterval
  • Graceful degradation: preserves enabled state and stale data on refresh errors

The PokemonSelectorComponent injects this service and calls load() in ngOnInit(). When enabled() is true, it renders:

  • A "Live > Spawning" filter toggle chip (with animated pulse dot)
  • Green availability dots on autocomplete options and tile grid items
  • Available-first sorting when any filter is active

docs.title: Alarm lists
docs.text: All ten alarm types use the shared rule card and list toolbar described under Rule card and list toolbar: neutral filter pills, a status slot, the scope chip and a Details toggle for PoracleNG's own summary.

docs.title: Bulk operations
docs.text: Select mode toggle (checklist icon) on each alarm list. Its count is read to screen readers only once it has stopped changing. The bulk bar is one shared component, shared/components/bulk-action-bar/: the count of selected cards on screen (actionIds), Select all / Deselect all as text buttons, a tonal Change radius, and a filled warn "Delete N". Below 600px it is fixed to the bottom of the screen and styles.scss pads main while it shows. bulk-action-bar.component.spec.ts pins all ten lists to it.

docs.title: Loading states
docs.text: Animated skeleton card placeholders on Pokemon, Raids, and Quests pages.

docs.title: Page header and design rules
docs.text: Every page uses the one .page-header in styles.scss: the title, one line on what the page is for, and the page's one primary action, a filled, labelled mat-flat-button.page-primary-action placed last ("New alarm" on the ten alarm lists, "New profile" on Profiles). Pages don't restyle the header and nothing uses a FAB. Body text is Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, titles Plus Jakarta Sans, with tabular figures throughout. Labels are sentence case with no ALL-CAPS eyebrows, colour carries data (team, tier, type, state) and nothing decorative, and nothing moves unless the user did something: there are no staggered entrances or hover lifts. design-foundations.spec.ts checks all of this.

docs.title: Theming
docs.text:
The toolbar gradient, the sidenav's active link and the UI accent colours follow an accent theme picked from the user menu. The colours are applied as CSS custom properties on document.body.style so they reach across Angular's view encapsulation.

Dark and light mode bridge Material tokens to component styles through CSS variables, and the choice is stored in localStorage('poracle-theme').

docs.title: Onboarding wizard
docs.text: Shows on the dashboard for new users until explicitly dismissed. Detects existing location/areas/alarms and marks steps as complete. Route-based actions (Choose Areas, Add Alarm) hide the overlay temporarily without setting the localStorage completion flag.

docs.title: Active hours components
docs.text:
ActiveHoursChipComponent (shared/components/active-hours-chip/) renders a compact read-only summary of a profile's active hours schedule as a Material chip. Displayed inline on ProfileOverviewComponent cards.

ActiveHoursEditorDialogComponent (shared/components/active-hours-editor-dialog/) provides a full editing UI for active hours rules. Opened from the profile overview when the user clicks the active hours chip or the "Set active hours" action. Validates entries client-side (day 1--7, hours 0--23, mins 0--59, max 28 entries) before submitting. A rule can repeat across a window, which sends step, end_hours and end_mins alongside the start; see Active hours.

LocationWarningComponent (shared/components/location-warning/) displays a contextual warning when the user's location is not set, since active hours depend on the user's timezone derived from their location.

ProfileOverviewComponent integrates active hours display and editing — each profile card shows the ActiveHoursChipComponent and opens the editor dialog for modifications.

ProfileListComponent removed

The unused ProfileListComponent has been removed. Profile management is handled entirely by ProfileOverviewComponent.

docs.title: Where an alarm reaches you
docs.text:
ScopePickerComponent (shared/components/scope-picker/) is the one control for an alarm's delivery scope, wherever the question is asked. Three mutually exclusive options — inherit the profile's areas, a radius from a point or saved place, or only specific areas — modelled as a radio group because PoracleNG refuses every combination of them, so a state that would need validating cannot be expressed. It is rendered inline by every alarm add and edit dialog and by the quick-pick apply dialog. It previously existed as two copies, a two-option radio in the dialogs and a three-option sheet on the card, which drifted apart within a day and left no way to set a per-alarm area override before the alarm existed.

WhereChipComponent (shared/components/where-chip/) states the answer on the alarm card as a sentence fragment — "Anywhere I get alerts", "Anywhere in my areas", "Within 2 km of Home", "Only in Terrigal, Erina" — and is the way into the sheet. All ten list templates put it in the card's footer. An editable input turns it into a plain statement where there is nothing to open.

WhereSheetComponent (shared/components/where-sheet/) is a dialog shell around the scope picker and nothing else, for changing scope from a card where there is no form to put the control in.

docs.title: Rule card and list toolbar
docs.text:
AlarmCardComponent (shared/components/alarm-card/) is the one card all ten alarm lists draw. The list projects the parts by attribute (ruleMedia, ruleTitle, ruleSubtitle, ruleStatus, ruleFilters, ruleScope, ruleActions) and the card lays them out the same way everywhere: subject and status on top, one line of filters, scope chip and actions on one row. The shared pieces of vocabulary (.rule-pill, .rule-tag, .rule-subtitle, .rule-sprite, .rule-icon) are styled by the card. Its edge input takes a team, tier or primary-type colour from shared/utils/rule-colours.ts, the only place those colours are defined; each is a light/dark pair held at 3:1 against the card in both themes (rule-colours.spec.ts). alarm-card-parity.spec.ts pins every list to the card and says which ones carry an edge.

The card also owns the rule summary: the description PoracleNG returns beside each rule, the same sentence its bot answers a !pokemon command with, behind a Details toggle. It offers no toggle when there is no description, or when the alert language and the display language disagree, since Poracle localises the sentence with the alert language while the card follows the display language. Fort changes (a raw JSON array upstream) and Pokéstop events (no description) do not pass one.

AlarmMoreMenuComponent (shared/components/alarm-more-menu/) is the "More actions" icon button that ends the action row, after Edit and Delete, in the seven lists that can send a sample (<app-alarm-more-menu alarmType="pokemon" [uid]="monster.uid" />; the raid list passes raid or egg by card). Its menu holds one item, Send test notification, with a quiet second line saying the result is a sample. Sending used to be a paper-plane button beside Edit and members pressed it by accident (#1097), so a stray press now only opens a menu. The component reads isSending and isCoolingDown from TestAlertService and owns no state of its own: the button becomes a spinner while a request is out, and the item is dimmed with the existing "Cooldown active" wording for the 15 seconds after. Pokéstop events, max battles and fort changes render no menu, and alarm-card-parity.spec.ts pins that.

AlarmListToolbarComponent (shared/components/alarm-list-toolbar/) is the bar above every list: search, count, sort menu and the select-mode toggle, plus a "no matches" line with the way back. Each list decides what a search matches and what each sort means through shared/utils/alarm-list-query.ts, whose sort is stable, so the default order (orderAlarms) survives ties and an edited card does not move.

docs.title: Quiet periods
docs.text:
Three components make up the quiet surface: QuietChipComponent on the card, QuietSheetComponent for muting one subject, and QuietListSheetComponent for reviewing what is muted.

The chip appears only where the card names something a mute can be scoped to, which is six templates and four scopes: pokemon and nests (pokemon), gyms and raids (gym), max battles (station), and the areas list (area). Quests, invasions, lures and fort changes deliberately do not carry it — a quest is defined by its reward, an invasion by its grunt type, a lure by its lure type, and a fort change by nothing that maps to a mute scope. quiet-surface-parity.spec.ts pins both halves of that list, so adding the chip to a tenth surface or dropping it from one of the six fails the build.

docs.title: Places section
docs.text: PlacesSectionComponent (shared/components/places-section/) lists the user's named places inside the Areas & places page's Pin and places panel, directly under the row holding the pin. The page is map first: AreaMapComponent draws the pin and every named place as markers (its places input), and clicking one opens the panel. The pin is not repeated in the list, since the row above it is the pin. Adding a place borrows LocationDialogComponent as a coordinate picker rather than growing a second map, then asks for the name separately.

docs.title: Server profile card
docs.text: ServerProfileCardComponent (shared/components/server-profile-card/) sits on the admin settings page and says which PoracleNG the deployment talks to, which capabilities are switched on, and whether the version is below what this build needs. Only enabled capabilities are listed — a key present and false means the binary knows the feature and has it off. See Server capability probe.

docs.title: Level selector
docs.text:
LevelSelectorComponent (shared/components/level-selector/) is the chip-based picker for raid, egg, and raid-boss levels. A single pickerType: 'raid' | 'egg' | 'boss' input drives layout and behavior — multi-select vs single-select, whether the Any (9000) chip is offered, and which canonical levels go in the primary chip row vs the "More raid types…" overflow menu. See Raid level selector for the user-facing behavior.

RaidLevelService (core/services/raid-level.service.ts) fetches the canonical raid-level list from GET /api/masterdata/raid-levels on first dialog/list usage and caches the result in a signal. A baked-in KNOWN_LEVELS constant in core/models/raid-level.models.ts is the fallback when the network call fails or hasn't resolved. The same constant powers the synchronous resolveLevel(value) helper used by LevelLabelPipe so alarm cards have a usable label even before the API response lands. The pipe detects ngx-translate's key-not-found pass-through and falls back to a generic "Level {n}" string so future masterfile additions don't leak raw translation keys into the UI.

Custom integers typed via the + Add chip live in the component's local signal — they are not persisted to localStorage. Closing the dialog (or refreshing the page) discards typed-but-not-saved chips. Existing alarms at custom levels re-seed the chip when the edit dialog opens via the [value] input setter.

docs.title: Gym picker
docs.text:
GymPickerComponent (shared/components/gym-picker/) is a standalone autocomplete for selecting a gym from the scanner database. It wraps a Material autocomplete input with debounced search (300ms, minimum 2 characters). Each option row displays the gym photo thumbnail, name, and area name. The component exposes a two-way gymId model binding so parent dialogs can read/write the selected gym ID directly.

In edit mode, when the component initializes with an existing gymId, an effect() calls ScannerService.getGymById to load and display the gym details. A searchSubject piped through debounceTime / distinctUntilChanged / switchMap drives the autocomplete options. Subscription cleanup uses takeUntilDestroyed.

Integrated into gym-add-dialog, gym-edit-dialog, raid-add-dialog, and raid-edit-dialog.

docs.title: Gym list cards
docs.text: Gym alarm list cards resolve and display targeted gym names. When alarms have a gym_id, the component uses ScannerService.getGymById with forkJoin to batch-lookup gym details, showing the gym name on each card instead of the raw ID.

docs.title: GeoJSON import/export
docs.text: The geofences module includes GeoJSON import and export dialogs for interoperability with external mapping tools. Users can export their custom geofences as GeoJSON FeatureCollection files and import geofences from GeoJSON files. The import dialog validates the GeoJSON structure and previews polygons on a Leaflet map before confirming the import. Admin geofence management also supports GeoJSON export for bulk operations.

docs.title: Linked Accounts
docs.text:
A person who uses Poracle from both Discord and Telegram has two PoracleNG humans, one discord:user and one telegram:user. PoracleWeb.NET pairs them so the person sees one list of alarms, saves a location or an area once, and chooses which app each alarm is delivered to. PoracleNG knows nothing about the pair: every call PoracleWeb.NET makes is one it would make for an unlinked person, sent once per human.

This page is the technical reference. What a person sees is in Linked Accounts, and the operator side of Telegram is in Telegram and Discord and Telegram.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
PoracleNG owns humans, profiles, areas, saved places and tracking rules, and it delivers alerts through its Discord and Telegram bots. PoracleWeb.NET adds one table, poracle_web.account_links, and a layer of services that turn "the signed-in human" into "the signed-in person's humans". Nothing in PoracleNG was changed for the feature.

The diagram shows where the pair lives and which side of the line each piece sits on.

flowchart LR
    SPA["Angular SPA<br/>Linked accounts page,<br/>drift banner, Deliver to"]
    subgraph API["PoracleWeb.NET API"]
        Ctl["Controllers<br/>alarms, person settings,<br/>account-link, alarm-move"]
        Link["ILinkedAccount<br/>resolves the pair"]
        Svc["LinkedAlarmRouter, AlarmMover,<br/>PairedHumanWriter, PairDriftService"]
        Proxies["PoracleNG proxies"]
    end
    Links[("poracle_web.account_links")]
    NG["PoracleNG /api/v2<br/>two humans, unaware of the pair"]
    DBot["Discord bot"]
    TBot["Telegram bot"]
    SPA -->|"HTTPS + JWT"| Ctl
    Ctl --> Link
    Ctl --> Svc
    Link -->|"link row"| Links
    Link -->|"human reads"| Proxies
    Svc -->|"one call per human"| Proxies
    Proxies -->|"X-Poracle-Secret"| NG
    NG -->|"alerts for discord:user"| DBot
    NG -->|"alerts for telegram:user"| TBot
    DBot -.->|"bot commands change one human"| NG
    TBot -.->|"bot commands change one human"| NG

The dotted edges are where drift comes from: a bot command writes the one human it was sent from, and PoracleWeb.NET finds out on its next read (see Drift).

docs.title: Data model
docs.text:
account_links is created by the AddAccountLinks migration.

Column Type Notes id int, PK Auto-increment discord_id varchar(64), required, unique The discord:user human's id telegram_id varchar(64), required, unique The telegram:user human's id default_destination varchar(16), required discord or telegram. New alarms go here when the dialog names no app. Set to the side that made the link discord_verified_at datetime, nullable When that side's identity was last proven telegram_verified_at datetime, nullable Same, for Telegram created_at datetime When the link was made

The two unique indexes are the whole of "one link per account": an id can appear in at most one row, on its own side. A concurrent second link trips the index, and the repository turns that into AccountLinkConflictException.

The row joins to PoracleNG by id only. Nothing else about either human is stored here, and nothing about the pair is stored in PoracleNG. The type is checked live on every resolve rather than trusted from the column.

What isn't stored is computed per request:

  • Pending state. A side whose human doesn't exist yet ("Waiting to register") is a link row whose id PoracleNG answers 404 for.
  • Paused state. Read from the human's admin_disable and enabled.
  • Drift. Compared from fresh reads of both humans.

LinkedPair (Core.Models/AccountLink.cs) is the resolved form handed to every consumer:

Member Meaning CallerId The signed-in (or impersonated) human Link The AccountLink row, or null when unlinked Discord, Telegram A PairSide each: HumanId, Exists, Pause (None, NotRegistered, AdminDisabled, Stopped), Name IsLinked Link is not null ExistingHumanIds The sides that exist, the caller's own first. What reads and writes walk LinkedHumanIds Every id the link names, existing or not. For limits that must hold while a side is away, such as the drawn-fence cap SideOf(id), HumanIdFor(side) Map between a human id and its side

LinkedPair.Single(callerId) is the unlinked answer, and every consumer treats it as "do exactly what you did before linking existed".

docs.title: Pair resolution
docs.text:
ILinkedAccount.ResolveAsync(userId) answers the pair for the current request. The JWT carries nothing about the link, so a link made, cut or retargeted in another tab takes effect without a new token.

  1. Feature gate. With disable_account_linking on, it returns LinkedPair.Single before reading anything. Rows are kept, so switching the feature back on restores every pair.
  2. The link row, cached one minute under account-link:{id}. A cached "no link" is held too, so an unlinked person costs one database read a minute.
  3. Each side's human, read through IHumanService.GetByIdAsync (PoracleNG's GET /api/v2/humans/{id}), cached one minute under account-link-human:{id}.
  4. Type check. A side whose live type isn't discord:user or telegram:user respectively is treated as absent (Exists: false), and the retype is logged once per cache fill.
  5. Pause. admin_disable = 1 is AdminDisabled, enabled = 0 is Stopped, a missing human is NotRegistered.

The sequence below is one request from a linked person, with a cold cache.

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Controller
    participant L as ILinkedAccount
    participant G as IFeatureGate
    participant M as IMemoryCache
    participant R as AccountLinkRepository
    participant H as IHumanService
    participant NG as PoracleNG v2
    C->>L: ResolveAsync(userId)
    L->>G: disable_account_linking?
    G-->>L: enabled
    L->>M: account-link:{userId}
    M-->>L: miss
    L->>R: GetByHumanIdAsync(userId)
    R-->>L: AccountLink
    L->>M: cache link, 1 min
    loop each side
        L->>M: account-link-human:{id}
        M-->>L: miss
        L->>H: GetByIdAsync(id)
        H->>NG: GET /api/v2/humans/{id}
        NG-->>H: human, or 404
        H-->>L: Human or null
        L->>M: cache human, 1 min
        L->>L: check type, read pause
    end
    L-->>C: LinkedPair

Invalidation. Invalidate(humanId) drops the link and human entries for that id and, when the cached link names them, both ids of the pair. Link, unlink, a default change and the account purge call it for both ids explicitly, because a partner can only be found through a cached link. The cache is the process's IMemoryCache, so a second API instance sees a change within the minute.

Fails open on poracle_web. A failed account_links read, or a row the repository can't read (AccountLinkUnreadableException, such as an unknown default_destination), answers LinkedPair.Single, logs a warning and is not cached. The pair is resolved before every person-level write, so a database outage must not stop an unlinked person from saving anything. A linked person acts as their signed-in account alone until the read succeeds.

Doesn't fail open on PoracleNG. A human read that fails for any reason other than 404 throws, as every GetHumanAsync caller does. The alarm and person controllers answer that 503 through PoracleUnreachableExceptionFilter.

docs.title: Linking flows
docs.text:
IAccountLinkService.LinkAsync(callerHumanId, newSide, newId, newName) is the one place a verified identity becomes a link. Its checks, in order:

  1. disable_account_linking must be off (link_disabled, 403). Checked here rather than only on the routes, so a Discord or Telegram sign-in started before an admin switched linking off can't complete.
  2. The caller's human must be discord:user or telegram:user, and the new side must be the other app (link_wrong_type).
  3. The new id must be digits only, 1 to 20 characters, no leading zero, and fit a long for Telegram (link_bad_id).
  4. Neither id may already be in a link (link_taken). Checked before anything is created, so a refused link never leaves a provisioned human behind.
  5. If PoracleNG has a human with the new id, it must be the matching person type (link_type_mismatch). This is what stops a channel, group or webhook being linked.
  6. If it has none, LinkRegisterModes.Parse reads link_register_missing (off, when-qualified, always; a stored true is always, false or absent is off, anything unrecognised is off). always has the provisioner create it (below). when-qualified does so only for a Telegram side that ITelegramRegistrationCheck admits, passing the communities it found. Otherwise, and for a missing Discord side under when-qualified, the link is stored anyway and that side waits to register.
  7. The row is inserted with default_destination set to the caller's side. An index collision rolls back a provisioned human and answers link_taken.

docs.title: Discord
docs.text:
The Discord half reuses the sign-in OAuth flow and its callback. POST /api/account-link/discord/start builds the authorize URL with the same DiscordAuthorizeRequest the sign-in uses, which sets the oauth_state cookie, and also sets an oauth_link cookie: an AccountLinkTicket sealed with ASP.NET Data Protection (purpose AccountLink.v1) holding the caller's human id, that flow's state and a 10-minute expiry.

The sequence follows one link from the Linked accounts page back to it.

sequenceDiagram
    actor U as Person, signed in with Telegram
    participant SPA
    participant API as AccountLinkController
    participant D as Discord
    participant CB as AuthController callback
    participant S as IAccountLinkService
    U->>SPA: Link Discord
    SPA->>API: POST /api/account-link/discord/start
    API-->>SPA: url, Set-Cookie oauth_state and oauth_link
    SPA->>D: authorize, state=S1
    D->>CB: GET /api/auth/discord/callback?code&state=S1
    CB->>CB: check state against oauth_state
    CB->>CB: open oauth_link, ticket.State == S1
    CB->>D: exchange code, GET /users/@me
    D-->>CB: discord id, username
    CB->>CB: enable_discord and role checks
    CB->>S: LinkAsync(ticket.HumanId, Discord, id, name)
    S-->>CB: AccountLink
    CB-->>SPA: 302 /linked-accounts#linked=discord

The callback deletes the oauth_link cookie whatever happens. A ticket that is tampered with or expired ends on #link_error=link_expired. Discord sign-in switched off by the time the callback runs is link_app_unavailable; an account that fails the role check is link_not_permitted. A ticket whose state doesn't match the callback's is ignored, so an abandoned link can't turn a later ordinary sign-in into a link, and that request continues as a sign-in. The link branch never looks up a human for sign-in and never issues a token. A cancelled approval is link_cancelled, and a failed token exchange or user read is link_failed. The sign-in start deletes any leftover ticket.

docs.title: Telegram
docs.text:
The Telegram half is the login widget in redirect mode. The widget's callback mode (data-onauth) makes Telegram's script eval the attribute, which the site's CSP refuses (script-src has no unsafe-eval), so the button never drew. In redirect mode (data-auth-url) Telegram navigates the browser to the page with the signed fields in the query string, and the page posts them on.

sequenceDiagram
    actor U as Person, signed in with Discord
    participant SPA as /linked-accounts
    participant T as Telegram widget
    participant API as AccountLinkController
    participant V as TelegramWidgetVerifier
    participant S as IAccountLinkService
    U->>T: approve in Telegram, allow messages
    T->>SPA: redirect ?id&first_name&username&auth_date&hash
    SPA->>SPA: read fields, clear them from the URL
    SPA->>API: POST /api/account-link/telegram {fields}
    API->>V: Verify(fields, bot token, 10 min)
    V-->>API: valid, user id, name
    API->>S: LinkAsync(caller, Telegram, id, name)
    S-->>API: AccountLink
    API-->>SPA: 200 {linked}

TelegramWidgetVerifier is shared with Telegram sign-in, which allows 24 hours; linking allows 10 minutes. It refuses a payload with no id or hash, a non-numeric id, a missing or non-numeric auth_date, one more than five minutes in the future (clock drift), and one older than the window, all before the hash. The hash is HMAC-SHA256 of the sorted key=value lines, keyed with SHA-256 of the bot token, compared in constant time. An expired payload answers link_expired, every other failure link_bad_id.

The widget asks for write access (data-request-access="write"), which lets the bot DM the person.

docs.title: Registering the missing side
docs.text:
Under always, or when-qualified with a qualified person, LinkedHumanProvisioner.CreateMirrorAsync creates the other human by copying the caller's. Alarms are never copied.

TelegramRegistrationCheck mirrors PoracleNG's /poracle rule (telegrambot/reconciliation.go, reconcileNonAreaSecurity and reconcileAreaSecurity). IPoracleApiProxy.GetTelegramRegistrationGroupsAsync reads values.telegram.channels, values.area_security.enabled and each values.area_security.communities[] row's name and telegram_channels from GET /api/config/values. TelegramBotApiClient asks Telegram's getChatMember for each group once. member, administrator, creator and restricted count (a restricted user whose is_member is false doesn't); left, kicked and every failure don't. Without area security one group is enough. With it, every community whose own group holds the person is recorded, lowercased, and the create sends them as community, which PoracleNG turns into the area restriction. The bot token is part of the request path, so the client logs only the failure's type and the group id, never a URL or an exception message.

  1. POST /api/v2/humans with the new id, name, type, location, community membership and language, and the name of the caller's profile 1 as the default profile's name.
  2. Check the new human's default profile is number 1.
  3. Walk profile numbers from 1 to the caller's highest. PoracleNG gives a new profile the lowest free number, so each POST .../profiles must come back with the expected number or the whole create fails. A gap in the caller's numbering is filled with a placeholder profile, deleted at the end.
  4. Write each profile's areas and location with POST .../areas?profile=N and .../location?profile=N, and copy its active_hours. The areas pass through IUserAreaWriter.FilterAllowedAsync first, the same check profile create uses. The new human isn't linked yet, so its own allowed set can't see the person's drawn fences: a name is kept when either the new account or the caller's may select it, and a dropped name is logged at debug.
  5. Switch to the caller's active profile, delete the placeholders, then copy saved places. A place PoracleNG refuses is logged and skipped.

Profile numbers must agree because moves and drift compare them across the pair. A legacy profile 0 isn't copied: PoracleNG never numbers a new profile 0.

Any failure deletes the human it created, but only if PoracleNG still holds one with this link's type and name. Another request may have created that id in between, and that row isn't ours to remove. The caller sees link_provision_failed and nothing is linked.

docs.title: Refusal codes
docs.text:
Every refusal carries { error, code }. The SPA words the code; error is the English fallback.

Code Status Meaning link_wrong_type 400 The caller isn't a Discord or Telegram person, or both sides are the same app link_bad_id 400 The id isn't a possible account id, or the Telegram payload didn't verify link_type_mismatch 400 That id is a PoracleNG human of another type, such as a channel or group link_taken 409 One of the ids is already in a link link_expired 400 The Telegram payload or the Discord ticket is past its 10 minutes link_app_unavailable 403 That app's sign-in isn't available on this site: not configured in .env, or enable_discord / enable_telegram is off. Sent by the Discord start, the Telegram link and the Discord callback's link branch link_not_permitted 403 The account fails the site's sign-in rules (a required Discord role), or (for a default change) that side isn't registered link_disabled 403 disable_account_linking is on. Checked when the link completes, so a Discord or Telegram sign-in started before an admin switched linking off can't finish. Unlinking still works link_provision_failed 502 Registering the missing side failed and was rolled back link_failed redirect The Discord exchange or user read failed link_cancelled redirect The person backed out of Discord's approval

The Discord flow can't answer JSON, so it ends on /linked-accounts#link_error=<code>.

The other routes: DELETE /api/account-link unlinks, PUT /api/account-link/default {destination} sets the default app, and GET /api/account-link/status answers { linked, link, sides, defaultDestination, drift, legacyProfileZero }. Admins have GET /api/admin/account-links and DELETE /api/admin/account-links/{humanId}, which aren't gated on disable_account_linking so a stuck pair can still be cut while the feature is off.

docs.title: Alarm routing
docs.text:
The eleven alarm controllers reach their services only through LinkedAlarmRouter. Unlinked, each method makes the exact call it made before, and the JSON is byte-identical: Destination and PausedDestination are omitted when null, and the router only sets them for a linked caller.

Router method Linked behaviour ListAsync Reads each existing human's rules for the profile and concatenates them, stamping destination FindAsync(svc, userId, uid) Looks the uid up on each human in turn; answers the alarm and its owner id FindAsync(userId, lookup) Same, for a lookup narrower than a uid. The invasion controller uses it with ?kind=event or invasion, because invasion and Pokéstop event rules share one list but number their uids separately CountAsync, DeleteAllAsync, UpdateDistanceAllAsync Run once per human; distance results are merged UpdateDistanceByUidsAsync One list read per human maps every uid to its owner, then one call per owner. An unknown uid goes to the caller, where the service skips it as it always did CreateTargetAsync The human a create belongs to (below) MoveTargetAsync, MoveAsync An edit naming the other app becomes a move

A create with no destination goes to the pair's default app, or to the caller while the default side has no human. A create naming a side with no human answers 409 ("Telegram isn't set up yet"), and an unknown destination 400, both through AlarmDestinationExceptionFilter. A create that lands on a paused side is answered with pausedDestination: true so the dialog can say the alert won't arrive until that app is on again.

Edits, deletes and test alerts go to the owner FindAsync returned, so a uid on either human works from the merged list.

docs.title: Moves
docs.text:
An alarm changes app in two ways: PUT /api/{type}/{uid} with a destination naming the other app (an edit that moves), and POST /api/alarm-move { type, uids, destination, kind? } for a selection of up to 500. Both call AlarmMover, and both are refused with 403 while an admin is viewing as someone else, because a move writes the other human's rules. alarm-move is rate limited to 10 requests a minute per person and is gated on disable_account_linking and on the type's own disable_* key.

The protocol, for one alarm:

sequenceDiagram
    participant AM as AlarmMover
    participant NG as PoracleNG v2
    participant Svc as Type's alarm service
    participant QP as QuickPickUidTransfer
    Note over AM: preflight, nothing written yet
    AM->>NG: GET both humans
    AM->>AM: same current_profile_no?
    AM->>NG: GET target's saved places, if the rule names one
    AM->>AM: target may use the rule's override areas?
    AM->>NG: GET source rows, to carry unmodelled fields
    Note over AM,Svc: create on the target
    AM->>Svc: CreateAsync(targetId, rule)
    Svc->>NG: POST tracking?dry_run=true
    NG-->>Svc: insert, update or unchanged
    Svc->>NG: POST tracking, if insert
    Svc-->>AM: created rule and uid
    Note over AM,NG: delete the source, at most twice
    AM->>Svc: DeleteAsync(sourceId, uid, kind)
    Svc->>NG: DELETE tracking/{type}/{uid}
    Note over AM,QP: follow the uid in quick-pick state
    AM->>QP: TransferAsync(source, target, profile, type, old, new)

Why create, then delete. The other order has a window where the alert exists nowhere, and a failed create in that window loses it. Creating first means the worst case is an alert on both apps, which the person can see and fix.

Preflight refuses before any write when the target side has no human (not_set_up), the two humans are on different active profiles (different_profiles; a rule lives on its human's active profile, and a v2 read carries no profile_no), the rule measures from a saved place the target lacks (place_missing), or the target may not use one of its override areas (area_not_allowed, through IUserAreaPolicy).

The create goes through the type's own service, so it gets the same dry-run protection as an Add (see PoracleNG API Proxy). The model is cleared of its uid and stamps first. Stored fields the typed model has no property for are carried across, as an edit does with TrackingFieldPreserver (not for Pokéstop events, which have no untyped path). An identical rule already on the target counts as moved onto that rule, using ExistingUid. A would-be takeover is a conflict carrying the target rule's existingUid.

The delete names the invasion kind, so moving a Pokéstop event never deletes a plain invasion that shares its uid. It's tried twice. If it still fails the alarm stays on both apps.

Quick picks. A quick pick's applied state is kept per human and profile, so the moved uid is added to the same pick's row on the target first and then removed from the source's. A source row left tracking nothing is deleted. A failure here is logged and doesn't change the outcome.

Outcome Meaning Single edit answers moved On the target, gone from the source 200, the rule as it now stands, X-Move-Status: moved alreadyThere Already on the requested app; nothing to do 409 (an edit only asks to move to the other app) conflict The target holds a rule this one would take over. Nothing written 409 with existingUid, through the global filter sourceRemains Copied, but the original couldn't be deleted 200, X-Move-Status: source_remains refused A check failed before anything was written 409 { error, code, app, place } failed The create failed in a way PoracleNG didn't explain; it may or may not exist on the target. Source untouched 502

Bulk moves answer { results: [{ uid, status, newUid, existingUid, reason, reasonCode, reasonApp, reasonPlace }] }, one per uid, plus not_found for a uid neither human has. Reason codes: already_there, not_linked, not_yours, not_found, not_set_up, different_profiles, place_missing, area_not_allowed, invalid, conflict, failed, source_remains. The SPA translates the code and never shows reason.

The single edit answers in the body PUT always had, the alarm, so whether the original is gone travels as X-Move-Status. It and X-Pair-Warning are in CorsPolicySetup.ExposedHeaders; an unexposed header reads as absent and a half-done move would look clean.

docs.title: Paired writes
docs.text:
Every person-level write goes through IPairedHumanWriter.WriteAsync(userId, write):

  1. Resolve the pair.
  2. Run the write for the signed-in human. If it throws, that's the request's error, and the other human isn't tried.
  3. Run the write for the other existing human. A paused side is still written; only a side with no human is skipped.
  4. If the second write fails, the request still succeeds with the first side's result, and the response carries X-Pair-Warning: {"side":"telegram","reason":"...","code":"..."}.

The warning never changes a body or a status. code is one of unreachable (anything without a sentence meant for people, so a host and port never reach the browser), refused (PoracleNG's own sentence, as reason), out_of_step and rename_refused. The SPA's pairWarningInterceptor reads it once per response and shows "Saved for Discord, but not for Telegram", with an action that opens Linked accounts.

The sequence shows a location save where the second side is unreachable.

sequenceDiagram
    participant SPA
    participant LC as LocationController
    participant W as PairedHumanWriter
    participant NG as PoracleNG v2
    SPA->>LC: PUT location
    LC->>W: WriteAsync(userId, SetLocation)
    W->>NG: POST /humans/{discord}/location
    NG-->>W: 200
    W->>NG: POST /humans/{telegram}/location
    NG--xW: connection refused
    W->>W: log, warning code unreachable
    W-->>LC: Primary result plus warning
    LC-->>SPA: 200, X-Pair-Warning
    SPA->>SPA: toast "Saved for Discord, but not for Telegram"

What goes through it: location, saved places (add, move, delete), area selection, profile create, update, switch, delete, duplicate and import, alert language, quiet periods, quest summary schedules, and alerts on and off. The cleaning toggle and the geofence services do the same thing in their own code, with the same warning shape.

A few writes need more than "the same call twice":

  • Profile numbers. PoracleNG gives each human its own lowest free number, so a profile created on both can land on different numbers if the pair had drifted. PairedNewProfile.ReconcileAsync keeps the signed-in side's profile, deletes the other side's mismatched one, and warns out_of_step. An edit to profile N reaches the other human only if its profile N has the same name; otherwise it's left alone with the same warning.
  • Alerts on. Stop reaches both humans. Start reaches the other human only if nothing paused it, so an operator's block or a stop the person made in the other app is never undone.
  • Areas. Each human's list goes through IUserAreaWriter, which authorises names for that human. UserAreaPolicy counts the pair's drawn fences as each human's own.
  • Quiet periods. PoracleNG canonicalises an area's casing per human and its delete matches exactly, so lifting one on the other side sends the value that human's own list returned.
  • Drawn geofences. A fence belongs to one human id but is listed, toggled, renamed and deleted across the pair, the ownership check accepts either id, and the 10-fence cap counts LinkedHumanIds, so the pair can't draw past it while one side is away.

docs.title: Drift
docs.text:
The two humans drift because PoracleNG's bots write the human a command came from. !location in Discord moves the Discord human; /profile in Telegram switches the Telegram human. PoracleWeb.NET never resolves a difference on its own. It shows it and waits for the person to choose.

IPairDriftService.GetAsync reads both humans (human, area list, profiles, saved places) in parallel and compares five settings. It returns nothing unless both sides exist.

Field Compared as location Latitude and longitude rounded to 5 decimal places areas The active profile's areas, each through UserAreaPolicy.Key (lowercase, trimmed, _ equal to space, PoracleNG's NormalizeAreaKey), de-duplicated and sorted, so order doesn't matter profiles Every profile by number: name (exact), active_hours (numbers or numeric strings read as ints, entries sorted by day, hour, minute), and the areas and location of profiles neither side is on current_profile The active profile number. Skipped when either side is on profile 0 places Saved places by lowercase label, with location to 5 decimal places

The profiles either side is on are compared without their areas and location, because each human holds that profile's live copy and the location and areas lines already compare it. Comparing both reported one cause twice.

Not compared, though written to both: alert language, quiet periods (held in PoracleNG's memory and gone on restart) and summary schedules. Profile 0 is outside the pair: PoracleNG never numbers a new profile 0, so it's never compared, copied, switched to or deleted, and status reports which side has one as legacyProfileZero for a note on the page.

Each item carries both sides' comparable values, a fingerprint (lowercase hex SHA-256 over the Discord value, a newline, and the Telegram value) and details outside the fingerprint (profile names, place labels as typed) so renaming one profile doesn't stale another line.

The state diagram follows one difference from a bot command to its resolution.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> InStep
    InStep --> Drifted: bot command writes one human
    Drifted --> Shown: status read finds it
    Shown --> Banner: first read or a navigation
    Banner --> Dismissed: dismiss, per fingerprint
    Banner --> Panel: Review
    Dismissed --> Panel: open Linked accounts
    Panel --> Resolving: person keeps one side
    Resolving --> InStep: other side written
    Resolving --> Panel: refused, drift_changed and others
    Resolving --> Panel: partially_applied

The banner sits under the toolbar, appears only with the first status read or at a navigation (never mid-page), is hidden while impersonating and on Linked accounts itself, and stores dismissed fingerprints in sessionStorage. The panel on Linked accounts always lists every difference, with what each choice changes in the other app. A choice that deletes something (a profile or a place) asks first, naming it. LinkedAccountService.refreshSoon() re-reads status shortly after any successful write, so the banner never offers to undo what the person just did.

docs.title: Resolving
docs.text:
POST /api/account-link/resolve { field, keep, expected } makes the other human match the kept one for one field. It writes the other human only, never through PairedHumanWriter, which would rewrite the side being kept. kind (event or invasion) applies to the invasion list only, where a Pokéstop event and an invasion can share a uid. Everything that can refuse is checked before the first write.

flowchart TD
    A["POST resolve"] --> B{"Impersonating?"}
    B -->|yes| R403["403"]
    B -->|no| C{"field, keep,<br/>expected valid?"}
    C -->|no| R400["400"]
    C -->|yes| L{"Linked?"}
    L -->|no| R400L["400 no linked account"]
    L -->|yes| D{"Both sides<br/>exist?"}
    D -->|no| CH["409 drift_changed"]
    D -->|yes| E["Fresh read of both humans"]
    E --> F{"Fingerprint<br/>still matches?"}
    F -->|no| CH
    F -->|yes| G{"Which field?"}
    G -->|"current_profile"| H{"Other side has<br/>that profile?"}
    H -->|no| PM["409 profile_missing"]
    G -->|profiles| I{"A profile to delete<br/>holds alarms?"}
    I -->|yes| PH["409 profile_holds_alarms"]
    G -->|places| J{"A place to delete<br/>is used by alarms?"}
    J -->|yes| PU["409 place_in_use"]
    H -->|yes| W["Write the other human"]
    I -->|no| W
    J -->|no| W
    G -->|"location, areas"| W
    W --> K{"Failed after<br/>a write landed?"}
    K -->|yes| PA["409 partially_applied"]
    K -->|no| OK["204"]

Refusals are DriftRefusalExceptions, answered by PairDriftExceptionFilter as 409 { error, code, side, name, count }. Alarm counts for profile_holds_alarms and place_in_use come from GET /api/v2/humans/{id}/tracking?all_profiles=true, because a place belongs to the human, not one profile.

The order matters within a field too:

  • Profiles before the active profile. Switching never creates a profile, so the profiles line is listed first and settled first.
  • Missing profile numbers are created in order, with filler profiles to reach a gap, each one checked against the number PoracleNG assigns. Fillers are deleted in a finally.
  • Extras are deleted last. If the other human is on one of them it's switched to the kept side's profile first, so PoracleNG doesn't choose where it lands.
  • Areas go through IUserAreaWriter.SaveSelectionAsync for the other human, so names are authorised for the human they're written to.

Once any write has landed, a later failure is partially_applied rather than the underlying error, so the person is never told nothing changed when something did. The SPA re-reads status after every resolve, success or not.

docs.title: Failure handling and invariants
docs.text: Invariant How it holds A move never loses an alert Create on the target before deleting the source. A failed delete is sourceRemains, both copies listed and tagged A paused side is never re-enabled Start skips a paused other side, and no other linked-account path calls enable Drift is never resolved without a choice Resolve needs a field, a side and the fingerprint the person saw; nothing resolves in the background Unlinked people are unaffected Every component answers LinkedPair.Single with today's calls; alarm JSON is byte-identical PoracleNG is unchanged Only existing /api/v2 routes, one human at a time A refused link leaves nothing behind link_taken is checked before provisioning; a provisioned human is rolled back if it's still ours A second-side failure doesn't fail the request X-Pair-Warning, never a changed status or body When this is down What happens poracle_web database ILinkedAccount fails open: everyone acts as their signed-in account, writes reach one human, nothing is cached. Linking, unlinking and default changes fail PoracleNG Human reads throw; alarm, person and move endpoints answer 503. A status read fails and the SPA keeps what it showed. A drift read failing alone answers drift: null, which hides the banner PoracleNG for the second human only The write lands on the first; X-Pair-Warning with unreachable

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Link ticket. The Discord link's identity is a Data Protection-sealed cookie bound to that flow's OAuth state and good for 10 minutes. A forged or stale cookie opens to null. The state check still guards CSRF as it does for sign-in.
  • Telegram HMAC. Verified server-side against the bot token, with a 10-minute window for linking and a five-minute allowance for clock drift. The SPA never decides whether a payload is valid.
  • Impersonation. Every account-link write, resolve and move is refused with 403 while an admin views as someone else, and the admin link routes refuse too: UserId is then the inspected account. The status read stays open.
  • Feature gate. AccountLinkController and AlarmMoveController carry [RequireFeatureEnabled(disable_account_linking)], and ILinkedAccount answers single accounts when it's off.
  • CSP. script-src allows https://telegram.org and frame-src allows https://oauth.telegram.org for the widget. No unsafe-eval, which is why redirect mode.
  • Logging. Linked-account log lines pass human ids through LogSafe.Id, which masks URL-shaped ids (webhook tokens). Discord and Telegram user ids are logged unchanged. Bot tokens and widget hashes are never logged.
  • Destinations never link. LinkAsync accepts only a discord:user caller with a telegram:user partner or the reverse, and ILinkedAccount re-checks both types on every resolve. A channel, group or webhook can't join a pair, so no alert ever leaves a person's own DM because of a link.

docs.text:
Backend tests are in Tests/Pgan.PoracleWebNet.Tests/:

Area Tests Resolution and linking LinkedAccountTests, AccountLinkServiceTests, AccountLinkRepositoryTests, AccountLinkMappingTests, AccountLinkControllerTests, AuthControllerLinkCallbackTests, TelegramWidgetVerifierTests, LinkedHumanProvisionerTests Alarm routing LinkedAlarmRouterTests, LinkedAlarmOwnerRoutingTests, LinkedCreateFallbackTests, LinkedInvasionKindTests, AlarmDestinationExceptionFilterTests Moves AlarmMoverTests, AlarmMoverReasonCodeTests, AlarmMoverCarriesStoredFieldsTests, QuickPickUidTransferTests, AlarmMoveControllerTests, AlarmMoveWhileImpersonatingTests, AlarmMoveRateLimitTests, MoveStatusSerializationTests Paired writes and drift PairedHumanWriterTests, LinkedPersonWritesTests, LinkedGeofenceOwnershipTests, LinkedSurfacesTests, PairDriftServiceTests

Three architecture tests in Tests/.../Architecture/ fail the build when a rule is broken:

Test Rule AlarmControllersUseRouterTests None of the eleven alarm controllers passes this.UserId (directly or through a local) to its service; everything goes through LinkedAlarmRouter PersonWritesUseWriterTests A person-level write (location, places, areas, profiles, language, quiet periods, alerts on and off, summaries) in the person controllers or UserGeofenceService is made inside IPairedHumanWriter AlarmUpdateMoveGuardTests Each alarm controller's PUT /{uid} refuses a move while impersonating, before anything is merged or written

SPA specs cover linked-account.service, alarm-move.service, pair-warning.interceptor, the Linked accounts page, pair-drift-panel, pair-drift-banner, deliver-to-field and deliver-to, the redirect-mode telegram-login-button, and the admin settings for linking.

docs.title: Extension points
docs.text:
IAccountLinkService is the only way to create a link. A caller hands it an identity it has already verified, and the service applies the pairing rules, provisioning and invalidation. Another sign-in provider could call it the same way the Discord callback and the Telegram endpoint do, without touching the router, writer or drift code.

A new person-level write belongs inside IPairedHumanWriter (and in the list PersonWritesUseWriterTests checks). A new alarm type goes through LinkedAlarmRouter in its controller and gets an entry in AlarmMoveDispatcher. A new compared setting is a new DriftField with its comparable form, its resolution, and its pre-checks ahead of the first write.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: PoracleWeb.NET is a full-stack application with a .NET 10 backend API and Angular 21 frontend SPA.

docs.title: Solution structure
docs.text:

docs.text:

    Koji["Koji<br/>public areas, regions"]
    Discord["Discord API<br/>OAuth, avatars,<br/>geofence review forum"]
    Golbat["Golbat API, optional"]
    Browser -->|"HTTPS + JWT"| API
    API --> Proxies
    API --> Linked
    Linked -->|"one call per human"| Proxies
    Linked -->|"account_links"| WebDB
    Proxies -->|"humans, profiles, areas,<br/>alarms, mutes, test alerts, geocode"| NG
    NG --- NGDB
    API --> WebDB
    API --> Scanner
    API --> Koji
    API --> Discord
    API --> Golbat
    Feed -->|"admin areas"| Koji
    Feed -->|"user geofences"| WebDB
    NG -->|"pulls geofence.path"| Feed
    API -.->|"GET /api/geofence/reload"| NG

PoracleWeb.NET has no line to Poracle's database: everything about humans, profiles, areas and alarms goes through PoracleNG. Its own state lives in poracle_web. ScannerService reads the scanner database directly through ScannerContext for the gym picker, station names and weather. PoracleNG pulls its geofences from PoracleWeb.NET's feed, and PoracleWeb.NET asks it to reload them after a geofence changes.

All operations go through PoracleNG

Alarm tracking CRUD for ten of the eleven types (including Fort Change and Max Battle) is proxied via IPoracleTrackingProxy; Pokéstop Events go through IPoracleIncidentProxy instead, because that type exists only on PoracleNG's /api/v2. Single-user human/profile operations (reads, creates, location, areas, profile switch) are proxied via IPoracleHumanProxy. Humans, profiles, areas (including user-drawn geofence names) and the admin user list and delete all go through PoracleNG's /api/v2. PoracleWeb.NET has no connection to Poracle's database at all. The poracle_web database is its own. See Backend. Optional integrations include Pokemon availability from the Golbat API and weather from the optional scanner database via IScannerService. See PoracleNG API Proxy for details.

docs.title: Operations proxied through PoracleNG
docs.text: All alarm tracking writes (create, update, delete) and single-user human/profile operations go through the PoracleNG REST API, not to Poracle's database. PoracleNG detects duplicates and takeovers (PoracleWeb.NET asks with a dry run before every create), keeps humans.area and profiles.area in step, and reloads its state after each write. PoracleNG fills a field only when it's absent, and the *Create models send every field they declare, so the defaults on those models are what gets stored. See Backend Patterns. Profile duplication, from either POST /api/profile-overview/duplicate/{n} or POST /api/profiles/duplicate, uses PoracleNG's copy endpoint; import writes each alarm straight to the new profile with ?profile=N. The eleven supported alarm types are Pokemon, Raids, Eggs, Quests, Invasions, Lures, Nests, Gyms, Fort Changes, Max Battles and Pokéstop Events. PoracleNG 5.4.0 is the minimum; see Version compatibility. Test alerts are sent via PoracleNG's POST /api/test endpoint, which formats and delivers a mock notification to the user. See PoracleNG API Proxy.

docs.title: Separate databases
docs.text: PoracleWeb.NET doesn't connect to Poracle's database, which PoracleNG manages. Application-owned data (user geofences, site settings, webhook delegates, quick pick definitions) lives in a separate poracle_web database managed by EF Core migrations.

docs.title: Linked accounts on top of PoracleNG
docs.text: A person who uses both Discord and Telegram has two PoracleNG humans. PoracleWeb.NET pairs them in its own account_links table and changes nothing in PoracleNG. ILinkedAccount resolves the pair live on each request (cached a minute), LinkedAlarmRouter merges both humans' alarms and sends each write to the human that owns it, PairedHumanWriter sends every person-level write to both, AlarmMover moves an alarm between them by creating before it deletes, and PairDriftService reports where bot commands have made the two differ. For an unlinked person every one of these makes exactly the calls it made before. See Linked Accounts.

docs.title: Unified geofence feed
docs.text: PoracleWeb.NET acts as the single geofence source for PoracleNG. It fetches admin geofences from Koji, merges them with user-drawn geofences, and serves everything via one endpoint (GET /api/geofence-feed). No custom code needed in PoracleNG or Koji. User geofences support GeoJSON import/export for interoperability with external mapping tools.

docs.title: Manual mapping extensions
docs.text: Mapping lives in static extension methods under Core.Mappings/ -- there is no AutoMapper dependency. AlarmMappingExtensions provides To*() for *Create DTOs and ApplyUpdate() for *Update DTOs; EntityMappingExtensions provides ToModel(), ToEntity(), and ApplyTo() for the poracle_web tables (user geofences, site settings, webhook delegates, quick-pick definitions and applied state). Update models use nullable properties and ApplyUpdate skips nulls, so partial updates don't zero out unset fields. Alarm data itself flows as raw JSON through the PoracleNG API proxy. See Backend Patterns.

docs.title: Gym picker
docs.text: The GymPickerComponent (shared) lets users search for specific gyms when creating team, raid, or egg alarms. It calls the ScannerService (frontend) which hits scanner gym search endpoints on the backend (ScannerController). Search results use the GymSearchResult model and include photo thumbnails and area names resolved via the PointInPolygon geo utility. The scanner DB is optional — when not configured, the gym picker is hidden.

docs.title: Partitioned rate limiting
docs.text: The seven rate-limit policies partition by user or by IP, never one global bucket. This prevents one user's activity from locking out others. See Backend Patterns.

docs.title: PoracleNG Version Compatibility
docs.text:
PoracleWeb.NET requires PoracleNG 5.4.0 or newer. There is nothing to configure, and no feature switches on or off with the server's version.

5.4.0 is the minimum

PoracleWeb.NET still starts against an older PoracleNG, because refusing to start would take the whole site down over something an operator can fix in minutes. It logs an error at startup and the Versions card on Admin → Server settings says the server is too old. Beyond that it makes no allowance: it calls PoracleNG's /api/v2 routes for humans, profiles, areas, places and mutes with no v1 fallback, and a route that doesn't exist answers with a message naming the version it needs.

Upgrade PoracleNG before taking a PoracleWeb.NET release that requires a newer one. The upgrade guide covers the order of steps and the rule repair to run afterwards.

docs.title: Which PoracleNG to run
docs.text:
PoracleNG doesn't publish tagged releases. Its develop branch is where its releases land and reports 5.4.0 from 21 October 2026. Its main branch, which is also what the latest image is built from, has stayed at 5.2.1 since 1 September 2026. Choose PoracleNG by branch or image tag, never by latest.

PoracleWeb.NET PoracleNG Status This version develop at commit 34421b82 (22 October 2026) or newer; image ghcr.io/jfberry/poracleng:develop Required. Tested against 34421b82. This version 5.4.0 built before 34421b82 (21–22 October 2026) Works, except that rules on a profile number with no profile row stay out of Profile Overview and the rule repair scan (jfberry/PoracleNG#331). This version main or latest (5.2.1), or anything older than 5.4.0 Not supported. Startup logs an error, the Versions card says PoracleNG is too old, and most saves fail. 2.21.0 5.1.0 or newer, including main/latest (5.2.1) and develop (5.4.0) Supported. Quiet periods, editing saved places and alarm edits through /api/v2 need 5.2.0 or newer. Tested against 5.2.1 and against develop at 34421b82. Earlier 2.x releases 5.1.0 or newer Supported up to 5.3.x. Not tested against 5.4.0; move to 2.21.0 first. Experimental shiny line, 2.21.0-shiny.1 (image ghcr.io/pgan-dev/poracleweb.net-experimental:2.21.0-shiny.1) feat/personal-shiny (jfberry/PoracleNG#255); image ghcr.io/jfberry/poracleng:feat-personal-shiny Supported, with personal shiny alerts. On develop without that pull request it works with the shiny controls hidden.

The PoracleWeb.NET images: ghcr.io/pgan-dev/poracleweb.net:<version> for each release (and latest for the newest), :beta for PoracleWeb.NET's own develop branch, which follows the "This version" rows.

Known differences between the combinations above:

  • This version can't create an invasion alarm limited to genderless grunts, and can't save an existing one, because PoracleNG's /api/v2 has no genderless value for invasions. It says so and changes nothing.
  • 2.21.0 against a PoracleNG with personal shiny: adding an alarm next to a personal one that differs only in its radius is refused, because 2.21.0 doesn't know PoracleNG counts the personal flag as part of a rule. Nothing is overwritten.
  • 2.21.0: start PoracleNG before PoracleWeb.NET. If PoracleWeb.NET starts while PoracleNG isn't answering, quiet periods stay unavailable until PoracleWeb.NET restarts. This version doesn't have that problem.

These results come from running PoracleWeb.NET's API test suite against each pairing on 22 October 2026, using the published images.

docs.title: Why 5.4.0
docs.text:
PoracleNG 5.4.0 is the release that carries everything PoracleWeb.NET asked upstream for while working out how to stop reading and writing PoracleNG's database (jfberry/PoracleNG#328; the requests are listed under Upstream history). Supporting an older server meant keeping each workaround beside the code that replaced it, so the fallbacks were deleted instead of gated. What went in the first step, which covers humans, profiles, places, mutes and geocoding:

Removed What it did on an older PoracleNG HumanRepository, ProfileRepository Listed and deleted humans, renamed profiles and wrote a new profile's areas and location straight into PoracleNG's tables. Admin list and delete now use GET /api/v2/humans and DELETE /api/v2/humans/{id}; rename and new-profile geography use the v2 profile, area and location routes ProfileNumbering (list, create, re-list, diff) Worked out which number PoracleNG gave a new profile, because the create answered {"status":"ok"} and nothing else. The create now returns it The v1 branch of every single-human call /api/humans/... and /api/profiles/... fallbacks behind a cached "v2 is absent" flag MuteCapabilityService, PlaceUpdateCapabilityService, QuestPokecoinCapabilityService, CostumeCapabilityService Asked whether the server could do the thing before the SPA showed the control. Quiet periods, moving a saved place, Pokécoin quest rewards and costume filters are always offered The legacy geocoder call Called the geocoder PoracleNG was configured with, as Nominatim, when PoracleNG had no /api/geocode routes ProbePokestopEventsAsync Probed for the Pokéstop Events page on a server without it Poracle:TrackingApiVersion (PORACLE_TRACKING_API_VERSION) Pinned the tracking surface for a fork whose version string lied. A leftover setting is ignored Eleven PoracleV2Capabilities flags Each asked the server's /openapi.json whether one field or route existed. TrustedSetAreas went with the area writes

No call to the v1 tracking API is left in this application. Alert reads, creates, edits, deletes, bulk distance changes and the cleaning toggle are all v2 (the last two as a PATCH), with no fallback. User-drawn geofence names, including the ones an alert is limited to, reach PoracleNG through its /api/v2 routes with the trusted flag, which 5.4.0 carries; nothing is written straight to PoracleNG's database.

trusted also lifts PoracleNG's [tracking] max_areas and max_distance (jfberry/PoracleNG#346), so PoracleWeb.NET reads both from /api/config/poracleWeb and applies them itself, following PoracleNG's rules: an area list over max_areas is refused unless it only keeps or shrinks the list it replaces, a bulk radius change is cut to max_distance, and PoracleNG's admins and non-person destinations are exempt. A PoracleNG without #346 publishes neither value, and then nothing is limited here, which matches what it does itself.

docs.title: How support is decided
docs.text:
Two probes, cached for five minutes. The mechanics are in Backend Patterns.

Signal Source Answers Version GET /health Whether this server is known to be older than the minimum. Published schema GET /openapi.json Which properties each V2*Rule declares, and the numeric bounds it publishes. The tracking proxy reads them so a property PoracleWeb.NET doesn't model is carried through an edit, and a value outside the server's own bound is refused before it's sent.

PoracleServerProfile.IsSupported is true when PoracleNG answered and its version is not below MinimumSupported. An unparseable version, or the 0.0.0 a locally built binary reports because its build flags were never injected, counts as current: a build of today's source is newer than 5.4.0, and hiding features from it on a guess helps nobody. An unreachable server is not supported.

GET /health also carries a capability map, which covers bot and template-editor features and nothing about alarms. A missing key there means unsupported, PoracleNG's own contract for the map, so reaching for Supports() to answer an alarm question quietly answers false forever.

docs.title: What still depends on the server
docs.text:
Feature Signal Needs Alarm reads and deletes through /api/v2 A plaintext 404 only (no version gate) A PoracleNG that serves the v2 routes. There is no v1 fallback: a route that answers gin's plaintext 404 page not found raises PoracleUnsupportedException. Deletes of a rule outside the active profile are re-issued with ?profile=N, since v2 only deletes on the active one Alarm creates and edits through /api/v2 A plaintext 404 only (no version gate) A PoracleNG that serves the v2 routes, including dry_run on a create and 409 on a colliding edit. There is no v1 fallback: a plaintext 404 raises PoracleUnsupportedException("saving alarms", ...), and a row the translator can't express is refused rather than sent elsewhere Pokéstop-event tracking (incident) Poracle's own general.disable_showcase Only true hides the page. Absent or unreadable leaves it on Pokemon edit-in-place Poracle's tracking.pokemon_edit config The key true. Absent or unreadable hides the toggle Translated grunt display names Response field A /api/masterdata/grunts entry carrying grunt_type and short_name Rule descriptions on alarm cards Response field Any v2 read

The flags IPoracleV2SchemaService used to answer (profile create returning its number, rename through PATCH, the admin human routes, trusted setAreas) went with 5.4.0, which carries all of them. The one flag left, InvasionGruntType, is still parsed but nothing reads it. What the schema still decides is the per-rule property list and bounds above, which the tracking proxy reads from /openapi.json itself and caches.

SummaryCapabilityService and PokemonEditCapabilityService answer from Poracle's configuration, not from the version, because quest summary delivery and pokemon edit-in-place are deployment settings an operator can switch off on a server that supports them. Pokéstop Events are decided by UpstreamFeatureFlagService for the same reason, with disable_showcase.

There is deliberately no central registry. A registry was written and abandoned, because the per-feature shape already existed and two mechanisms answering one question is how one of them ends up being the one nobody updates.

Costume names are the awkward one. PoracleNG loads them into its game data under costume_{id} keys but publishes them nowhere (/api/masterdata/ offers only monsters and grunts), so the costume picker reads the same WatWowMap masterfile PoracleNG itself reads. The names are therefore English in every language, and a costume too new for that file shows as its number.

TrackingFieldPreserver carries forward every stored field PoracleWeb.NET has no model for on an edit, and bulk distance and cleaning send only the field they change, so a field set with the bot survives a web edit whatever the server is.

Rule descriptions belong on this list too. A v2 tracking read takes ?include_descriptions=true and returns a description on each rule, the same sentence PoracleNG's bot answers a !pokemon command with. It is easy to conclude otherwise: description is not on the named V2PokemonRule request schema, and the response envelope that carries it is an inline object under rules.items rather than a named component, so a search of components/schemas finds nothing. Resolve V2ListOutput...Body.properties.rules.items before believing a field is absent.

Reading and deleting an existing rule is never gated, only creating one. A rule can already exist (set with the bot, or left behind by a downgrade), and a row nobody can see is a row nobody can delete.

docs.title: When a request cannot be served
docs.text:
On a server below 5.4.0 a human, profile, area, place or geocode route answers gin's plaintext 404 page not found. Telling that apart from a real "not found" is the whole job: PoracleProblemDetails.IsProblemJson says whether the body is PoracleNG's own answer. A problem+json 404 keeps its meaning (no such human, no such profile, nothing at this coordinate). A plaintext one throws PoracleUnsupportedException(feature, "PoracleNG 5.4.0"), and the global PoracleUnsupportedExceptionFilter turns it into 409 Conflict:

{
  "error": "This PoracleNG does not support listing areas. It requires PoracleNG 5.4.0.",
  "feature": "listing areas",
  "requires": "PoracleNG 5.4.0"
}

409 rather than 403 on purpose. The 403 branch belongs to disable_* site settings and keys off a disableKey in the body; borrowing it would put an operator's switch and a version shortfall behind the same toast, and the version shortfall has the one detail worth reading in it. 409 has no interceptor branch, so it falls through to the caller, which shows the message beside the control that caused it (the same route TrackingConflictExceptionFilter takes). Address search is the exception: its caller swallows the 409, so on a too-old server the search just returns nothing.

A separate filter, PoracleUnreachableExceptionFilter, answers 503 with a message when PoracleNG cannot be reached at all. It is applied to the mute and location controllers and to all eleven alarm controllers, where a failed read used to look like an empty answer: a quiet-period chip claiming nothing is quiet, or a places list that said the user had none.

Throw PoracleUnsupportedException from the service layer, not from a controller. Quick-pick apply, profile duplicate and profile import all reach the alarm services without passing an action that could have checked first.

docs.title: Adding a feature that needs a newer PoracleNG
docs.text:
1. Raise the minimum, or gate on what the server publishes. A feature every supported server has needs no gate. One that only some do goes through IPoracleV2SchemaService: add a typed question, read it from the target's /openapi.json, answer false when the document cannot be read. Don't add a version compare; the minimum is the only version PoracleWeb.NET checks.
  2. Write a small per-feature service if the SPA needs to ask, shaped like ISummaryCapabilityService: one method, one question, answering false when it cannot tell.
  3. Guard the service write path, on create, update and bulk alike, and throw PoracleUnsupportedException(feature, requires) with words the user can act on.
  4. Give the SPA a way to ask. GET /api/admin/server-profile is admin-only, so it cannot be the answer for a user-facing control. An ordinary authenticated endpoint answers instead, like GET /api/summary-schedules/capability.
  5. Prefer hiding the control to disabling it with an explanation. There is nothing the user can do about their operator's PoracleNG version.
  6. Add a row to the table above.

docs.title: Raising the minimum again
docs.text: Move PoracleServerProfile.MinimumSupported, then delete what only the old floor needed, as 5.4.0 did. Before deleting a fallback, ask whether it is there for the old version or for a server that answers differently today. The plaintext-404 handling on each v2 route was the first kind, which is why it now throws PoracleUnsupportedException everywhere rather than falling back.

docs.title: Things that look like they differ between versions and do not
docs.text:
These are the ones most likely to send you writing a check that buys nothing.

The v1 API is frozen. Its release notes describe RFC 9457 application/problem+json error bodies and 422 status codes, and those are real, on /api/v2 only. A v1 tracking POST for a user that does not exist answers {"message":"User not found","status":"error"}; a malformed v2 path parameter answers 422 with Content-Type: application/problem+json and an errors array. Assuming the new shapes applied everywhere cost a wrongly framed issue and pull request. Each proxy reads errors through PoracleProblemDetails, which handles both dialects. See PoracleNG API Proxy.

Do not take active_hours day numbering from PoracleNG's OpenAPI schema. On older builds V2ActiveHourEntry.day was declared minimum: 0, maximum: 6 and described as "0=Sunday … 6=Saturday".
