The scheduler uses ISO weekdays, Monday 1 through Sunday 7 (isoDow in processor/cmd/processor/profiles.go), and PoracleWeb.NET validates 1 to 7. ProfileController.ValidateActiveHours is the place that would be wrong if somebody "fixed" it against a stale document.

The /health capability map is not where alarm features appear. It covers bot and template-editor features (buttons, snapshots, autocreate, tomlDts, costume, customMaps and the like) and says nothing about incidents or mutes. Reaching for Supports() for an alarm feature will quietly answer false forever.

docs.title: PoracleNG API Proxy
docs.text:
All alarm tracking operations (create, read, update, delete) are proxied through PoracleNG's REST API instead of writing to Poracle's MySQL database. PoracleNG then owns duplicate detection, validation and the state reload after every change.

PoracleNG 5.4.0 or newer

PoracleServerProfile.MinimumSupported is 5.4.0. Against anything older PoracleWeb.NET still runs, but the server capability probe logs an error at startup and warns an admin, and the human, profile, area, place and mute calls answer with a message naming the version they need. See Version compatibility.

docs.title: Why we migrated
docs.text:
On March 31, 2026, a NULL template column written directly by PoracleWeb.NET crashed PoracleNG's state reload for 15 hours. PoracleNG's Go SQL scanner cannot handle NULL in the template column of the monsters table, causing the entire state reload to fail. All users received stale alarm state and unwanted DM floods until PoracleNG was manually restarted.

Direct database writes bypassed everything PoracleNG does on its own write path, including filling an absent template with the configured default. Going through the API removes that class of bug. It doesn't make PoracleWeb.NET's own defaults irrelevant: PoracleNG fills only fields that are absent, and the *Create models send every field they declare (see Backend → Monster filter defaults).

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text:
Frontend (Angular)
    |
    v
ASP.NET Core Controllers  (/api/pokemon, /api/raids, etc.)
    |
    v
Alarm Services  (MonsterService, RaidService, etc.)
    |
    v
IPoracleTrackingProxy  (PoracleTrackingProxy)
    |  HTTP + X-Poracle-Secret header
    v
PoracleNG REST API  (/api/v2/humans/{id}/tracking/*)
    |
    v
MySQL (Poracle DB)  +  State Reload

docs.title: What goes through the proxy
docs.text:
All alarm tracking CRUD for these types:

Type PoracleNG tracking type Service Pokemon pokemon MonsterService Raids raid RaidService Eggs egg EggService Quests quest QuestService Invasions invasion InvasionService Lures lure LureService Nests nest NestService Gyms gym GymService Fort Changes fort FortChangeService Max Battles maxbattle MaxBattleService

There is an eleventh tracking type, Pokéstop Events (incident), and it is not in that table. It has no v1 route at all, so it goes through its own IPoracleIncidentProxy against /api/v2/humans/{id}/tracking/incident. Its rows live in the same invasion table as invasion rows, told apart only by grunt_type carrying an event name. PoracleNG's two v2 endpoints each filter to their own rows. The invasion read the application uses folds the incident rules back into the invasion list, the way v1 returned them, and InvasionService splits them out again. When the Pokéstop Events page is switched off it doesn't, so those rules stay visible on the invasion page. See Database.

Also proxied:

Operation How Dashboard counts One read of the v2 tracking snapshot (GET /api/v2/humans/{userId}/tracking), counted per type Cleaning toggle One v2 PATCH per type naming the uids and the clean bit Admin delete of all alarms Reads the uids per type and bulk-deletes them through the proxy Bulk distance One v2 PATCH per type naming the uids and the new distance. Max battles included; they're no longer deleted and re-created

docs.title: Read-only calls that shape the UI
docs.text:
PoracleNG's own config and master data are read for things other than tracking. Each read degrades to a usable default rather than failing the request:

Call Used for If it fails GET /api/masterdata/monsters?locale={code} Pokemon names, types, form names and evolution chains, translated into the display language Falls back to the English WatWowMap masterfile cached server-side, so the pickers stay populated GET /api/config/poracleWeb → disabledHooks The per-type disable flags Poracle sets in its own config, honoured here as a floor under the site settings Empty set: the local disable_* settings are in sole charge. Fails open, deliberately GET /api/config/values → general.disable_showcase Whether the Pokéstop Events page exists at all Only true hides the page; absent or unreadable leaves it on, because every supported PoracleNG serves the v2 incident route GET /api/config/values → tracking.quest_summary_enabled Whether quest summary delivery is offered Treated as off, so the control is hidden rather than saving into a delivery nothing performs

Fort changes arrive in disabledHooks as fort (jfberry/PoracleNG#197). A second read of general.disable_fort_update covered servers before 5.2.1; it is gone.

The locale on the first row is the display language, which is why switching language re-fetches the map — Poracle owns the translations, so this site does not carry Pokemon names of its own.

docs.title: Insert, update or duplicate
docs.text:
PoracleNG decides what a tracking POST does by diffing the submitted row against the ones already stored. The outcome is not obvious from the request:

Diff result Outcome No differences Duplicate. Nothing is written, reported as alreadyPresent Exactly one difference, and it is an updatable field Update of that existing row Anything else New insert

The updatable set is clean, distance and template, plus slot_changes and battle_changes on gyms. Everything else identifies the alarm. The consequence that kept biting: an Add that differs from a different alarm by exactly one updatable field takes that alarm over, and one alarm exists where there were two.

PoracleWeb.NET no longer reconstructs that rule. Since 5.4.0 PoracleNG reports what a create would do: POST ?dry_run=true classifies each row as inserted, updated or unchanged without writing, and a colliding edit comes back 409. The proxy acts on the answer:

  • A single Add the dry run calls an update is refused with "Another alarm of this type already uses those settings. Edit or remove that one instead." (TrackingConflictException, mapped to 409).
  • A single Add that is unchanged writes nothing and answers 200 with uid 0.
  • Anything else commits. If the commit itself reports a takeover (another request got there between the dry run and the write), the other alarm is restored from the previous PoracleNG returns and the Add is refused.
  • A batch (quick picks, profile import) is dry-run whole first. If every row is new it commits; if none is, it writes nothing. Only a mixed answer dry-runs each row alone, because PoracleNG classifies the batch against stored rules and can't say which row was which. Then only the new rows are created, and identical rows and would-be takeovers are skipped.
  • Max battles get the same protection. 5.4.0 merges max battles on v2 creates, so an Add of the same boss differing only by radius is refused where v1 used to stack it.
sequenceDiagram
    participant SPA
    participant API as PoracleWeb.NET
    participant NG as PoracleNG
    SPA->>API: POST /api/{type}
    API->>API: translate to a V2 rule, refuse if it can't be expressed
    API->>API: IUserAreaPolicy checks override_areas, sets trusted
    API->>NG: POST .../tracking/{type}?silent=true&dry_run=true
    NG-->>API: created, updated, unchanged
    alt updated, it would take over another rule
        API-->>SPA: 409 takeover message
    else unchanged
        API-->>SPA: 200, uid 0, nothing written
    else created
        API->>NG: the same POST without dry_run
        NG-->>API: created, or updated with previous
        opt a race turned it into a takeover
            API->>NG: PUT .../tracking/{type}/{uid}?trusted=true restores previous
            API-->>SPA: 409
        end
        API-->>SPA: 201 with the uid
    end

The ... is /api/v2/humans/{id}. Pokemon has one quirk here: an Add that differs from an existing rule only in its clean setting comes back as already tracked (200, uid 0) and changes nothing, so a clean-only change has to be made by editing that rule.

No client-side takeover check is left. Bulk distance sends a PATCH, and PoracleNG refuses a rule whose new radius would make it clash with another, naming it as a conflict. TrackingFieldPreserver still merges the stored row into an edit, because a v2 PUT is a full replace; see Backend → Update pattern.

docs.title: The v2 write path
docs.text:
PoracleNG 5.2.0 added a second tracking surface at /api/v2 and left v1 frozen. Every read, create, edit and delete for all eleven types now goes through it. Bulk distance and the cleaning toggle use v2's PATCH /api/v2/humans/{id}/tracking/{type} with {uids, set}: one request per type, the one setting named, every rule keeping its uid. PoracleNG answers per rule, so a rule it refuses (conflict, invalid, not_found) doesn't fail the rest; conflicts come back to the SPA as skippedConflict. No v1 tracking call remains.

Every PATCH is sent ?trusted=true. PoracleNG re-validates the whole stored rule on a PATCH, and untrusted its area check allows only userSelectable fences, so a rule limited to the user's own drawn fence came back invalid and kept its old setting. Trusting the PATCH grants nothing new: its set has no override_areas, so the only areas re-checked are the ones already on the rule.

Pokéstop Events have their own proxy (PoracleIncidentProxy), whose only surface is v2. Invasion rules go to the invasion routes, except the event grunts (kecleon, gold-stop, showcase), which are saved from the invasion page to the incident routes. The steel grunt used to be saved as metal, which matched nothing on v1 and which v2 refuses; it is steel now, and a stored metal rule is saved as steel on its next edit.

Reads and deletes go through v2. TrackingV2Translator.ToV1Row rebuilds the v1 row from a v2 rule: enums back to integers, booleans to 0/1, the three clean booleans to the CleanFlags bitmask, and every null to a default from DefaultsFor, which follows PoracleNG's own read translation where it differs from ours (fort include_empty null is 1, raid and max battle level null is 9000 with a pokemon and 90 without). A property the table doesn't know is carried through, so a field PoracleNG's own /openapi.json declares that PoracleWeb.NET doesn't model (a personal-shiny flag, say) isn't dropped, and an edit sends it back. The whole-profile reads use the v2 snapshot; the all-profiles read adds the active profile's rules itself when that profile has no profiles row, since PoracleNG only lists profiles that have one. Pokéstop event rules come from incident and are folded into the invasion list as v1 returned them. Deletes use the uid route, a {uids} body for bulk; a uid on a profile other than the active one is looked up with one all-profiles read and deleted with ?profile=N, and an invasion delete retries leftovers as incident.

Creates run the dry-run protocol above. The uid-addressed PUT 404s when the uid is not that human's and 409s when the replacement would duplicate or take over another rule, so the server enforces what the old client-side mirror had to reconstruct.

A v2 PUT is a full replace. Omitting min_iv wipes a stored 90, verified live against 5.2.1. That makes TrackingFieldPreserver load-bearing in a stronger way than it was on v1, where PoracleNG merged.

The uid is read back on every edit. The v2 engine is delete-then-insert, then reassigns the old uid (jfberry/PoracleNG #303, in 5.4.0). A failed reassignment still answers 200 with a new uid, so the response is always read. TrackingV2Replacement.ApplyAsync calls ITrackedUidRemapper for every type but pokemon, and MonsterService does the same after its own update, but only when the uid actually moved, so quick-pick applied state follows the row rather than pointing at a uid that is gone.

Max battle edits are one PUT. v1 could only delete and recreate, which left a window where the alarm existed nowhere.

docs.title: What changes at the wire
docs.text:
TrackingV2Translator rewrites a v1-shaped row into what that type's V2*Rule accepts, once, at the proxy boundary. Everything inside PoracleWeb.NET keeps v1's shape as its single internal currency.

Each type has its own field table, never a shared one: V2PokemonRule declares 28 integer filters, V2FortRule declares one and has no clean field at all. Four kinds of field change shape:

v1 v2 clean, a 3-bit mask three booleans — clean, edit, summary 0/1 columns: exclusive, slot_changes, battle_changes, gmax, shiny, include_empty real booleans team, gender and rsvp_changes as integers string enums change_types, stored as a JSON string an array

uid, id, profile_no and description have no place in a v2 rule body — they are addressing and presentation, and v2 reconstructs all of it. Every V2*Rule sets additionalProperties: false, so one stray property is a 422 and the write fails outright.

Defaults go out as absent. A v2 rule stores nothing for a field at its wildcard, so the translator omits a property whose value equals the type's read default unless the schema marks it required. A boss-specific raid or max battle (stored level 9000) is sent without level, so boss edits no longer depend on the older API.

A row the translator can't express is refused, never sent elsewhere. A property it does not know, a gender outside 0-3, a pvp_ranking_league outside {0, 500, 1500, 2500}, an egg with no level: it raises AlarmValidationException("PoracleNG can't store this alarm as it is: {reason}. Nothing was changed."). Dropping the field silently would be the #730 field-loss bug again.

ping is a real column on every type and v2 declares it on every rule (jfberry/PoracleNG#249, in 5.4.0), so a role or user mention survives an edit. The earlier refusal for an edit that would have dropped it went with the v1 path it protected against. The SPA shows the Mention field in edit dialogs while managing a webhook, a Discord channel or a Discord thread, and nowhere else: not on Telegram destinations, which have no mention, and not on people.

docs.title: Choosing the surface
docs.text: There is no setting for it. Poracle:TrackingApiVersion and PORACLE_TRACKING_API_VERSION are gone, and a leftover value is ignored. A v2 tracking route that answers gin's plaintext 404 page not found raises PoracleUnsupportedException("saving alarms", ...), the same as the human routes.

docs.title: Reading a refusal
docs.text:
PoracleNG speaks two error dialects and PoracleProblemDetails.Describe reads both:

Surface Status Body v1 400 {"message": "...", "status": "error"} v2 422, not 400 RFC 9457 application/problem+json: {title, status, detail}, plus an errors[] array on a schema violation

Precedence is errors[] first, because a field error names the field that was refused; then detail, message, error, title. status is never used as the message: v1's is the word error and v2's is a number. Field-error locations are JSON pointers whose prefix moves with the route (body.pokemon_id on the single-object PUT, body[0].pokemon_id on the array POST), so both prefixes are trimmed. At most three are quoted, with a count of the rest. A body that is not JSON is echoed raw up to 300 characters. The fallback is "Poracle rejected the alarm."

PoracleTrackingProxy treats 422 as the caller's problem alongside 400, so a v2 validation failure surfaces as a sentence rather than an opaque 500.

A v1-shaped error reader renders blank against v2

Anything reading err.error.error is reading v1's shape and shows nothing when v2 refuses. Use PoracleProblemDetails.Describe for any new v2 call site.

docs.title: When the server is too old
docs.text:
PoracleUnsupportedException carries a feature name and what the server would need, in words, and the global PoracleUnsupportedExceptionFilter turns it into 409 Conflict with {error, feature, requires}. 409 rather than 403 because 403 is the disable_* path and keys off disableKey in the body; 409 has no interceptor branch, so the message lands beside the control that asked for it. PoracleHumanProxy and the areas and geocode calls on PoracleApiProxy throw it for a plaintext 404 from a route 5.4.0 added; a problem+json 404 keeps its ordinary meaning. See Version compatibility.

When PoracleNG cannot be reached at all, PoracleUnreachableExceptionFilter answers 503 with a message on the mute and location controllers and all eleven alarm controllers.

docs.title: What PoracleWeb.NET reads from a database
docs.text:
None of it is Poracle's.

Operation Reason poracle_web database (geofences, settings, webhook delegates, quick picks) Application-owned data, not managed by PoracleNG Scanner database (gym search, weather) Read-only, separate database

No Poracle table is read or written directly. Per-alarm override_areas go through PoracleNG with ?trusted=true after IUserAreaPolicy has authorised them (see Backend → Areas). The Database page describes the same set.

Every human and profile operation is proxied

HumanService and ProfileService read and write a single human through IPoracleHumanProxy with no DB fallback, and so do the admin-bulk operations: the full user list, the webhook list, the batch read that resolves geofence owners' names, and user deletion use GET /api/v2/humans (with ?type= and ?id=a,b,c) and DELETE /api/v2/humans/{id}. HumanRepository and ProfileRepository no longer exist. The existence check the purge runs first reads the proxy too: its human read answers null only for a 404 and throws for anything else, the same contract as GetAdminRolesAsync, so an unreachable PoracleNG is not reported to the admin as "already gone" (#994).

A new profile's areas and location are written by NewProfileGeography through POST /api/v2/humans/{id}/areas?profile=N and .../location?profile=N, because PoracleNG's add ignores both (#993). Names PoracleNG rejects are logged and dropped, create first filters the list through the same allowed-name check as the Areas page (IUserAreaWriter.FilterAllowedAsync), both duplicates send the caller's own source profile's list unfiltered, import sends none, and whatever is sent is always trusted, so the profile keeps the user's drawn fences whatever area_security is, and a refusal of either write deletes the profile just created and returns the original error, since there is no direct write left to repair it with.

Rename is PATCH /api/v2/humans/{id}/profiles/{n}, and it sends only the active_hours the caller submitted, so renaming a profile whose stored schedule v2 would refuse still works.

docs.title: Which human operations use /api/v2
docs.text:
All of them, with no fallback. A route 5.4.0 added that answers gin's plaintext 404 page not found is a PoracleUnsupportedException, not a retry on v1.

Operation Route Get human GET /v2/humans/{id} Create human POST /v2/humans Admin list / delete GET /v2/humans, DELETE /v2/humans/{id} Enable / disable POST .../enable, .../disable Admin disable POST .../admin-disable {disabled} Set location POST .../location {latitude,longitude} Switch profile POST .../profile {profile_no} Set language POST .../language List / add / move / delete saved place GET, POST .../locations, PUT, DELETE .../locations/{label} Admin roles GET .../admin-roles Save areas, toggle a fence, create POST .../areas {areas, trusted: true}, after IUserAreaWriter has checked every name (see Backend → Areas). Names PoracleNG has no fence for come back in rejected and are not an error Delete a fence DELETE .../areas?name=&all_profiles=true, preceded by a dry_run=true call that reports the alarms scoped to that fence alone. Alarms the user chose to delete go first, per profile, through the tracking bulk delete with ?profile=N Rename a fence PATCH .../areas?from=&to=&all_profiles=true&trusted=true, after a geofence reload so to is loaded Available areas GET .../areas List profiles GET .../profiles, translated back to v1's {"profile":[...]} with area and active_hours as strings Create / rename profile POST .../profiles (returns the number), PATCH .../profiles/{n} Delete profile DELETE .../profiles/{n} Copy profile POST .../profiles/{to}/copy {from_profile} A new profile's geography POST .../areas?profile=N, POST .../location?profile=N

Three things are worth knowing about how a missing route is told from a missing record:

  • The content type is the only thing separating them. gin answers a route it does not have with the plaintext 404 page not found; the v2 surface answers a missing human or place with problem+json at the same status. PoracleProblemDetails.IsProblemJson is consulted before concluding anything.
  • Every webhook id in a path goes through Uri.EscapeDataString, because the id is a URL.
  • Bodies differ from v1 in more than shape. admin-disable renames state to disabled. The location writes take latitude/longitude, matching what every read answers (jfberry/PoracleNG#303). The profile create and update bodies are translated, never forwarded: V2AddProfileBody and V2UpdateProfileBody declare name and active_hours under additionalProperties: false, and active_hours is the entry array rather than the JSON string stored here.

The profile list restates the v2 answer in v1's shape before ProfileService sees it: the wrapper key changes from profile to profiles, and active_hours and area arrive as arrays. Copy inverts its arguments (destination in the path, source as from_profile) and replaces the destination's rules, which the tests pin. Both surfaces' copy replaces, so copying from a profile with no rules empties the destination. Delete cascades the profile's rules and moves current_profile_no off a deleted active profile.

A ?profile=N write for a profile number that does not exist answers 200 and writes nothing, on both routes, so a geography write can't report "no such profile"; callers pass the number PoracleNG has just assigned.

docs.title: Calls the linked-accounts feature makes
docs.text:
Linked accounts use no route the rest of the site doesn't, and send nothing that tells PoracleNG two humans belong together. Each call goes to one human at a time.

What Calls Resolve the pair GET /v2/humans/{id} per side, cached a minute, for its type and pause state Merged alarm list, owner lookup, bulk distance The usual GET .../tracking/{type} and PATCH .../tracking/{type}, once per human Move an alarm On the target: POST .../tracking/{type}?dry_run=true, then the create. On the source: DELETE .../tracking/{type}/{uid}, tried twice. Preflight reads both humans, the target's GET .../locations and, except for Pokéstop events, the source's GET .../tracking/{type} to carry fields the typed model doesn't hold Person-level writes The same location, place, area, profile, language, mute, summary and enable/disable calls, sent to the signed-in human and then the other Drift read GET /v2/humans/{id}, GET .../areas, GET .../profiles, GET .../locations for both humans in parallel Drift resolve GET .../tracking?all_profiles=true before deleting a profile or place, then the writes for the one field: POST .../location, POST .../areas (through IUserAreaWriter), POST .../profile, POST/PATCH/DELETE .../profiles, POST .../areas?profile=N and .../location?profile=N, POST/PUT/DELETE .../locations Register the missing side POST /v2/humans, then GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE .../profiles, POST .../areas?profile=N, POST .../location?profile=N, POST .../profile, POST .../locations. A failure deletes the human with DELETE /v2/humans/{id}, only if its type and name are still the ones this link created

PoracleNG's "lowest free number" rule for new profiles is why profile creates on a pair check the number each human was given (see Linked Accounts).

docs.title: IPoracleTrackingProxy interface
docs.text:
public interface IPoracleTrackingProxy
{
    Task<JsonElement> GetByUserAsync(string type, string userId);
    Task<TrackingCreateResult> CreateAsync(string type, string userId, JsonElement body);
    Task<TrackingCreateResult> CreateOnProfileAsync(string type, string userId, JsonElement body, int profileNo);
    Task<TrackingUpdateResult> UpdateByUidAsync(string type, string userId, int uid, JsonElement body);
    Task<TrackingPatchResult> PatchAsync(string type, string userId, IReadOnlyList<int> uids, TrackingPatchSet settings);
    Task DeleteByUidAsync(string type, string userId, int uid);
    Task BulkDeleteByUidsAsync(string type, string userId, IEnumerable<int> uids);
    Task<JsonElement> GetAllTrackingAsync(string userId);
    Task<JsonElement> GetAllTrackingAllProfilesAsync(string userId);
    Task<IReadOnlyList<StoredRule>> GetStoredRulesAsync(string userId);
    Task<StoredRuleReplaceOutcome> ReplaceStoredRuleAsync(string type, string userId, int uid, int profileNo, JsonElement v1Row, bool dryRun);
    Task<IReadOnlyList<int>> BulkDeleteByUidsOnProfileAsync(string type, string userId, IReadOnlyList<int> uids, int profileNo);
    Task ReloadStateAsync();
}

Key design points:

Point Detail JsonElement throughout Alarm data flows as raw JSON. Services deserialize with JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower to map C# PascalCase models to PoracleNG's snake_case ?silent=true on create, update and delete Suppresses PoracleNG's DM confirmation. Without it on the delete routes, clearing a list DMed the user one filter dump per row removed, so a bulk delete, a cleaning reset or an admin delete-all could each send dozens X-Poracle-Secret header Authenticates every request, from Poracle:ApiSecret One update entry point UpdateByUidAsync is a v2 PUT and nothing else. Every service calls it through TrackingV2Replacement.ApplyAsync, which follows a moved uid. It returns the uid the rule now lives under, which may differ from the one that went in. See The v2 write path CreateOnProfileAsync CreateAsync with ?profile=N. Only profile import uses it, so it writes to the target profile without switching the active one GetStoredRulesAsync, ReplaceStoredRuleAsync Serve the rule repair: every rule on every profile exactly as v2 returns it, and a trusted PUT on the rule's own profile (?profile=N, optionally &dry_run=true) that skips the area policy because it restores what PoracleNG already holds BulkDeleteByUidsOnProfileAsync Deletes on a named profile, for a geofence delete that takes the alarms limited to it uid, profile_no, id, description never sent PoracleJsonHelper.SerializeToElement() strips "uid":0 and profile_no, and the translator drops all four from every rule body. profile_no matters most: PoracleNG takes a submitted one at face value while scoping reads to current_profile_no, and a stale JWT claim stamped onto writes stranded alarms that were invisible and undeletable. Without it each alarm is filed under the live active profile URL-encoded user ids PoracleTrackingProxy and PoracleHumanProxy pass user ids through Uri.EscapeDataString(). A webhook id is a full URL whose slashes would otherwise break routing

docs.title: snake_case JSON serialization
docs.text:
PoracleNG's API uses snake_case field names (pokemon_id, min_iv, max_cp). PoracleWeb.NET's C# models use PascalCase (PokemonId, MinIv, MaxCp). The shared PoracleJsonHelper class provides a centralized SnakeCaseOptions instance:

// PoracleJsonHelper.cs
public static readonly JsonSerializerOptions SnakeCaseOptions = new()
{
    PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower,
    PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true,
};

All alarm services use PoracleJsonHelper.SerializeToElement() for serialization (which also strips uid:0) and PoracleJsonHelper.DeserializeList<T>() for deserialization.

docs.title: PoracleNG response wrapper format
docs.text:
PoracleNG wraps certain responses in container objects:

Response Shape Human GET /api/v2/humans/{id} returns { "human": { ... } }; PoracleHumanProxy.GetHumanAsync() unwraps it Profiles GET /api/v2/humans/{id}/profiles returns { "profiles": [...] }, restated in v1's { "profile": [...] } shape for ProfileService Tracking GET /api/v2/humans/{id}/tracking/{type} returns the rules under a named envelope, and GET /api/v2/humans/{id}/tracking a snapshot keyed by type. The proxy restates both as v1 rows

When adding new proxy methods, check the actual PoracleNG response shape and unwrap accordingly.

docs.title: Active hours translation
docs.text:
active_hours is stored as a JSON string on the profile, and the SPA and ProfileController work with that string. v2 takes the entry array instead, under additionalProperties: false, so PoracleHumanProxy.V2ProfileBody parses the string and sends the array, and the profile list translates the array back to a string on the way in. A schedule v2 would refuse is answered with an error rather than sent. "No schedule" goes out as [], because v2 reads an omitted active_hours as "leave it as it is".

PoracleNG's profile scheduler evaluates these rules; PoracleWeb.NET validates, displays and edits them.

docs.title: Known gaps and workarounds
docs.text:
These operations lack dedicated PoracleNG endpoints and use workarounds:

Operation Workaround Impact Dashboard counts One read of the v2 tracking snapshot Returns full alarm payloads just to count them Admin delete all alarms Fetch UIDs per type, bulk delete each Multiple API calls instead of one

See PoracleNG Enhancement Requests for the full gap analysis and proposed endpoints.

docs.title: How to add a new alarm type
docs.text:
1. Add a service following MonsterService.cs: inject IPoracleTrackingProxy and IFeatureGate, define the TrackingType constant (PoracleNG's tracking type name), call EnsureEnabledAsync at the top of CreateAsync, BulkCreateAsync and UpdateAsync, and send edits through TrackingV2Replacement.ApplyAsync.
  2. Add the type's field table to TrackingV2Translator.Specs, listing exactly the properties its V2*Rule declares, and its read defaults (what DefaultsFor returns for a null). TrackingV2TypeTranslationTests checks the table against the schema in both directions.
  3. Add the *Create and *Update DTOs with validation attributes and defaults that match what the column stores for "no filter" (see Backend → Monster filter defaults), and their AlarmMappingExtensions.
  4. Add a DisableFeatureKeys constant and its ByTrackingType entry, then the controller under Controllers/ with [RequireFeatureEnabled(...)] and [TypeFilter(typeof(PoracleUnreachableExceptionFilter))] on the class.
  5. Register the service in ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs.
  6. In the SPA, add the route with a disabledFeatureGuard, the nav item with the same disableKey, and the toggle in the admin settings. Add the key to SettingsMigrationService too.

No repository or entity is needed for an alarm type. PoracleNG stores the rules.

docs.title: Registration
docs.text:
// In ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs
services.AddHttpClient<IPoracleTrackingProxy, PoracleTrackingProxy>();

services.AddHttpClient<IPoracleIncidentProxy, PoracleIncidentProxy>();
services.AddHttpClient<IPoracleHumanProxy, PoracleHumanProxy>();
services.AddHttpClient<IPoracleSummaryProxy, PoracleSummaryProxy>();
services.AddHttpClient<IPoracleMuteProxy, PoracleMuteProxy>();
services.AddHttpClient<IPoracleApiProxy, PoracleApiProxy>();

There are six Poracle proxies. Tracking, incident, human and mute speak /api/v2. Summary covers the quest summary schedule. IPoracleApiProxy covers everything else: config and config values, templates, masterdata, geofence maps, hashes and reload, test alerts (/api/test, plus the note after one through /api/deliverMessages), and geocoding through /api/geocode.

The HttpClient instances are managed by the .NET HTTP client factory, providing connection pooling and DNS rotation.

docs.title: Override areas are authorised in the proxy
docs.text: PoracleTrackingProxy is registered undecorated. When a create or an edit names override_areas, it checks the scope (OverrideScope: a place and a set of areas cannot both be set, areas cannot coexist with a radius, a place needs one), asks IUserAreaPolicy to authorise each name, and sends the write with ?trusted=true. A write that names no override area sends no flag. Nothing is written to PoracleNG's database.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text: PoracleWeb.NET ships docker-compose.yml.example as a template — copy it to docker-compose.yml on first install (cp docker-compose.yml.example docker-compose.yml). The compose file loads all user-configurable values from .env via env_file, so it rarely needs local edits. The .env file itself is the same format used by standalone mode — see the Configuration Reference for the full list of settings.

docs.title: Container settings
docs.text: Setting Value Port mapping Host ${PORT:-8082} → Container 8080. Set PORT in .env to change. Volumes ./data for avatar/DTS cache persistence, Poracle config directory (read-only) Health check HTTP check every 30s with 15s startup grace period Resource limits 2 CPUs, 2GB memory Logging JSON file driver, 10MB max per file, 3 file rotation Restart policy unless-stopped

docs.title: Example docker-compose.yml
docs.text:
services:
  poracleweb.net:
    image: ghcr.io/pgan-dev/poracleweb.net:latest
    ports:
      - "${PORT:-8082}:8080"
    env_file:
      - .env
    environment:
      # Container-side paths only; everything else is loaded from .env.
      # JWT issuer/audience default to "PoracleWeb" / "PoracleWeb.App" via Program.cs —
      # override by setting JWT_ISSUER / JWT_AUDIENCE in .env if needed.
      - DTS_SOURCE_DIR=/poracle-config
      - DATA_DIR=/app/data
    volumes:
      - ./data:/app/data
      - ${PORACLE_CONFIG_DIR:-./data}:/poracle-config:ro
    restart: unless-stopped

docs.title: Network requirements
docs.text:
Inside your own network, the PoracleWeb.NET container must be able to reach:

Service Why PoracleNG API (Poracle:ApiAddress) Every human, profile, area and alarm call goes through it. On the same Docker network, use the service name (e.g. http://poracleng:3030); otherwise the host IP or domain MySQL The poracle_web database. PoracleWeb.NET doesn't connect to Poracle's Golbat API (Golbat:ApiAddress) Optional. Turns on the Pokemon availability indicators Scanner database (ConnectionStrings:ScannerDb) Optional. Backs the gym picker in the raid, gym and egg dialogs and the dashboard weather panel; without it both are absent Koji (Koji:ApiAddress) Admin geofences and region lookups (see below)

Koji is required for admin geofences and region lookups. A user can still draw and use a private custom geofence without it: if Koji is unreachable the feed still serves user geofences from the local database, but approving one to a public area, and the region auto-detection on the draw page, both need Koji.

Outbound to the internet:

  • discordapp.com and cdn.discordapp.com, for Discord OAuth sign-in, role lookups, avatars, and the geofence review forum posts. Unavoidable if Discord login is enabled.
  • raw.githubusercontent.com (Masterfile-Generator), for the game master data behind the move and item pickers, fetched on the first request after a cold start and cached in memory. Pokemon names, types and forms come from Poracle instead, so they are translated and need no outbound call; this remains their fallback when Poracle cannot serve them. Not switchable; without it the pickers fall back to whatever is already cached. The browser makes no request of its own here -- everything is proxied through the API.
  • api.github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com, for the version check behind the Versions card on Admin > Server settings. Two anonymous GETs, made when an admin opens the card and cached six hours afterwards, nothing sent. On a locked-down egress policy it fails silently and the card cannot tell you whether an update exists. Turn it off with the disable_update_check site setting.

docs.title: Data directory
docs.text:
Mounted at DATA_DIR (/app/data in the image). It persists:

  • DataProtection keys. These encrypt the stored OIDC refresh tokens, so losing them signs every SSO user out on the next container recreate.
  • Cached avatars (Discord, and Telegram profile photos)
  • Cached DTS template files

See Paths for the environment variables behind these.

The container runs as appuser, uid and gid 999. Docker creates a bind-mounted ./data that doesn't exist yet as root, and the app then can't write to it: the keys live in memory only, and the log starts with DATA_DIR /app/data is not writable. Create the directory with the right owner before the first start, or fix an existing one:

mkdir -p data && sudo chown -R 999:999 data

./scripts/docker.sh start creates the directory and warns when its owner is wrong.

docs.title: Poracle config directory
docs.text:
Mount your PoracleNG config/ directory as read-only for DTS template preview functionality:

volumes:
  - /path/to/PoracleNG/config:/poracle-config:ro

docs.title: Building locally
docs.text:
Using the convenience script:

./scripts/docker.sh build     # Build from source
./scripts/docker.sh start     # Start the container
./scripts/docker.sh update    # Rebuild and recreate
./scripts/docker.sh clean     # Force rebuild (no cache)
./scripts/docker.sh logs      # Tail logs
./scripts/docker.sh stop      # Stop the container

Or with raw Docker commands:

docker build -t poracleweb.net:latest .
docker compose up -d
docker compose up -d --force-recreate
docker build --no-cache -t poracleweb.net:latest .

Building from source builds whatever is checked out

These commands build your working tree. On a fresh clone that is main, which tracks releases; on develop it is unreleased work. Check out a release tag first (git checkout "$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)"), or skip the build entirely and use the published ghcr.io/pgan-dev/poracleweb.net:latest image, which only moves when a release is published.

docs.title: External SSO / OpenID Connect Login
docs.text:
PoracleWeb.NET can delegate login to a generic external OAuth2 / OpenID Connect provider, so users sign in with your own identity provider instead of (or alongside) Discord and Telegram. This page is the provider-agnostic guide to configuring that login flow.

Provider-agnostic — PogoAlerts is just the reference

The SSO flow is a configurable twin of the Discord OAuth flow, parameterized entirely by OIDC_* config. PogoAlerts (PGAN's identity provider) is one instance, but nothing in the flow is special to it — it rests only on spec-standard OAuth2/OIDC (/authorize, /token, /userinfo, plus optional /end-session). It works with any compliant provider: Keycloak, Authentik, Auth0, Google, Azure AD / Entra, Okta, and more.

You can ignore OIDC entirely — it is off by default and the sign-in page stays in Local mode (Discord / Telegram). Turn it on only when you want to point PoracleWeb.NET at a provider.

The one inherent constraint

The identity claim returned by your provider's userinfo endpoint must resolve to an existing Poracle human id — i.e. a Discord or Telegram id that already exists in your Poracle database. PoracleWeb.NET does not provision new users from SSO; it authenticates existing Poracle users through your provider. If the claim doesn't match a registered human, login fails with user_not_registered. Set OIDC_IDENTITY_CLAIM to the userinfo claim that carries that id (it falls back to the standard sub claim when the configured claim is absent). If your provider carries a Telegram id as well, set OIDC_SECONDARY_IDENTITY_CLAIM to it: a member with no Discord login, or whose Discord id isn't registered, then signs in as their Telegram human. The Discord guild-role gate (enable_roles) applies to Discord ids only, as it does for the Telegram login widget.

Silent session renewal and refresh-token handling are documented separately on the OIDC Refresh Tokens page — this page covers the login itself.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The flow is the standard OAuth2 authorization-code grant (with PKCE by default):

sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser
  participant P as PoracleWeb.NET API
  participant I as Provider (IdP)
  B->>P: GET /api/auth/oidc/login
  P->>B: 302 to provider authorize (state cookie, PKCE S256)
  B->>I: authorize → sign in / consent
  I->>B: 302 /api/auth/oidc/callback?code&state
  B->>P: callback(code, state)
  P->>P: validate state (CSRF) + PKCE verifier
  P->>I: POST /token (grant=authorization_code)
  I-->>P: { access_token, ... }
  P->>I: GET /userinfo (Bearer access_token)
  I-->>P: { identity claim, username, avatar }
  P->>P: resolve human → check enabled + roles + enable_oidc gate
  P->>B: 302 /auth/oidc/callback#token=JWT
  • CSRF. A random state value is stored in an HttpOnly cookie and verified on callback.
  • PKCE. When OIDC_USE_PKCE=true (default), a code verifier is stored in an HttpOnly cookie and only the S256 challenge is sent to the provider.
  • Redirect URI. PoracleWeb.NET always uses {your-host}/api/auth/oidc/callback. Register exactly this URI at your provider. {your-host} comes from the incoming request unless PUBLIC_URL is set, in which case it is that value — worth setting behind a reverse proxy, where the app otherwise sees plain HTTP and sends an http:// redirect URI the provider will refuse.
  • Identity resolution. The identity claim is looked up against Poracle's humans first, then OIDC_SECONDARY_IDENTITY_CLAIM when the first is absent or names nobody registered, then sub when neither claim is present. The provider authenticates; Poracle authorizes.
  • JWT type claim. Successful logins mint PoracleWeb.NET's internal JWT with the type claim taken from the matched Poracle row (telegram:user for a Telegram id). OIDC_IDENTITY_TYPE (default discord:user) is used only for a row that has no type of its own.

docs.title: Step-by-step setup
docs.text:
1. Register a client at your identity provider. Create an OAuth2 / OIDC application and set its redirect (callback) URI to:
{your-host}/api/auth/oidc/callback

for example https://poracle.example.com/api/auth/oidc/callback. Note the client id and client secret. Enable PKCE if your provider supports it (recommended).

  1. Configure the OIDC_* variables in your .env (see the reference table). At minimum you need the three endpoint URLs, the client id, the client secret, and — unless your provider's sub claim already holds the Poracle id — OIDC_IDENTITY_CLAIM. Restart PoracleWeb.NET so the server config takes effect.

  2. Switch the sign-in mode to SSO. In Admin → Server settings → Authentication, flip the Local ⇄ SSO segmented switch to SSO. This is the runtime opt-in (enable_oidc=true) and is gated on OIDC being fully configured plus a confirmation dialog. See Auth mode below.

Verify before flipping the switch

OIDC_ENABLED is auto-inferred true when OIDC_CLIENT_ID and the three URLs (OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_URL, OIDC_TOKEN_URL, OIDC_USERINFO_URL) are all set — you don't have to set it explicitly. The admin Authentication panel shows a read-only OIDC config card (from /api/settings/oidc-config, with secrets masked) so you can confirm the server picked up your config before switching everyone to SSO.

docs.title: Login configuration reference
docs.text:
All variables are read from .env (or the Oidc__* .NET convention) and require a restart to take effect. The provider secret is never stored in the database and is only ever returned masked.

.env name .NET env variable Default Description OIDC_ENABLED Oidc__Enabled (auto-inferred true when OIDC_CLIENT_ID + the three URLs are set) Master switch from server config. When false the provider is hidden regardless of other values. OIDC_PROVIDER_NAME Oidc__ProviderName "" Display name shown on the login button, e.g. PogoAlerts. OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_URL Oidc__AuthorizationUrl "" Browser-facing authorize endpoint. Any existing query string is preserved (e.g. a ?hide=… filter, or Google's ?access_type=offline). OIDC_TOKEN_URL Oidc__TokenUrl "" Token endpoint that exchanges the authorization code for tokens. OIDC_USERINFO_URL Oidc__UserInfoUrl "" Userinfo endpoint returning the user's claims. OIDC_END_SESSION_URL Oidc__EndSessionUrl "" Optional. RP-initiated end-session endpoint. When set, enables OIDC single logout (SLO) — see Single logout. OIDC_CLIENT_ID Oidc__ClientId "" OAuth2 client id. OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET Oidc__ClientSecret "" OAuth2 client secret. Never stored in the database; returned masked by the admin config endpoint. OIDC_SCOPES Oidc__Scopes openid profile email Space-delimited OAuth scopes requested at authorization time. OIDC_IDENTITY_CLAIM Oidc__IdentityClaim discord_id Userinfo claim whose value is the user's Poracle human id (a Discord/Telegram id). Falls back to sub when neither identity claim is present. Must resolve to an existing human — see the inherent constraint. OIDC_SECONDARY_IDENTITY_CLAIM Oidc__SecondaryIdentityClaim "" Optional. A second userinfo claim holding a Poracle human id, tried when OIDC_IDENTITY_CLAIM is absent or names nobody registered. Set it to the provider's Telegram id claim (telegram_id on PogoAlerts) so a member with only a Telegram login signs in as their telegram:user human. OIDC_USERNAME_CLAIM Oidc__UsernameClaim preferred_username Userinfo claim used as the display username. OIDC_AVATAR_CLAIM Oidc__AvatarClaim picture Userinfo claim used as the avatar URL. OIDC_IDENTITY_TYPE Oidc__IdentityType discord:user JWT type claim for an SSO login whose Poracle row has no discord:user/telegram:user type of its own. A row that has one wins. OIDC_USE_PKCE Oidc__UsePkce true Use PKCE (S256) for the authorization-code exchange. Recommended. AUTH_FORCE_LOCAL Auth__ForceLocal false Break-glass. Forces the local login page regardless of SSO mode — see Break-glass.

The refresh-token variables (OIDC_USE_REFRESH_TOKENS, OIDC_ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES, OIDC_OFFLINE_ACCESS_SCOPE, OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH_METHOD, …) are documented on the OIDC Refresh Tokens page. See also the full Configuration Reference.

docs.title: Auth mode (Local vs SSO)
docs.text:
The admin Authentication panel exposes a single segmented Local ⇄ SSO switch backed by the one runtime site setting enable_oidc:

enable_oidc Sign-in mode absent / false Local — Discord / Telegram (the default; SSO is opt-in). true SSO — the login page auto-redirects to your OIDC provider.
  • OIDC is opt-in. Unlike Discord/Telegram (where an absent setting means enabled), SSO is only active when enable_oidc is explicitly true. The default sign-in mode is always Local.
  • Switching to SSO is gated on OIDC being fully configured and a confirmation dialog, to prevent locking yourself out against a misconfigured provider.
  • In SSO mode the Discord and Telegram sections of the Authentication panel are hidden, replaced by the read-only OIDC config card (from /api/settings/oidc-config, secrets masked), the single-logout toggle (when an end-session URL is set), and the silent-refresh toggle (when refresh is configured — see the refresh page).

Admins can always reach the login page

Even when enable_oidc=false, the enable_oidc gate is not an early block — it is enforced only after the user is identified, and admins bypass it. This means an admin can always sign in (via any configured method) to re-enable the setting, exactly like the Discord/Telegram gates.

docs.title: Login page behavior
docs.text:
• When SSO is active, the login page auto-redirects to your provider so users aren't shown an unnecessary intermediate screen.
  • /login?loggedout=1 shows a "Signed out" panel and suppresses the auto-redirect, so a user who just logged out isn't immediately re-logged-in. The single-logout flow redirects here.
  • The /api/auth/providers endpoint drives the login UI. Its oidc block reports: configured, enabledByAdmin, providerName, endSession (whether SLO is available), and refresh (whether silent refresh is wired up).

docs.title: Single logout (SLO)
docs.text:
When OIDC_END_SESSION_URL is set, signing out can also end the user's session at the provider (RP-initiated logout), not just locally. GET /api/auth/oidc/logout bounces the browser to the provider's end-session endpoint with a post_logout_redirect_uri of {origin}/login?loggedout=1, then returns to the signed-out panel.

Single logout requires both:

  1. OIDC_END_SESSION_URL configured, and
  2. the runtime toggle enable_oidc_slo not set to false (absent = on once the URL is wired).

If either is missing, logout falls back to local-only — PoracleWeb.NET clears its own session but the provider session survives.

docs.title: Break-glass (AUTH_FORCE_LOCAL)
docs.text:
AUTH_FORCE_LOCAL=true (Auth__ForceLocal) forces the local login page regardless of the SSO mode. It is a recovery mechanism: if an admin switches to SSO against a provider that is down or misconfigured and everyone is locked out, set this env flag and restart to get the local Discord / Telegram login back without touching the database.

It overrides enable_oidc for the /api/auth/providers response (OIDC reports enabledByAdmin=false while it is set). The admin OIDC config card surfaces a forceLocal flag so the UI can explain why OIDC appears inactive even when enabled.

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text:
On any failure the browser is redirected to /login#error=CODE. The login page maps these to a message.

CODE Meaning oidc_disabled OIDC is not configured at all, or a non-admin user attempted SSO while enable_oidc=false. oidc_token_exchange_failed The /token code exchange failed (bad client secret, wrong redirect URI, expired code, auth-method mismatch). oidc_userinfo_failed The /userinfo call failed or returned no usable body. oidc_no_identity None of OIDC_IDENTITY_CLAIM, OIDC_SECONDARY_IDENTITY_CLAIM (when set) or the fallback sub claim was present in userinfo. user_not_registered The identity claim resolved, but no matching Poracle human exists. Register the user in Poracle first (the inherent constraint). not_in_guild Role gating reused from the Discord path: the (Discord) user isn't in the configured guild. missing_required_role Role gating: the user has none of the allowed roles. role_check_failed Role gating: the role check itself errored, or allowed_role_ids is set but holds no usable role IDs.

The not_in_guild / missing_required_role / role_check_failed codes only apply when role-based access (enable_roles) is configured and the identity is a Discord id — they are shared verbatim with the Discord login path.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Method & path Purpose GET /api/auth/oidc/login Begins the flow; 302s to the provider's authorize endpoint. 404s when OIDC isn't configured. GET /api/auth/oidc/callback Handles the provider redirect: validates state + PKCE, exchanges the code, fetches userinfo, mints the JWT. GET /api/auth/oidc/logout RP-initiated end-session (single logout) when configured + enabled; otherwise redirects to the signed-out panel. GET /api/auth/providers Returns provider availability for the login page, including the oidc block (configured, enabledByAdmin, providerName, endSession, refresh). GET /api/settings/oidc-config Admin-only. Read-only server-side OIDC config for the admin panel; secrets masked.

POST /api/auth/oidc/refresh and /refresh/revoke belong to the silent-renewal feature — see the OIDC Refresh Tokens page.

docs.title: Provider matrix
docs.text:
For login, the per-provider differences come down to the identity claim. (If you also enable refresh tokens, the token-endpoint auth method and offline-access scope also matter — those columns are included for convenience.)

Provider OIDC_IDENTITY_CLAIM OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH_METHOD † OIDC_OFFLINE_ACCESS_SCOPE † PogoAlerts discord_id client_secret_post offline_access Keycloak sub client_secret_basic offline_access Authentik sub client_secret_post offline_access Auth0 sub client_secret_post offline_access Google sub client_secret_post (empty — append ?access_type=offline to the authorize URL) Azure AD / Entra sub or oid client_secret_post offline_access Okta sub client_secret_basic offline_access

† Only relevant if you also enable refresh tokens. For plain login, these are ignored.

Copy-paste login snippets for the most common providers (replace the example URLs with your provider's actual endpoints):

docs.title: Keycloak
docs.text:
OIDC_PROVIDER_NAME=Keycloak
OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_URL=https://kc.example.com/realms/poracle/protocol/openid-connect/auth
OIDC_TOKEN_URL=https://kc.example.com/realms/poracle/protocol/openid-connect/token
OIDC_USERINFO_URL=https://kc.example.com/realms/poracle/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo
OIDC_END_SESSION_URL=https://kc.example.com/realms/poracle/protocol/openid-connect/logout
OIDC_CLIENT_ID=poracleweb
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=your_client_secret
OIDC_SCOPES=openid profile email
OIDC_IDENTITY_CLAIM=sub
OIDC_USE_PKCE=true

Mapping sub to a Poracle id

For providers like Keycloak that key on sub, the user's sub must equal their Poracle human id (their Discord/Telegram id). Configure your provider to expose the Discord/Telegram id as the subject — or as a custom claim and point OIDC_IDENTITY_CLAIM at it — otherwise login resolves to a non-existent user and fails with user_not_registered.

docs.title: Auth0
docs.text:
OIDC_PROVIDER_NAME=Auth0
OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_URL=https://your-tenant.us.auth0.com/authorize
OIDC_TOKEN_URL=https://your-tenant.us.auth0.com/oauth/token
OIDC_USERINFO_URL=https://your-tenant.us.auth0.com/userinfo
OIDC_END_SESSION_URL=https://your-tenant.us.auth0.com/oidc/logout
OIDC_CLIENT_ID=your_client_id
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=your_client_secret
OIDC_SCOPES=openid profile email
OIDC_IDENTITY_CLAIM=sub
OIDC_USE_PKCE=true

For Google, Azure AD / Entra, and Okta, use the same shape — set the three endpoint URLs and the identity claim from the matrix above. Google needs ?access_type=offline appended to OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_URL only if you go on to enable refresh tokens.

docs.title: Next: silent session renewal
docs.text:
By default PoracleWeb.NET mints a short-lived internal JWT and discards the provider's tokens at login. To keep sessions alive in the background and propagate provider-side disable/logout to PoracleWeb.NET, enable refresh-token consumption:

➡️ OIDC Refresh Tokens — opt-in silent renewal, revocation propagation, the provider config matrix for refresh, and the security model.

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• Configuration Reference — the full OIDC_* variable list and every other env var.
  • Site Settings — the enable_oidc and enable_oidc_slo runtime toggles.
  • Discord OAuth — the login flow SSO mirrors, and the source of the reused role-gating error codes.

docs.title: OIDC Refresh Tokens
docs.text:
PoracleWeb.NET can log users in through External SSO / OIDC — a generic external OIDC / OAuth2 provider. Once that login is working, it mints its own short-lived internal session token (a JWT) and, by default, discards the provider's access and refresh tokens.

This page documents an opt-in feature that makes PoracleWeb.NET consume the provider's refresh token so it can:

  • keep sessions alive without a hard 24-hour re-login (silent renewal in the background),
  • propagate provider-side revocation: when an admin disables the user (or they "log out everywhere") at the identity provider, PoracleWeb.NET drops the session at the next refresh, and
  • re-validate the user on every refresh, so disabling a user takes effect within roughly one access-token lifetime (~30 minutes).

Default OFF and provider-agnostic

This feature is disabled by default (OIDC_USE_REFRESH_TOKENS=false). When off, behavior is byte-for-byte identical to today: the provider's tokens are discarded and the internal JWT lives its full lifetime. PogoAlerts is only the reference provider — the mechanism rests only on spec-standard OAuth2/OIDC (/token with grant_type=refresh_token, /userinfo, and expires_in) and works with any compliant provider (Keycloak, Authentik, Auth0, Google, Azure AD / Entra, Okta, …). See For any OIDC provider below.

Prerequisite: configure External SSO / OIDC login first

Refresh tokens are an optional layer on top of a working OIDC login — they add silent session renewal and provider-side revocation propagation, but they do not set up login by themselves. Configure base External SSO / OIDC first (provider URLs, client id/secret, identity claim, PKCE, the enable_oidc auth-mode switch, single logout) on the External SSO (OIDC) page, confirm users can sign in, then opt into refresh tokens here.

docs.title: When to enable it
docs.text:
Enable it when all of the following hold:

  • You authenticate via an external OIDC provider (OIDC_ENABLED=true and the provider configured).
  • Your provider issues refresh tokens. Most providers only do this when the offline_access scope is requested (handled automatically — see below). Google uses a non-standard access_type=offline instead.
  • You want sessions that renew in the background and/or want provider-side disable/logout to terminate PoracleWeb.NET sessions promptly.

docs.title: When NOT to enable it
docs.text:
• You log in with Discord, Telegram, or local accounts only — those flows have no provider refresh token and this feature does nothing for them (they stay on the existing path).
  • Your provider cannot issue refresh tokens. If you turn the flag on but the provider returns no refresh token, PoracleWeb.NET gracefully falls back to the normal 24-hour JWT for that login and logs LogOidcRefreshUnavailable so you can see why. Nothing breaks — the feature simply no-ops.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text:
All variables are optional and default-safe. Add them to your .env (or use the Oidc__* .NET convention). They take effect only when OIDC_USE_REFRESH_TOKENS=true.

.env name .NET env variable Default Description OIDC_USE_REFRESH_TOKENS Oidc__UseRefreshTokens false Master opt-in. When off, the provider's tokens are discarded and the internal JWT lives its full lifetime (24h). When on, refresh-backed OIDC sessions are created (if the provider issues a refresh token). OIDC_ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES Oidc__AccessTokenMinutes 30 Internal JWT lifetime (minutes) for refresh-backed OIDC sessions only. Kept short so a disable/revocation at the provider propagates within ~one access-token lifetime. Other logins are unaffected. OIDC_REFRESH_TOKEN_LIFETIME_DAYS Oidc__RefreshTokenLifetimeDays 30 PoracleWeb.NET-side absolute cap (days) on a refresh session/family before a real re-login is forced. Independent of the provider's own refresh-token lifetime; if the provider's token expires first, the refresh call fails and the session is revoked. OIDC_SESSION_REVOKED_RETENTION_DAYS Oidc__RevokedRetentionDays 2 How long a revoked/rotated oidc_sessions row is kept (so a replayed old token is still detected and family-revoked) before the 6-hourly cleanup deletes it. Kept short and separate from the session cap so frequent rotation doesn't accumulate weeks of dead rows. Expired rows are deleted regardless. OIDC_OFFLINE_ACCESS_SCOPE Oidc__OfflineAccessScope offline_access Scope appended to the authorize request (only when UseRefreshTokens is on and the scope isn't already in OIDC_SCOPES) so a standards-compliant provider issues a refresh token (this includes PogoAlerts). Set empty only for providers that issue refresh tokens unconditionally regardless of scope, or that use a non-standard mechanism (e.g. Google's access_type=offline). OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH_METHOD Oidc__TokenEndpointAuthMethod client_secret_post How client credentials are presented at the token endpoint: client_secret_post (credentials in the form body — PogoAlerts, Authentik, Auth0, Google, Azure AD) or client_secret_basic (HTTP Basic header — Keycloak, Okta). Applies to both the code exchange and the refresh grant.

docs.title: Relationship to the existing OIDC_* variables
docs.text: These variables extend the base External SSO / OIDC login configuration — see External SSO (OIDC) for the provider URLs, client id/secret, identity claim, scopes, and PKCE. The refresh feature reuses the same token and userinfo endpoints — no new endpoints need to be configured on the provider side beyond enabling refresh tokens. The identity claim (OIDC_IDENTITY_CLAIM, falls back to sub) is re-read on every refresh to re-validate the user.

docs.title: Relationship to the enable_oidc site settings
docs.text:
Two runtime site settings gate OIDC behavior independently of the env vars:

Site setting Effect enable_oidc Runtime on/off for the OIDC login button. The env OIDC_ENABLED is the hard master switch; this toggle disables it at runtime without a restart. enable_oidc_slo Runtime toggle for OIDC single-logout (RP-initiated end-session).

Refresh-token consumption has no runtime site setting — it is controlled solely by the OIDC_USE_REFRESH_TOKENS env flag. Refresh is coupled to the per-login JWT lifetime, so it's a deploy-time decision (disabling it at runtime would strand the short-lived tokens of users who are already signed in; single logout, by contrast, only affects the next logout, so it stays a runtime toggle).

The /api/auth/providers response exposes a read-only oidc.refresh boolean (= OIDC is configured AND OIDC_USE_REFRESH_TOKENS is on) so the frontend knows whether silent refresh is active.

docs.title: Per-login JWT lifetime
docs.text:
PoracleWeb.NET's internal JWT lifetime (Jwt__ExpirationMinutes, default 1440 = 24h) is a global setting today. This feature introduces a per-login lifetime so the two session models can coexist:

Login type Internal JWT lifetime OIDC with an issued refresh token (refresh-backed session) OIDC_ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES (default 30 min) Discord / Telegram / local unchanged — 1440 min (24h) OIDC without a refresh token (provider issued none) unchanged — 1440 min (24h)

docs.title: Why short JWTs only for refresh-backed sessions
docs.text: A blanket cut of the global JWT lifetime to 30 minutes would log out Discord/Telegram/local users every 30 minutes, because their flows have no way to silently renew. Only refresh-backed OIDC sessions can renew in the background, so only those get the short lifetime. The short lifetime is what makes revocation propagation prompt: a disabled user keeps a valid PoracleWeb.NET session for at most one access-token lifetime (~30 min) before the next refresh re-validates them and fails.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
PoracleWeb.NET never sends the provider's refresh token to the browser. The browser holds an opaque PoracleWeb.NET-minted token (in localStorage as poracle_refresh_token) that keys a server-side oidc_sessions row. That row's EncryptedRefreshToken column holds the real provider refresh token, encrypted at rest via ASP.NET Core DataProtection. One family (FamilyId) is one login session and one rotation chain.

 Browser (localStorage:                 PoracleWeb.NET API                 Provider (IdP)
   poracle_token = short JWT            /api/auth/oidc/callback            /token
   poracle_refresh_token = opaque)      /api/auth/oidc/refresh   ───────▶   grant=authorization_code
        │  proactive ~60s before exp    /api/auth/oidc/refresh/revoke      grant=refresh_token
        │  or reactive 401              /api/auth/oidc/logout              /userinfo
        ▼                                      │
   oidcRefreshInterceptor ──────────────▶  OidcRefreshService ──┐
                                               │                 │   ┌──────────────────────────┐
                                               ▼                 └──▶│ oidc_sessions (poracle_   │
                                          OidcSessionRepository      │ web): SHA-256 hash,        │
                                          (atomic rotate / revoke)   │ FamilyId chain,            │
                                                                     │ EncryptedRefreshToken      │
                                          OidcSessionCleanupService  │ (DataProtection)           │
                                          (~6h set-based DELETE)     └──────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Login and refresh-token issuance
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser
  participant P as PoracleWeb.NET API
  participant I as Provider (IdP)
  B->>P: GET /api/auth/oidc/login
  P->>B: 302 to provider authorize (PKCE, offline_access if enabled)
  B->>I: authorize → consent
  I->>B: 302 /api/auth/oidc/callback?code
  B->>P: callback(code)
  P->>I: POST /token (grant=authorization_code)
  I-->>P: { access_token, refresh_token, expires_in }
  P->>I: GET /userinfo (Bearer access_token)
  I-->>P: { identity claim, username, ... }
  P->>P: validate human exists + enabled + roles
  alt UseRefreshTokens AND refresh_token present
    P->>P: encrypt(refresh_token), INSERT oidc_sessions (new family)
    P->>P: mint JWT (OIDC_ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES ≈ 30m)
    P->>B: 302 /auth/oidc/callback#token=JWT&refresh_token=OPAQUE
  else flag off OR no refresh_token returned
    P->>P: mint JWT (24h), graceful fallback, logs if flag on but no RT
    P->>B: 302 /auth/oidc/callback#token=JWT
  end

docs.title: Proactive silent refresh
docs.text:
The browser interceptor refreshes proactively ~60 seconds before the JWT expires, so the user never sees an interruption.

sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser (interceptor)
  participant P as PoracleWeb.NET API
  participant I as Provider (IdP)
  Note over B: ~60s before JWT expiry
  B->>P: POST /api/auth/oidc/refresh { refreshToken: OPAQUE }
  P->>P: hash, load session (active, not expired, not past cap)
  P->>P: atomic rotate guard (ExecuteUpdateAsync)
  P->>I: POST /token (grant=refresh_token, client_secret)
  I-->>P: { access_token, refresh_token', expires_in }
  P->>I: GET /userinfo
  P->>P: re-validate human enabled + roles
  P->>P: encrypt(refresh_token'), INSERT successor row (same family)
  P->>P: mint fresh JWT (≈30m)
  P-->>B: 200 { token, refreshToken: OPAQUE', expiresIn }

docs.title: Reactive 401 refresh
docs.text:
If a request returns 401 before the proactive timer fires, the interceptor refreshes once and retries the original request. Concurrent 401s are coalesced into a single refresh (single-flight).

sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser (interceptor)
  participant P as PoracleWeb.NET API
  participant I as Provider (IdP)
  B->>P: GET /api/... (expired JWT)
  P-->>B: 401 Unauthorized
  B->>P: POST /api/auth/oidc/refresh { refreshToken: OPAQUE }
  P->>I: POST /token (grant=refresh_token)
  I-->>P: { access_token, refresh_token', expires_in }
  P-->>B: 200 { token, refreshToken: OPAQUE', expiresIn }
  B->>P: retry GET /api/... (fresh JWT)
  P-->>B: 200 OK
  Note over B: refresh itself failing ⇒ logout (no retry loop)

docs.title: Revocation propagation
docs.text:
When the provider disables the user (or its refresh token is revoked/expired), the next refresh fails and PoracleWeb.NET revokes the family and logs the user out — provider-side revocation reaches PoracleWeb.NET within one access-token lifetime.

sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser (interceptor)
  participant P as PoracleWeb.NET API
  participant I as Provider (IdP)
  Note over I: admin disables user / logout-everywhere
  B->>P: POST /api/auth/oidc/refresh { refreshToken: OPAQUE }
  P->>P: atomic rotate guard
  P->>I: POST /token (grant=refresh_token)
  I-->>P: error (invalid_grant — revoked/disabled)
  P->>P: revoke family (same transaction)
  P-->>B: 401 { error: "invalid_grant" }
  B->>B: clear localStorage → logout

PoracleWeb.NET also re-validates the human record (exists + enabled + role gating) on every refresh, so disabling a user inside Poracle (not just at the provider) terminates the session the same way.

docs.title: Logout and family revoke
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser
  participant P as PoracleWeb.NET API
  participant I as Provider (IdP)
  B->>P: POST /api/auth/oidc/refresh/revoke { refreshToken }
  P->>P: revoke family server-side (delete stored provider RT path)
  P-->>B: 204 No Content
  B->>B: clear localStorage
  opt enable_oidc_slo
    B->>P: GET /api/auth/oidc/logout (RP-initiated end-session)
    P->>B: 302 to provider end-session (single logout)
  end

Replay protection: presenting an already-rotated (revoked) opaque token revokes the entire family in the same transaction as the 401, defeating token theft/replay.

docs.title: For any OIDC provider (self-hosters)
docs.text: The entire mechanism rests only on spec-standard OAuth2/OIDC. No assumptions are special to PogoAlerts. The provider-specific behavior is captured by config plus graceful fallback.

docs.title: The three real divergences
docs.text: Divergence How PoracleWeb.NET handles it Getting a refresh token at all. Most providers only issue one when the offline_access scope is requested. OIDC_OFFLINE_ACCESS_SCOPE (default offline_access) is appended to the authorize request only when refresh is enabled and the scope isn't already present. Set it empty for providers that issue refresh tokens unconditionally, or that use a non-standard mechanism. Token-endpoint client auth. Some providers read the secret from the form body; others require HTTP Basic. OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH_METHOD = client_secret_post (body) or client_secret_basic (HTTP Basic header). Applies to both the code exchange and the refresh grant. Refresh-token rotation. Some providers rotate the refresh token on every refresh; many return none and expect reuse of the original. PoracleWeb.NET uses newProviderRt = response.refresh_token ?? currentProviderRt — when the provider returns no new token it carries the existing one forward, re-encrypted. The opaque PoracleWeb.NET token still rotates on every call regardless.

docs.title: Graceful no-refresh-token fallback
docs.text: If you enable the flag but the provider returns no refresh token (refused, or offline_access not granted), the callback falls back to the normal 24-hour JWT with no opaque token, and logs LogOidcRefreshUnavailable. The feature simply no-ops for that login — nothing breaks. This makes first-time integration safe: turn it on, log in, and check the logs to confirm a refresh token arrived.

docs.title: Provider config matrix
docs.text:
Copy-paste the matching block into your .env. All also require the base External SSO / OIDC login variables (OIDC_ENABLED, OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_URL, OIDC_TOKEN_URL, OIDC_USERINFO_URL, OIDC_CLIENT_ID, and OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET) for your provider — see External SSO (OIDC).

Note

The same provider matrix also appears on the External SSO (OIDC) page; it is repeated here with the refresh-specific columns (OIDC_OFFLINE_ACCESS_SCOPE, OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH_METHOD) filled in.

Provider OIDC_SCOPES OIDC_OFFLINE_ACCESS_SCOPE OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH_METHOD OIDC_IDENTITY_CLAIM PogoAlerts openid profile email offline_access client_secret_post discord_id Keycloak openid profile email offline_access client_secret_basic sub Authentik openid profile email offline_access client_secret_post sub Auth0 openid profile email offline_access client_secret_post sub Google openid profile email (empty — use access_type=offline) † client_secret_post sub Azure AD / Entra openid profile email offline_access client_secret_post sub / oid Okta openid profile email offline_access client_secret_basic sub

† Google uses a non-standard access_type=offline query parameter instead of the offline_access scope. The authorize-URL builder preserves arbitrary query params on OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_URL, so append ?access_type=offline (and optionally &prompt=consent) directly to the URL and leave OIDC_OFFLINE_ACCESS_SCOPE empty.

OIDC_SCOPES=openid profile email
OIDC_OFFLINE_ACCESS_SCOPE=offline_access
OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH_METHOD=client_secret_basic
OIDC_IDENTITY_CLAIM=sub

docs.title: Tuning lifetimes
docs.text:
• OIDC_ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES trades responsiveness of revocation against refresh frequency. Shorter (e.g. 15) propagates a disable faster but refreshes more often; longer (e.g. 60) is lighter but widens the revocation window. The default 30 minutes is a reasonable middle.
  • OIDC_REFRESH_TOKEN_LIFETIME_DAYS is a PoracleWeb.NET-side absolute cap that forces a real re-login periodically. It is independent of the provider's own refresh-token lifetime — if the provider's token dies first, the refresh fails and the session is revoked anyway.

docs.title: What is NOT required
docs.text: No discovery document, id_token, or JWKS validation is needed — endpoints are configured explicitly, which also supports plain OAuth2 providers without an OIDC discovery doc. PoracleWeb.NET relies solely on /token (grant_type=refresh_token), /userinfo, and expires_in.

docs.title: Security model
docs.text:
Risk Mitigation Provider refresh-token theft The provider refresh token is encrypted at rest via ASP.NET Core DataProtection (purpose Pgan.PoracleWebNet.OidcRefresh.v1) and is never sent to the browser. The browser only ever holds an opaque PoracleWeb.NET token that is useless without the server-side session row. Opaque-token XSS (localStorage) Exposure is bounded by the short (~30 min) JWT, rotate-on-use of the opaque token, and family-revoke on replay. Recommended: set a Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self') on your reverse proxy to reduce XSS surface, since the opaque token lives in localStorage. Replay / reuse The opaque token rotates on every refresh (rotate-on-use). Presenting an already-revoked token triggers a family revoke in the same transaction as the 401, killing the whole rotation chain. The rotation guard uses an atomic conditional ExecuteUpdateAsync (affected-rows classify), no row locks. Revocation propagation Userinfo is re-fetched and the human record re-checked (exists + enabled + roles) on every refresh. A provider refresh failure (revoked/disabled) revokes the family and logs the user out. An admin-disable hook (RevokeAllForUserAsync) revokes all of a user's sessions immediately, before the ~30 min window. Absolute-cap bypass FamilyIssuedAt + RefreshTokenLifetimeDays is enforced before each rotation, forcing periodic real re-auth. Rate-limit abuse /api/auth/oidc/refresh and /api/auth/oidc/refresh/revoke run under the per-IP auth rate-limit policy (30 requests / 60s per IP). Open redirect on callback Unchanged — the existing oauth_origin CORS validation still gates the fragment redirect. Other consumers' safety Default off, additive empty table, graceful fallback when the provider returns no refresh token — instances that don't opt in are byte-for-byte unchanged.

Token hashing uses SHA-256 over 32 random bytes with a unique index — a full-entropy secret correctly uses a fast hash (never bcrypt/PBKDF2) for O(1) indexed lookup. Expired and old-revoked session rows are pruned by a background OidcSessionCleanupService (~every 6 hours, one set-based DELETE). That delete is issued as raw SQL rather than EF's ExecuteDeleteAsync, which emits an aliased DELETE FROM oidc_sessions AS o — valid on SQLite and MySQL 8, a 1064 syntax error on MariaDB (#707).

docs.text:
• External SSO (OIDC) — base External SSO / OIDC login setup (prerequisite for this page).
  • Configuration Reference — base OIDC_* provider variables.
  • Site Settings — the enable_oidc and enable_oidc_slo runtime toggles.

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text:
All configuration can be provided via environment variables or appsettings.json. The same .env file works for both Docker and standalone mode.

Short env var names

The .env file uses friendly short names (WEB_DB_HOST, JWT_SECRET, DISCORD_CLIENT_ID, etc.). The app automatically translates these to .NET's configuration format at startup. You can use either the short names or the __-delimited names shown in the table below.

docs.title: Server
docs.text: Setting Env Variable Default Description Port PORT 8082 HTTP port the app listens on. In Docker, this is the host port. Standalone, this is the port the app binds to. Server:Port Server__Port 8082 Alternative to PORT for the .NET config convention. PORT takes precedence. Ignored when ASPNETCORE_URLS is set.

docs.title: Required settings
docs.text: Setting .env name .NET env variable Description Database WEB_DB_HOST, WEB_DB_PORT, WEB_DB_NAME, WEB_DB_USER, WEB_DB_PASSWORD ConnectionStrings__PoracleWebDb MySQL connection to PoracleWeb.NET's own database. See Databases. JWT Secret JWT_SECRET Jwt__Secret JWT signing key (minimum 32 characters) Poracle API Address PORACLE_API_ADDRESS Poracle__ApiAddress PoracleNG API base URL. Critical -- all alarm tracking, human/profile management, location, and area operations are proxied through this endpoint. Poracle API Secret PORACLE_API_SECRET Poracle__ApiSecret PoracleNG API shared secret. Sent as the X-Poracle-Secret header on every request. Admin IDs PORACLE_ADMIN_IDS Poracle__AdminIds Comma-separated admin user IDs, Discord or Telegram. Admins listed in Poracle's own config are recognised too. A sign-in method see Sign-in methods At least one of Discord, Telegram or an OIDC provider

docs.title: Sign-in methods
docs.text:
PoracleWeb.NET needs at least one way for people to sign in, and any one is enough: Discord is optional, so a site can run on Telegram alone or on an OIDC provider alone. It refuses to start in two cases, each with a message naming the variables involved:

  • Discord half configured. DISCORD_CLIENT_ID without DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET, or the other way round. Set both to offer Discord sign-in, or neither to run without it.
  • No sign-in method at all. No Discord client id and secret, Telegram not enabled with a bot token, and no OIDC provider: nobody could sign in.
Method Configured when Discord DISCORD_CLIENT_ID and DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET are both set. See Discord OAuth2. Telegram TELEGRAM_ENABLED is true (inferred when TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME are both set) and TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is set. OIDC OIDC_CLIENT_ID, OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_URL, OIDC_TOKEN_URL and OIDC_USERINFO_URL are set. See External SSO / OIDC.

A method that isn't configured gets no button on the login page. Without Discord, the Discord section of Admin > Server settings says so, and its switch does nothing. The Discord bot token, guild id and forum channel are separate from sign-in and stay optional either way.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Setting .env name .NET env variable Default Description JWT Expiration — Jwt__ExpirationMinutes 1440 Token expiry (24 hours) JWT Issuer JWT_ISSUER Jwt__Issuer PoracleWeb Issuer claim (iss) baked into signed tokens. Override only if validating tokens externally. JWT Audience JWT_AUDIENCE Jwt__Audience PoracleWeb.App Audience claim (aud) baked into signed tokens. Override only if validating tokens externally. Discord Client ID DISCORD_CLIENT_ID Discord__ClientId — Discord OAuth2 application client ID. Set together with the secret, or not at all. Discord Client Secret DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET Discord__ClientSecret — Discord OAuth2 application client secret Discord Bot Token DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN Discord__BotToken — Posts geofence submissions to the forum channel and checks guild roles for role-gated Discord sign-in. Not needed for sign-in itself. Discord Guild ID DISCORD_GUILD_ID Discord__GuildId — Discord server ID Discord Geofence Forum DISCORD_GEOFENCE_FORUM_CHANNEL_ID Discord__GeofenceForumChannelId — Forum channel for geofence submission threads Discord Frontend URL — Discord__FrontendUrl http://localhost:4200 Unused. The setting class still declares it, but sign-in redirects come from PUBLIC_URL or the request; setting it changes nothing. docs.title: External SSO / OIDC
docs.text:
Optional. Delegates PoracleWeb.NET login to your own OAuth2/OIDC provider (e.g. PogoAlerts) for single sign-on. See External SSO setup for the full setup guide.
