  5. Under Message on the same tab, optionally pick a template, and set clean mode and the other message switches. Below the picker, a preview shows what the template looks like: a Discord embed for Discord accounts, a chat bubble for Telegram accounts (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, code, links and spoilers in the template's parse_mode, with a line noting a sticker or location pin the template also sends). The preview fills in sample values, so the numbers aren't yours
  6. Save the alarm

docs.title: Editing alarms
docs.text:
Open an alarm's edit dialog from its card. Changing anything and saving replaces the rule upstream.

All eleven types take a uid-addressed replace: the rule is swapped in one call rather than deleted and re-created, so there is no window in which the alarm does not exist. Lure and max battle edits used to have exactly that window and no longer do.

An edit keeps the alarm's internal id

PoracleNG 5.4.0 puts the replaced rule back under its old uid, so the card, its filters and its scope are all unchanged after a save. If PoracleNG can't reassign the id it logs that and the rule comes back under a new one, which is rare; Quick Pick applied state follows the new id, so a pick's remove button keeps working on a rule you have since edited. The card also stays where it was in the grid; see Card order.

docs.title: Where an alert reaches you
docs.text:
Every alarm answers the same question, and the Delivery tab of every add and edit dialog asks it outright: Where should this alert reach you? Three options, one radio group.

Option What it means Anywhere in my areas The alarm inherits whatever areas the active profile subscribes to. This is the default and the behaviour every alarm had before per-alarm scope existed. Near a point A radius around one fixed point. Measured from picks the point: your pin, or any saved place. Add a place in the same select opens the map picker without losing the alarm you are editing. Only in specific areas A list of areas for this alarm alone. It replaces the profile's area list rather than narrowing it, and geofences you drew yourself are offered alongside the admin areas.

The list under Only in specific areas holds the areas the active profile subscribes to, not every area on the instance, plus your own drawn geofences. On a server shared between communities the whole list is hundreds of areas from places you have nothing to do with, and this option narrows an alarm within what you already get rather than subscribing you to something new. An area the alarm already carries stays on the list even if you have since unsubscribed from it, so editing that alarm does not quietly drop it. Matching is case-insensitive, because subscriptions are stored lowercased while the area list carries the published name.

The three are exclusive rather than combinable, because PoracleNG refuses every mixture of them: a place with areas, areas with a radius, and a place without a radius are all rejected upstream. Modelling the choice as a radio group means those states can't be typed in the first place.

Under the hood the picker writes three fields. "Anywhere in my areas" clears both overrides and sends distance = 0. "Near a point" sends the radius in metres, plus override_location_label when a saved place is chosen and nothing when the pin is. "Only in specific areas" sends override_areas and forces distance to 0. Both overrides are always sent explicitly, including empty, because a null means "leave what's stored" on the write path. Without that you could set an override and never take it off.

A radius you type runs from 0.1 to 100 km. Outside that the field says so and Save stays off. An alarm already stored with a radius outside that range (the API itself allows up to half the Earth's circumference) keeps it, to the metre, through an edit that leaves the radius alone; only a changed radius is held to the range. To set a radius past 100 km on existing alarms, use the bulk Change radius. When PoracleNG sets [tracking] max_distance, Change radius stores at most that distance, the way PoracleNG caps one in the bot; PoracleNG's admins and destinations that aren't people (channels, threads, webhooks, groups) are not capped. Likewise [tracking] max_areas caps how many areas Only in specific areas can name, and Save answers with the limit when there are too many.

If you choose "Near a point" without ever having set a pin, the picker says so and offers a Set your pin button in place, rather than saving an alarm that measures from 0,0.

Under the three answers the dialog draws what you picked on a small map: the circle at the typed radius around the pin or place (drawn even when the radius is out of range, so a typo of 500 km is obvious), the chosen areas shaded, or the profile's areas for "Anywhere in my areas". Nothing is drawn when there is nothing to show yet, and under disable_location the near-a-point map is not drawn at all, since the pin and places are never read.

Your own geofences work here

PoracleWeb.NET serves user-drawn geofences with userSelectable: false to keep them out of the bot's !area picker, so PoracleNG would normally refuse them in override_areas. PoracleWeb.NET checks each name itself (selectable for you, one of your own drawn geofences, on your active profile, or already on the alarm you're editing) and then asks PoracleNG to save the alarm with those names trusted. A geofence you drew can scope one alarm whether or not your profile subscribes to it, and nothing is written to PoracleNG's database directly. See Custom geofences.

An Add that would replace another alarm is refused

PoracleNG treats an alarm that differs from one you already have in a single setting (the distance, the template or the clean flag) as an update of that alarm, not a new one. Before saving, PoracleWeb.NET asks PoracleNG what an Add would do. If it would take another alarm over, nothing changes and a single Add keeps its dialog open with your settings: a line above the buttons reads "Already covered by:" and the alarm it collided with, and Edit that one opens that alarm's edit dialog instead. When the server names no rule, the line gives its reason alone. Adding several at once closes as before, skips the clashes and reports the first reason. If the alarm already exists exactly, nothing is written. Editing an alarm into a copy of another one is refused the same way. Max battles follow the same rule, so a second alarm for the same boss that differs only by radius is refused where it used to stack.

Pokemon is the exception for the clean setting. An Add that matches an existing Pokemon rule in everything but Clean mode comes back as "already tracked" and the stored rule keeps its old setting. To change Clean mode on a Pokemon rule, edit it.

An alarm PoracleNG can't store is refused whole

A few shapes have no v2 representation: an egg without a level (old quick picks and import files can carry one), an invasion limited to gender 3, a PVP league other than 500, 1500 or 2500. Saving one fails with "PoracleNG can't store this alarm as it is: ... Nothing was changed." naming the field, rather than dropping the part PoracleNG can't hold.

docs.title: Saved places
docs.text:
A place is a named point ("home", "work", "the gym") that an alarm can measure from instead of your profile pin. They live on the Areas & places page: the area map draws each one as a labelled violet dot beside the blue pin, and the Pin and places panel under the map is where you add, move and delete them. (/places still resolves; it redirects to /areas.)

The pin is set from the My pin row of that panel, through a map picker with an address search; the search goes through PoracleNG's geocoder, and the disable_nominatim site setting hides it.

Add one with Add a place: drop the marker, then name it. Names are yours to choose and are what an alarm's override_location_label refers to. Places are user-scoped, not profile-scoped.

A name you already have is refused, and so is one longer than 64 characters — the column will not hold it. Both come back with the reason against the field rather than as a server error.

To move one, use the move button beside the bin on its row. It reopens the same map picker adding one does, and the label is untouched, so every alarm aimed at that place follows it. There is no naming step, because the label is what the alarms point at and changing it is a different act.

Moving needs a reachable PoracleNG

Every supported PoracleNG (5.4.0 and later) has the endpoint, so the move button is always there. If PoracleNG is unreachable the move fails with an error. Without the endpoint the only route would be delete-and-re-add, which is refused while any alarm still points at the place, so those alarms would have to be repointed first.

Deleting a place that alarms still point at is refused. Before any dialog opens, the bin reads GET /api/location/place-usage?label= (the active profile's rules aimed at that label, each with PoracleNG's own one-line description). If some are, an information dialog titled "place is in use" lists them (up to eight, then "and N more") with only a Close button; if none are, the ordinary delete confirm appears; if the read fails, a cautious confirm appears instead. DELETE /api/location/places/{label} still answers 409 with a referencingRules list for a rule added in between, and the snackbar names those alarms.

The API is four endpoints on LocationController, all gated by disable_location:

Endpoint Purpose GET /api/location/places Every place plus the profile pin, as { default, named }. default is null when the user has never set a pin. POST /api/location/places Saves a place. A label PoracleNG refuses comes back as a 400 the dialog shows against the field. PUT /api/location/places/{label} Moves a place, keeping its label. 409 with the version it needs on a server without the route. DELETE /api/location/places/{label} Deletes a place, or 409s with the alarms still using it.

docs.title: Changing scope from a card
docs.text: Every alarm card carries a scope chip reading the alarm's answer back to you: "Anywhere I get alerts" when the profile has no areas selected, otherwise "Anywhere in my areas", "Within 2 km of Home", "Only in Terrigal, Erina". Clicking it opens the same picker in a small dialog (on a phone, a sheet from the bottom of the screen), so one alarm's scope can be changed without opening its edit dialog.

docs.title: Default delivery scope (Alert Defaults)
docs.text:
By default, every new alarm opens pre-set to Areas (geofence-based — the alarm sends distance = 0). If you usually track by radius, you can change that default so new alarms open on Distance with a radius you choose, instead of switching the location mode and re-typing a distance on every add.

Open the user menu (your avatar, top-right) and select Alert defaults:

Setting What it does Default mode Areas or Distance for new alarms Default distance When Distance is the default, the radius (0.1–100 km) used to pre-fill new alarms. A live delivery preview shows what the choice covers Measured from Also Distance-only: the pin, or a saved place new alarms should measure from. Switching the default back to Areas clears it, since a place without a radius is a scope PoracleNG refuses

The preference is per-browser (stored in localStorage under poracle-default-alert-mode / poracle-default-alert-distance-km / poracle-default-alert-place, the same pattern as the theme and language settings) and is read by the AlertDefaultsService. It seeds the scope picker in every add-alarm dialog and in the Quick Pick apply dialog.

Applies to new alarms only

Alert Defaults only changes what the add/apply dialogs open with. Existing alarms are untouched, and you can still set a different scope on any individual alarm before saving it. Because the preference lives in the browser, it does not sync across devices.

docs.title: Pokemon Availability
docs.text: When a Golbat scanner is configured, the Pokemon selector shows which species are currently spawning in the wild. This helps users create alarms for Pokemon that are actually available to encounter.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The backend fetches spawn data from Golbat's GET /api/pokemon/available endpoint
  2. Results are cached for 5 minutes with a stale-data fallback if Golbat goes down
  3. The frontend fetches availability via GET /api/pokemon-availability and auto-refreshes every 5 minutes in the background
  4. The Pokemon selector renders availability indicators when data is available

docs.title: What the user sees
docs.text: Add by type or generation under the picker's search box opens the Gen, Type and Live > Spawning rows; the Spawning chip narrows the list to species spawning now. Small green dots mark available Pokemon in both the autocomplete dropdown and the tile grid, and unavailable ones get a muted grey dot. While any filter (Gen, Type or Spawning) is active, spawning species sort to the top, and a "X species active" label counts them.

docs.title: Feature gating
docs.text:
The availability UI is automatically hidden when Golbat is not configured. No admin toggle is needed — the feature is infrastructure-driven.

To turn it on, set GOLBAT_API_ADDRESS (the Golbat API's URL, for example http://localhost:9001) and GOLBAT_API_SECRET in your .env.

docs.title: Alarm cards
docs.text:
Alarms are displayed as a card grid, and every alarm type uses the same card:

  • the subject large at the top: the Pokémon sprite, raid boss or egg, quest reward, grunt, lure, team or event, with its name
  • on the right of the subject, the rule's status: clean, edit in place, daily summary, RSVP, and on the types that name a subject a quiet chip
  • one line of filters, each just the value ("IV 90-100%", "L30-55", "XXL", "Valor")
  • on gym, raid and egg cards, the name of the targeted gym when one was picked
  • the scope chip, saying where the alert reaches you, beside the test, edit and delete actions; click the chip to change the scope from the card
  • a Details control that opens the rule summary

Colour on a card means something or isn't there. Gym and raid cards take the team as their left edge (Mystic blue, Valor red, Instinct yellow, grey for any team), egg cards the colour of the tier's egg, and a single-species Pokémon card its primary type. Every other card has no coloured edge.

Every list has the same bar above the grid: a search box (by name, boss, tier, gym, reward, grunt, lure, move or change, depending on the type), the count, a sort menu and the select-mode toggle. When a search leaves nothing on screen the page says so and offers to clear it, and Select all selects only the cards the search left. The Pokémon list keeps its own quick filters and generation chips in the same bar.

docs.title: What this rule does, in Poracle's words
docs.text:
Behind Details on each card is the sentence PoracleNG itself uses to describe that rule. It states things the filters leave out (attack and defence floors, weight, the PVP CP cap) at the cost of restating some of what they already show.

Nine surfaces carry it: Pokémon, raids (both raid and egg cards), quests, invasions, lures, nests, gyms and Max Battles. Fort Changes does not, because upstream renders a raw JSON array there rather than a sentence. Pokéstop Events has no sentence either.

The sentence follows your Alert language, not your display language, because Poracle writes it. When the two differ the Details control is hidden rather than putting one language's prose under another language's filters. It is also absent when Poracle sends no description. Nothing extra is fetched for it: the field was already on the response.

docs.title: Card order
docs.text:
Raids, eggs, quests, invasions, lures, nests, gyms, max battles, fort changes and Pokéstop Events each sort their grid on what the card is titled by: Pokemon and level for raids and max battles, level for eggs, reward for quests, lure type, species for nests, team for gyms, change type for fort changes, event type for Pokéstop Events. An edited card therefore stays where it was instead of jumping to the end of the grid, even in the rare case where an edit gives the rule a new id.

The keys are the raw fields — dex number rather than species name, reward type rather than reward name — so the grid does not re-order itself once the master data arrives, and the order does not change with the display language. That order is Default in each list's sort menu; sorting by name, tier, reward type, Pokédex number or newest first is one click away, and ties keep the default order. The Pokémon list sorts by name by default, as it always has. Invasions sort on grunt type and gender the same way.

docs.title: Bulk operations
docs.text:
Each alarm list page has a select mode toggle (checklist icon in the toolbar):

  1. Toggle select mode on
  2. Check individual alarms or use Select all
  3. Use the bulk toolbar: Change radius sets a new radius (anything above zero, up to the API's cap of half the Earth's circumference), or no radius, on the selected alarms, and Delete removes them. The radius dialog names how many alarms you selected, and the Delete button does too ("Delete 4").

Delete is the one red, filled button in the bar, and Change radius sits beside it in a quieter tone, so the two can't be mistaken for each other. On a phone the bar is pinned to the bottom of the screen, so it stays in reach while you scroll and tick cards.

Bulk distance changes only the distance

A bulk distance update asks PoracleNG to change the distance on the selected alarms and nothing else, so every other setting on them stays as it is. PoracleNG checks each alarm separately: one it refuses doesn't stop the rest, and the confirmation says how many were skipped and why.

Message Why "Skipped N limited to areas: a radius doesn't apply to them." The alarm is limited to specific areas, which can't take a radius "Skipped N measured from a saved place: they need a radius." The alarm measures from a saved place, so a zero can't apply "Skipped N that would clash with another rule." At the new radius it would match another alarm you have exactly, or close enough that PoracleNG would merge the two. A refusal PoracleNG gives no clearer reason for is counted here too

Every alarm that was changed keeps its id. The cleaning toggle works the same way, changing only the clean setting.

The flow, for developers, is in Backend → Bulk operations.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
Users can maintain multiple alarm profiles. Only one profile is active at a time.

The Profiles page shows every alarm on every profile in one overview, and switches, edits, duplicates, deletes, exports and imports profiles from the same page. Each alarm belongs to a profile_no, and PoracleNG tracks the active one in humans.current_profile_no. Profiles covers the page in full.

docs.title: Cross-Profile Overview
docs.text: The Profiles page uses PoracleNG's v2 tracking snapshot (GET /api/v2/humans/{id}/tracking?all_profiles=true&include_descriptions=true) to fetch all alarms across all profiles in a single call. Alarms are grouped by profile (expandable accordion panels) and by type within each profile.

docs.title: Duplicating a profile
docs.text:
The Duplicate button on each profile panel creates a new profile with all alarms copied from the source profile:

  1. Click the Duplicate button on any profile panel
  2. Enter a name for the new profile (pre-filled as "<source name> (Copy)")
  3. Click Duplicate

The new profile inherits the source profile's areas, location, active hours and all alarm filters, including a role or user mention on a webhook's alarms. The copy is PoracleNG's own profile copy, and your active profile doesn't change while it runs. If the alarm copy step fails, the empty profile is rolled back (deleted) so you never end up with a shell profile.

Duplicate vs. Create

Use Duplicate when you want to start with an existing set of alarms and tweak them. Use Create when you want a blank profile.

docs.title: Profile Backup & Restore
docs.text:
Export writes a per-profile JSON backup of every alarm filter, without the internal fields (uid, id, profile_no), in the form { version: 1, exportedAt, profileName, alarms: { pokemon: [...], raid: [...], ... } }.

Import reads a backup into a new profile. The alarms are written straight to the new profile, so your active profile stays as it was, and every alarm is checked before the first one is saved. An alarm that already exists on the new profile, or would replace another, is skipped. Invasion rows that are really Pokéstop events (Kecleon, Gold Stop, Showcase) are saved as event rules, and a grunt saved as metal is imported as steel. A name you already use gets a numeric suffix, "Home (2)".

docs.title: Profile names
docs.text: The server doesn't require profile names to be unique, and accepts up to 255 characters. The dialogs are stricter: the add, duplicate and import dialogs flag a name you already use as you type, the edit dialog checks when you save, and the add and edit dialogs stop at 32 characters. Only import changes a clashing name itself, by adding a numeric suffix.

docs.title: Size filter
docs.text:
The size filter uses special sentinel values:

Value Means size = -1 No filter, all sizes. The default size = 1 to 5 A specific size: 1 = XXS, 2 = XS, 3 = Normal, 4 = XL, 5 = XXL max_size = 5 The default upper bound

When a user selects a specific size, both size and max_size are set to the same value, creating an exact match. For example, selecting XXL sets size = 5, max_size = 5.

docs.title: Costume filter
docs.text:
A Costume select sits beside Form in both Pokemon dialogs, and on raid alarms that name a specific boss. Three kinds of answer, and the sentinels are not the ones used elsewhere on this page:

Value Means 9000 Any costume, including none. The default. 0 No costume — the plain form only. N That costume and no other.

Note that 0 means "uncostumed" here, where on most other filters 0 means "any". The wildcard is 9000, matching the raid and move sentinels rather than the size filter's -1.

On raids the control appears on the By boss tab of the add dialog only, and in the edit dialog only for a rule that names a boss. A by-level raid rule is always "any costume": PoracleNG forces the boss to the wildcard on those, so there is no species for a costume to belong to. Eggs have no costume column at all.

Costume names come from the WatWowMap masterfile — the same file PoracleNG reads for its own costume lookups — and are English in every interface language. A costume too new for that file shows as its number rather than a name. See Game data names.

Always offered

The costume column exists in every supported PoracleNG (database migrations 6 for monsters.costume and 7 for raid.costume are in 5.4.0), so the select is always there and nothing asks the server first.

docs.title: Minior
docs.text: Minior's IVs, CP and level are rerolled for each player when it's caught, so a scanner may report it without stats, and a rule that filters on them never fires. Picking Minior in the Pokemon picker shows a note saying so, and the edit dialog of a Minior alarm shows it too. Track Minior with IV, CP and level left open.

docs.title: Level range
docs.text: The default maximum level is 55 (not 40 or 50), matching Poracle's support for shadow/purified/best-buddy boosted levels.

docs.title: Minimum time left
docs.text:
Under More filters, Time left skips spawns that will despawn before you could reach them. The field is a select rather than a free number, offering Any, 1, 2, 5, 10, 15 and 20 minutes. PoracleNG stores seconds (min_time), and a free field invited two silent failures: typing 5 meaning minutes asks for five seconds, and a value longer than a spawn lives mutes the alarm with no error. A value set from the bot that isn't one of the presets is kept and offered in the list rather than being overwritten on the next save.

When set, the card shows a "5 min left" pill alongside the IV and CP pills.

docs.title: PVP mega evolution
docs.text:
On the PVP tab, once a league is selected, Mega evolution chooses which form the rank applies to: Base, Mega, Mega X or Mega Y (pvp_ranking_evolution 0–3). Megas are ranked separately from their base forms, so a Mega rule will not match a base-form spawn. Pick Base unless you specifically want mega rankings.

The chosen form appears as a suffix on the card's PVP badge ("Great League · Mega X").

docs.title: Raid level selector
docs.text:
The raid and egg pickers share the <app-level-selector> chip component. The vocabulary follows the WatWowMap masterfile — the same source PoracleNG uses for in-DM notification text — so the names you see in the picker match what users receive in their alerts.

Raid picker. Multi-select. Primary chip row shows the seven most common types: 1 Star, 2 Star, 3 Star, 4 Star, Legendary (level 5), Mega (level 6), Mega Legendary (level 7). A Any chip selects the wildcard sentinel (level 9000) that matches every raid level. A More raid types… overflow menu surfaces the other 12 canonical types: Ultra Beast (8), Elite (9), Primal (10), 1–5 Shadow (11–15), 4–5 Super Mega (16–17), Coordinated 1–2 (18–19).

Egg picker. Multi-select. Only the five Star tiers (1–5) are surfaced — Pokémon GO has no Mega/Shadow/Primal eggs.

The "By boss" tab has no level picker. PoracleNG forces level to the wildcard 9000 for any raid alarm carrying a specific pokemon_id (trackingRaid.go), so a level chosen alongside a boss could never survive the request. The tab used to show a picker whose value was always discarded; it was removed in v2.14.0. Track a boss to be alerted at whatever level it appears.

+ Add. Both pickers expose an inline numeric input for any positive integer not in the canonical list. Useful for forward compatibility — if Niantic introduces a new raid type (raid_20) before PoracleWeb.NET ships an update, you can already alarm on it. Typed values are ephemeral to the dialog session: close the dialog (or refresh the page) and the chip is gone. Saved alarms at custom levels re-seed the chip when you open the edit dialog.

The canonical list is served by the API at GET /api/masterdata/raid-levels (cached server-side; baked-in fallback if the masterfile fetch fails). Card titles like "All Mega Legendary Raids" compose by combining the modifier ("Mega Legendary") with the localized "Raids" suffix from RAIDS.ALL_LEVEL_RAIDS, so card text reads naturally without the doubled word that an unaltered masterfile string would produce.

docs.title: Raid alarm filters
docs.text:
Raid alarms support these fields beyond the basic level/boss selection:

Field Default Description team 4 (any team) Gym team controlling the raid move 9000 (any move) Filter by raid boss move evolution 9000 (any) Filter by evolution type (e.g., Mega, Primal) exclusive false EX/exclusive raid flag gymId null (all gyms) Track a specific gym by ID (set via gym picker) rsvpChanges 0 (matches only) RSVP notification mode: 0 matches only, 1 matches + RSVP updates, 2 RSVP updates only. Selectable as a three-option toggle group in the raid add/edit dialog; shown as an "RSVP" / "RSVP only" status badge on raid cards (beside the auto-delete tag) when non-default. Selecting mode 1 or 2 also sets PoracleNG's edit-in-place bit (clean bit 2) so RSVP count changes edit the existing alert rather than sending a new message. Mode 2 requires the upstream scanner to emit RSVP webhooks — selecting it in deployments without one will silence the alarm.

docs.title: Egg alarm filters
docs.text:
Egg alarms support:

Field Default Description team 4 (any team) Gym team controlling the egg exclusive false EX/exclusive egg flag gymId null (all gyms) Track a specific gym by ID (set via gym picker) rsvpChanges 0 (matches only) RSVP notification mode: 0 matches only, 1 matches + RSVP updates, 2 RSVP updates only. Selectable as a three-option toggle group in the egg add/edit dialog; shown as an "RSVP" / "RSVP only" status badge on egg cards (beside the auto-delete tag) when non-default. Selecting mode 1 or 2 also sets PoracleNG's edit-in-place bit (clean bit 2) so RSVP count changes edit the existing alert rather than sending a new message. Mode 2 requires the upstream scanner to emit RSVP webhooks — selecting it in deployments without one will silence the alarm.

docs.title: Quest alarm filters
docs.text:
A quest alarm matches one reward. The Reward type dropdown on the Rewards tab decides the reward_type PoracleNG stores, and where the number you type ends up. Choosing one swaps the controls beneath it:

Reward type reward_type What you pick Minimum field Pokemon 7 Species the quest rewards (reward = pokemon id) — Items 2 The item (reward = item id) amount Mega Energy 12 Species whose energy is rewarded amount Candy 4 Species whose candy is rewarded amount Stardust 3 Nothing; the amount is the whole rule reward PokéCoins 8 Nothing; the amount is the whole rule reward

Minimum amount is the fewest of the reward the quest has to give; 0 means any. It only applies where a reward comes in a quantity: items, candy and mega energy. A Pokemon encounter has nothing to count.

Stardust and PokéCoins work differently from the rest, and identically to each other. There is nothing to pick — Poracle matches on the amount alone — so each offers a single number field, and PoracleNG reads the floor from reward rather than amount. On both, amount stays 0.

Quest cards render the amount ahead of the reward name — "3× Rare Candy" — but only when it is above one; an amount of 1 shows the reward name on its own. Stardust cards read "25000 Stardust", from reward, and PokéCoin cards read the same way.

PokéCoins is always offered

PokéCoins is the last entry in the dropdown. PoracleNG 5.2.0 widened its list of accepted reward types, so every supported release takes it and nothing asks the server first.

Reads and deletes are never refused, so a PokéCoin rule set from the Discord bot stays visible and removable.

docs.title: Gym alarm filters
docs.text:
Gym alarms support:

Field Default Description team 4 (any team) Gym team to track slotChanges false Notify when a slot opens at the gym battleChanges false Notify on battle activity changes at the gym gymId null (all gyms) Track a specific gym by ID (set via gym picker)

docs.title: Lure alarm filters
docs.text: A lure alarm names one lure type (lure_id): Normal, Glacial, Mossy, Magnetic, Rainy or Golden. Ticking several in the add dialog creates one alarm per type. Lures support Edit message in place, so a lure that's renewed updates the alert you already have.

docs.title: Nest alarm filters
docs.text: A nest alarm names the nesting species (and optionally its form) and a minimum spawns per hour (min_spawn_avg), so a nest too thin to be worth the trip stays quiet.

docs.title: Fort change alarm filters
docs.text:
Fort change alarms track changes to pokestops and gyms as points of interest (not activity at them). This includes name changes, location changes, image updates, description changes, removals, and new POI additions.

Field Default Description fort_type "everything" Fort type to track: pokestop, gym, or everything include_empty 0 (false) Include forts with no name change_types [] (all) JSON array of change types to monitor: name, location, image_url, description, removal, new

Fort change alarms are proxied through PoracleNG using tracking type "fort". The API endpoints follow the standard alarm CRUD pattern at /api/fort-changes.

docs.title: Max Battle alarm filters
docs.text:
Max Battle (Dynamax) alarms track battles at Power Spot stations. There are two tracking modes: By level tracks any Pokemon at the tiers you pick, one alarm per level, and By Pokemon tracks the Pokemon you pick at every level.

Field Default Description pokemon_id 9000 (any) Pokemon to track. 9000 = level-based tracking (any Pokemon). level 9000 (any) Battle level. Only meaningful when pokemon_id = 9000. gmax 0 (any) Gigantamax filter. 0 = matches all battles, 1 = Gigantamax only. form 0 (any) Pokemon form filter.

docs.title: Battle levels
docs.text:
Max Battle levels follow the PoracleNG util.json definitions:

Level Label Type 1 1 Star Max Battle Dynamax 2 2 Star Max Battle Dynamax 3 3 Star Max Battle Dynamax 4 4 Star Max Battle Dynamax 5 Legendary Max Battle Dynamax 7 Gigantamax Battle Gigantamax 8 Legendary Gigantamax Battle Gigantamax

No level 6

There is no level 6 in PoracleNG's max battle system. Levels 7 and 8 are Gigantamax battles where gmax is automatically derived (level > 6 = gmax).

docs.title: Duplicates and edits
docs.text: PoracleNG's older max battle handler had no duplicate check, so every Add created a row and an edit had to delete and re-create the alarm. PoracleNG 5.4.0 diffs max battles like every other type. An Add of a boss you already track that differs only by radius would merge into the existing alarm, so it's refused with the takeover message. An edit is one uid-addressed replace, a bulk distance change is a PATCH that keeps the uid, and an edit that would land on another max battle's settings is refused with a 409 before anything changes.

docs.title: Scanner-based Pokemon filter
docs.text:
When the scanner database is configured, the "By Pokemon" tab queries the station table for distinct battle_pokemon_id values. This limits the Pokemon selector to species that have actually appeared in Max Battles. If the scanner DB is not configured, all Pokemon are shown.

GymCreate.Team default

GymCreate.Team must default to 4 (any team), matching Raid and Egg defaults. A C# int defaults to 0, which maps to "Neutral only" in Poracle, causing new gym alarms to silently filter out all non-Neutral gyms.

docs.title: Gym picker
docs.text: The gym picker is a shared component (app-gym-picker) that allows users to optionally target a specific gym when creating or editing Gym, Raid, or Egg alarms. When a gym is selected, alerts only fire for events at that particular gym.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The picker displays a search field labeled "Search for a gym (optional)".
  2. As the user types (minimum 2 characters), the component debounces input (300ms) and queries the scanner database via GET /api/scanner/gyms?search=<term>&limit=20.
  3. Results appear in an autocomplete dropdown. Each option shows the gym's photo from the scanner DB (or a team icon when there's none), its name (or its ID when the name isn't set), and its area, found by checking which Koji geofence contains the gym (or its coordinates when none does).
  4. Selecting a gym sets the gymId on the alarm. A compact chip displays the selected gym's photo, name, and area with a clear button to remove the selection.
  5. In edit mode, the picker loads the existing gym's details from GET /api/scanner/gyms/{id} to display the name and photo.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• The scanner database must be configured (ConnectionStrings:ScannerDb). If not configured, the IScannerService is not registered and the search endpoints return empty results.
  • The Koji service is optional. When available, it enriches results with area names by checking gym coordinates against Koji geofence polygons.

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
• ScannerController exposes GET /api/scanner/gyms (search) and GET /api/scanner/gyms/{id} (lookup by ID).
  • IScannerService.SearchGymsAsync() queries the scanner DB's gym table by name (LIKE match), returning GymSearchResult with Id, Name, Url, Lat, Lon, TeamId, and Area.
  • Area enrichment runs server-side: for each gym result, the controller iterates Koji admin geofences and assigns the first matching fence name.

docs.title: Invasion alarm filters
docs.text:
Invasion alarms filter by grunt type and gender. A few things happen to the grunt type on the way in:

  • metal is saved as steel. PoracleNG's game data calls the grunt steel, and a metal rule never matched anything.
  • Kecleon, Gold Stop and Showcase are Pokéstop events, so picking one here saves a Pokéstop event rule instead.
  • PoracleNG stores a spaced name such as player team leader as player_team_leader.

Two catch-all rules, every grunt and every boss encounter, lost a gender limit the next time they were saved on PoracleNG builds before 22 October 2026, whose v2 read didn't report a gender on them; jfberry/PoracleNG#331 fixed the read, so a current build keeps it. The web dialogs don't create that combination; it comes from the bot.

docs.title: Pokéstop Event alarms
docs.text:
Showcases, Kecleon sightings and Gold Stops are the eleventh alarm type, on its own page at Pokéstop Events in the sidebar, directly after Invasions.

Event Stored as What it is Showcase showcase A showcase running at a pokestop Kecleon kecleon A Kecleon hiding on a pokestop Gold Stop gold-stop A pokestop that has turned gold

docs.title: Creating one
docs.text:
The add dialog has two tabs. The first, Pokéstop events, holds three checkboxes, one per event; an event you already track with the Delivery choice currently picked is unticked, disabled and labelled "Already tracked for this Delivery choice", so you can't create a duplicate. Change the Delivery choice and the same event can be ticked again, because a rule with another scope is a separate rule. Delivery is the usual scope picker, auto-delete toggle and template selector.

Ticking more than one event creates one rule per event, not one rule covering several. The edit dialog handles a single rule, so it offers one Event select rather than checkboxes.

docs.title: Eleven types, ten tables
docs.text:
Pokéstop Event rules live in the same invasion table as invasion rules; the two are told apart by the stored grunt_type. Everything else follows from that.

When you first see the Pokéstop Events page, your Invasions count drops by however many event rules you already had, and a Pokéstop Events count appears holding them. Nothing was created, deleted or moved — the same rows are being counted in two piles instead of one, and the overall total is unchanged.

The split is conditional. Where the page is switched off (Poracle reports disable_showcase = true, or an admin turned the type off), event rows stay listed and deletable under Invasions, and the invasion add dialog keeps offering the three events. The dashboard counts agree with whichever page the rows are on.

The Cleaning page's invasion toggle leaves event rows alone — it would otherwise set the auto-delete bit on rules belonging to a page it never mentions. Where the Pokéstop Events page is unavailable (Poracle reports disable_showcase = true) it sweeps them along with the invasion rules, because then that switch is the only control you have over them.

docs.title: What this type does not do
docs.text:
There's no test notification, because there's no mock payload builder for events, so no card has the More actions menu.

There's no separate section in the cross-profile overview either. Event rules appear there as invasion rows whose grunt is the event name. A profile export folds them into the invasion list the same way, an import saves them back as event rules, and a duplicate copies them with everything else.

On unless Poracle says otherwise

The page is there unless Poracle's configuration says general.disable_showcase = true. Absent or unreadable leaves it on, because every supported PoracleNG serves the v2 incident route. Like every other upstream flag this fails open: a Poracle outage must not switch off an alarm type that works.

Operators can also switch the type off here, independently of Poracle, with the disable_showcase site setting under Admin → Server settings → Alarms.

docs.title: Delivery & message modes
docs.text:
Every alarm carries a clean field that PoracleNG reads as a bitmask controlling how the notification is delivered. PoracleWeb.NET surfaces the bits the bot actually acts on as per-alarm toggles in the add/edit dialogs (and shows them as status badges on the alarm cards):

Mode (clean bit) Applies to What it does Auto-delete (bit 1) all alarm types except Fort Changes Deletes the Discord notification after the event expires (e.g. a Pokemon despawns or a raid ends). Toggle per-alarm in the dialog, or in bulk from the Cleaning page. PoracleNG has no clean column for fort changes, so the setting does not exist for that type. Edit message in place (bit 2) Lures; Pokemon; Raids/Eggs (via RSVP mode) Updates the existing Discord message when the event changes instead of sending a new one. For lures and Pokemon, enable the "Edit message in place" toggle in the alarm dialog; for raids/eggs it is set automatically when you choose an RSVP mode (see the rsvpChanges rows above). On Pokemon the toggle appears only when PoracleNG's tracking.pokemon_edit config value is true (jfberry/PoracleNG#246); when it's off, absent or unreadable the control is hidden rather than offered as a no-op, and a bit set from the bot is kept. While shown, an edit only updates the message within a short window after it was sent (the PoracleNG operator configures how long) -- a later change to the same Pokemon arrives as a threaded reply instead. Daily summary (bit 4) Quests Collects matching quests into a single summary message instead of one notification each. Enable the "Daily summary" toggle in the quest dialog. Requires a configured summary schedule on the bot.

The modes combine (a quest can be both auto-delete and daily-summary, for example). PoracleWeb.NET preserves any bits set elsewhere: if you configured a delivery mode via the bot's !command interface that isn't surfaced in the web UI, editing the alarm in the browser will not wipe it.

docs.title: RSVP updates (raids & eggs)
docs.text:
Raid and egg alarms add a third delivery setting on top of auto-delete and edit-in-place: an RSVP notification mode, stored in the rsvpChanges field (see the rsvpChanges rows under the raid and egg filter tables above). Choose it from the three-option toggle group in the raid/egg add/edit dialog:

Mode What you get Matches only (0, the default) One notification when a raid or egg matches, and nothing further Matches + RSVP updates (1) The same match alert, plus a re-notification whenever the RSVP count changes RSVP updates only (2) No match alert; a notification only when RSVP counts change

Picking mode 1 or 2 also turns on PoracleNG's edit-in-place behavior (clean bit 2), so RSVP count changes edit the existing Discord alert in place rather than sending a fresh message each time — your DMs stay to a single, updating notification per raid. When a non-default mode is set, the alarm card shows an "RSVP" (mode 1) or "RSVP only" (mode 2) status pill beside the auto-delete tag.

Scanner caveat: RSVP updates only arrive if the upstream scanner emits RSVP webhooks. In a deployment without one, mode 2 ("RSVP updates only") suppresses the initial match but never receives RSVP events — the alarm goes completely silent. Use mode 2 only if you know your scanner reports RSVPs.

docs.title: Default values
docs.text:
All monster (Pokemon) alarm defaults:

Field Default Description min_iv 0 Minimum IV percentage max_iv 100 Maximum IV percentage min_cp 0 Minimum CP max_cp 9000 Maximum CP min_level 0 Minimum level max_level 55 Maximum level min_weight 0 Minimum weight max_weight 9000000 Maximum weight atk 0 Minimum attack IV def 0 Minimum defense IV sta 0 Minimum stamina IV max_atk 15 Maximum attack IV max_def 15 Maximum defense IV max_sta 15 Maximum stamina IV pvp_ranking_best 1 Best PVP ranking position. Ranks are 1-based; a stored legacy 0 reads as 1 pvp_ranking_worst 4096 Worst PVP ranking position pvp_ranking_evolution 0 PVP form to rank against (0 = base, 1 = mega, 2 = Mega X, 3 = Mega Y) min_time 0 Minimum seconds of despawn time left (0 = no filter) gender 0 Gender filter (0 = any) costume 9000 Any costume size -1 Size filter (-1 = no filter / all sizes); a stored legacy 0 reads as -1 max_size 5 Maximum size upper bound

Raid-specific defaults:

Field Default team 4 (any team) move 9000 (any move) evolution 9000 (any evolution)

Egg-specific defaults:

Field Default team 4 (any team)

Gym-specific defaults:

Field Default team 4 (any team)

Max Battle-specific defaults:

Field Default pokemon_id 9000 (any Pokemon / level-based) level 9000 (any level) gmax 0 (any — not Gigantamax-only) move 9000 (any move) evolution 9000 (any — unused placeholder)

docs.title: Test Notifications
docs.text:
Most alarm cards have a More actions menu (the three-dot button after Delete) with a Send test notification item. It sends a sample notification for that alarm, so you can check your filters and message formatting without waiting for a real event.

The item sits behind a menu on purpose. It used to be a paper plane beside Edit, and people pressed it by accident, then went looking for a spawn that was never there (#1097). The item says so itself: its second line reads "A sample from this alarm, not a live alert".

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Open More actions on the alarm card and choose Send test notification
  2. PoracleWeb.NET builds a mock webhook payload using the alarm's actual filter values (e.g., pokemon_id, raid_level, quest_reward) and the user's saved location as the event coordinates
  3. The payload is sent to PoracleNG's POST /api/test endpoint, which formats it with the user's template and delivers it to their DMs, or to the destination when they're managing one
  4. Once PoracleNG has accepted the test, PoracleWeb.NET sends one short plain-text note to the same destination through POST /api/deliverMessages (see below)
  5. A snackbar displays the result: success, error, or cooldown warning. While the request is out, the More actions button turns into a spinner

docs.title: The note that follows a test
docs.text:
A test notification is built from your alarm's filters and your saved location, so it looks like a live one. The bot also sends this note to the same place (your DMs, or the channel, thread or webhook when you manage a destination):

Test notification from PoracleWeb.NET: the alert sent with this note is a sample built from your alarm's filters at your saved location. It isn't a live alert, so there's nothing to go and find.

The note is English only, because the backend doesn't localise any message text. It can arrive just before the sample as well as just after it: the sample goes through PoracleNG's render queue and the note doesn't, so the note never refers to the alert as "above" or "below". It is sent only after PoracleNG accepted the test, so a refused or unreachable test sends none. If the note itself fails, the test still counts as sent: the API logs a warning (the alarm type, the uid and the kind of destination, never the destination's address) and the member sees the usual success message. Because the note goes through PoracleNG's delivery queue, it counts toward PoracleNG's own per-destination delivery limits, so each test counts as two messages.

docs.title: Supported alarm types
docs.text:
Test notifications are available for eight of the eleven alarm types:

  • Pokemon
  • Raid
  • Egg
  • Quest
  • Invasion
  • Lure
  • Nest
  • Gym

Not Fort Change, Max Battle or Pokéstop Event — TestAlertController rejects all three, and none of those modules renders the More actions menu. They have no mock payload builder, so there is nothing to send.

docs.title: Clearing a test notification
docs.text: A test notification, and the note that follows it, are real DMs sent by the bot. This site never sees them and cannot take them back. The bot can: send it poracle-clean as a direct message, prefixed with your server's command prefix, and it deletes its own recent messages from that conversation. That includes real alerts, not only the tests. The FAQ on the Help page carries the same answer with your own instance's prefix filled in.

docs.title: Rate limiting
docs.text:
Test notifications are rate limited to prevent abuse:

The server allows 5 test notifications per 60 seconds per user (per IP address only for a request with no token). The browser adds a 15-second cooldown per alarm: the menu item is dimmed and its second line reads Cooldown active. It also drops a repeat click while a request for that alarm is still in flight.

docs.title: Weather Display
docs.text: The dashboard shows the current in-game weather conditions at the user's pin.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
It shows the in-game weather at the pin and in each of your selected areas, with the time the data was last refreshed, and refreshes in the background.

Pin required

The weather display requires a saved pin to function. Users who have not set one will not see weather information on the dashboard. Set a pin on the Areas & places page or through the onboarding wizard.

docs.title: Quick Picks
docs.text:
Admins can define Quick Pick templates — pre-configured alarm sets that users can apply with one click. Useful for onboarding new users or sharing recommended configurations.

When applying a Quick Pick, the apply dialog's Delivery tab holds the same scope picker the add dialogs use, seeded from your Alert Defaults. Whatever you choose there (areas, a saved place, a radius, or a specific set of areas) applies to every alarm the pick creates.

Applying a pick creates only the alarms that are new. One that already exists, or would replace another alarm of yours, is skipped, and the confirmation counts only the alarms it created.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Quiet Periods — silence one gym, area, species or station for a while without touching the alarms themselves
  • Quest Summary Delivery — collecting matching quests into one digest
  • Profiles — keeping separate alarm sets and switching between them
  • PoracleNG Version Compatibility — which features need which server

docs.title: Discord and Telegram
docs.text:
PoracleNG delivers alerts through two apps, Discord and Telegram, and a server can run either or both. Each app keeps its own accounts. A person who uses both has two PoracleNG accounts, a discord:user and a telegram:user, with their own alarms, areas, location and profiles. PoracleWeb.NET signs people in with either, and linking lets one person treat the two as one.

This page is for operators deciding what to offer and for members wondering which app to use. The Telegram setup itself is in Telegram.

docs.title: What each app does
docs.text:
Discord Telegram Sign in to PoracleWeb.NET Discord OAuth2 (see Discord OAuth2) Telegram's login widget, on the one domain set with /setdomain Turn sign-in on DISCORD_CLIENT_ID and secret (optional: leave both unset on a Telegram-only site), plus the enable_discord site setting TELEGRAM_ENABLED, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME, plus the enable_telegram site setting PoracleNG account type discord:user telegram:user How a person registers A registration channel (!poracle), or a role listed in user_role that grants access without registering Sending /poracle in a registration group the bot is in; optionally /start in a DM with register_on_start Bot commands Prefix ! by default (!location, !profile) Prefix / (/location, /profile) Direct messages The bot can DM anyone who shares a server with it and allows DMs from server members The bot can DM only someone who has started a chat with it (pressing Start, or allowing messages in the login widget) Destinations Webhooks, channels and threads Channels, groups and topics Mentions on an alarm A role or a person, on a webhook, channel or thread (the Mention field) Not offered Periodic access check [discord] check_role: still in a guild and holding a role [telegram] check_role: still in a registration group Area security communities discord = { channels, user_role } telegram = { channels }

Test notifications, quiet periods, quest summaries, profiles and clean mode work the same on both. The message itself comes from PoracleNG's templates, which can differ per app.

Destinations are covered in Destinations & delegates. They are never linked: a Telegram group and a Discord channel stay separate destinations, each with its own alarms.

docs.title: Registering on each app
docs.text:
PoracleWeb.NET doesn't register anyone by default. A person has to exist in PoracleNG before they can sign in, and signing in with an app they haven't registered on answers "Your account is not registered".

On Discord, the server's own setup decides. Usually it's a role from the community's Discord server (PoracleNG's user_role, or a community's user_role with area security), or !poracle in a registration channel.

On Telegram, PoracleNG only registers someone who is a member of a registration group, and only the bot can check that. The usual route is to join the group and send /poracle there. The bot reacts, posts a welcome in the group, and DMs a confirmation, which arrives only once the person has started a chat with the bot. Telegram has every route and what each one says.

The one exception is Register the other account when linking (link_register_missing). Set to Always, linking creates the missing account on the other app, skipping that app's registration rules. Set to When qualified, it creates a missing Telegram account only for someone who is in a registration group.

docs.title: From never used Poracle to both apps
docs.text:
This diagram follows a member who starts with neither account and ends with both linked and receiving alerts. The Telegram branch is the same whether they link first or register first.

flowchart TD
    A[Never used Poracle] --> B{Which app first?}
    B -->|Discord| C[Get the server's role, or send !poracle in the registration channel]
    B -->|Telegram| D[Join the registration group and send /poracle there]
    D --> D2[Press Start in a DM with the bot]
    C --> E[Sign in to PoracleWeb.NET with that app]
    D2 --> E
    E --> F[Open Linked accounts and link the other app]
    F --> G{Other app registered?}
    G -->|Yes| H[Both sides: Receiving alerts]
    G -->|No, always, or when-qualified and in a registration group| I[Site creates the account, copying areas, location, profiles and places]
    I --> H
    G -->|No, off, or when-qualified and not in a group| J[Other side: Waiting to register]
    J --> K[Register on the other app the usual way]
    K --> H
    H --> L[Choose the default app, then pick the app per alarm]

docs.title: What linking ties together
docs.text:
Linking pairs one discord:user with one telegram:user. Nothing is merged inside PoracleNG: there are still two accounts, and PoracleNG still sends each alert from the account that holds the alarm. PoracleWeb.NET does the joining.

  • Alarms are listed together, each marked with its app, and each alarm goes to one app. You pick the app per alarm and can move alarms between apps.
  • Person-level settings (location, saved places, areas, profiles, language, quiet periods, summary schedules, and alerts on or off) are saved to both accounts from the site.
  • Bot commands change one account only. When the two drift apart, PoracleWeb.NET shows the difference and lets the person choose which app's setting to keep.

The full behaviour is in Linked accounts.

docs.title: Choosing what to offer
docs.text: Running only Discord needs nothing on this page. Adding Telegram means a bot, a registration group and Telegram sign-in on the site; Telegram walks through it. Linking is on by default once both sign-ins work, and the Linked accounts settings cover the choices an operator makes.

docs.title: Internationalization (i18n)
docs.text: PoracleWeb.NET supports 11 UI languages. Users can switch the interface language at any time without reloading the page.

docs.title: Supported Languages
docs.text:
Flag Language Code English en (baseline) Français fr Deutsch de Español es Nederlands nl Italiano it Português pt Português (BR) pt-BR Polski pl Dansk da Svenska sv

Every language carries the full set of interface keys. Some text stays in English whatever you pick: move, item and costume names, and anything stored rather than translated, such as quick-pick names and the site title. In Dutch, Portuguese, Brazilian Portuguese and Danish, Pokemon names are English too, because Poracle has no translation to serve. What is not translated has the full list.

docs.title: Frontend (Angular)
docs.text:
The UI translation system uses ngx-translate for runtime language switching:

Translation files are stored in ClientApp/src/assets/i18n/{code}.json as namespaced JSON, and changing language updates every visible string straight away, with no page reload.

The language a visitor lands on is decided in this order, first match winning:

  1. A language they chose before, from localStorage('poracle-ui-language').
  2. A browser language this site ships. de-AT matches de; pt-BR matches exactly before falling back to pt.
  3. Poracle's own locale, read from its configuration. A German community running Poracle with locale = "de" therefore greets a first-time visitor in German rather than English, without configuring anything here.
  4. English.

Only a deliberate choice is written to localStorage. A language picked automatically is left unwritten so it can be re-decided next visit — otherwise the first page load would be authoritative forever, and a visitor who arrived while Poracle was unreachable would stay on English no matter what the server reported afterwards.

Poracle's locale has to clear the same two filters as any other option: this site must ship that language, and allowed_languages must permit it. Poracle carries translations for languages this UI does not have, and those simply do not qualify.

docs.title: Language selectors
docs.text:
There are two, and they sit next to each other in the user menu (top-right toolbar):

Display language changes this site's text and nothing else. Its submenu is hidden when an admin has restricted the selector to a single language.

Alert language is what Poracle writes your DMs in: alert text, Pokemon names, move names. The authoritative copy lives on your Poracle account (humans.language), with a browser cache used only for the first render, so it follows you between devices and reconciles if the bot changes it.

Its list is Poracle's to restrict, not this site's. Poracle publishes the language codes it accepts (availableLanguages on GET /api/config/poracleWeb), and the alert-language submenu offers only those — intersected with the eleven this UI has a flag row for. Restrict Poracle to English and German and those are the two rows you get; restrict it to languages this UI does not ship and the menu item disappears rather than offering a write Poracle answers 422 to. A Poracle that restricts nothing publishes no list and every language stays on offer.

allowed_languages does not apply here. It is this site's restriction on the display language, and it has nothing to say about what Poracle writes DMs in — the two menus answer to different owners.

Note that Pokemon names, types and forms in this site's own screens follow the display language, not the alert language — see Game data names below. Setting the display language to German gives you Bisasam in the species picker and Käfer on the type chips; the alert language decides what your DMs say.

Each submenu opens with its own hint line ("Changes this site's text only." / "Used for alert text and Pokemon names.") and lists the languages as flag and native name, with a check mark against the active one. Both draw from the same list of 11.

The two settings are independent. A German UI with English Pokemon names is a normal thing to want, and the menu now shows that they are separate rather than leaving it to a footnote.

This moved

The alert language used to live on the Areas page. It is in the user menu as of the Areas and Places merge, alongside the display language it kept being confused with.

docs.title: Admin Configuration
docs.text:
Admins can restrict which languages appear in the selector by setting the allowed_languages site setting:

Setting Value Effect allowed_languages (empty) All 11 languages available allowed_languages en,de,fr Only English, German, and French shown

English is always available regardless of the allowed_languages setting. The restriction applies to the signed-out login page as well as to signed-in users. It governs the display language only — see the alert-language note above.

Set this in Admin → Server settings under the Features category. Directly beneath it, the page reports Poracle's own configured locale as a read-only line — the default a new visitor lands on, per the order above. It is Poracle's to set, not this site's: it is read from Poracle's configuration on every load and cannot be edited or overridden here.

docs.title: Translation File Structure
docs.text:
Each language file uses namespaced keys organized by feature area:

{
  "NAV": {
    "DASHBOARD": "Dashboard",
    "POKEMON": "Pokemon",
    "RAIDS": "Raids"
  },
  "MENU": {
    "PAUSE_ALERTS": "Pause alerts",
    "LOGOUT": "Logout"
  },
  "DASHBOARD": {
    "TITLE": "Dashboard",
    "WELCOME": "Welcome back, {{username}}"
  }
}

docs.title: Key Namespaces
docs.text: Namespace Content NAV Navigation sidebar labels TOOLBAR Toolbar buttons and tooltips BANNER Status banners (impersonation, paused, disabled) MENU User menu items SHORTCUTS Keyboard shortcut overlay TOAST / HTTP_ERROR Toast notifications and HTTP error messages DASHBOARD Dashboard page POKEMON Pokemon alarm management RAIDS Raid & egg alarm management QUESTS Quest alarm management INVASIONS Invasion alarm management POKESTOP_EVENTS Pokéstop Event alarm management LURES Lure alarm management NESTS Nest alarm management GYMS Gym alarm management FORT_CHANGES Fort change alarm management MAX_BATTLES Max battle alarm management QUIET Quiet periods: chips, duration sheet and the dashboard's Quiet item AREAS Areas & places page PROFILES Profile management GEOFENCES Custom geofences CLEANING Clean mode settings QUICK_PICKS Quick pick alarm presets HELP Help page: section titles, search, and the guide body HTML AUTH Login page ADMIN Admin pages ALARM Shared alarm dialog fields DIALOG Shared dialog components TEST_ALERT Test notification feedback WHERE Per-alarm delivery scope and saved places ALERT_DEFAULTS Alert defaults dialog ALARM_INFO Shared alarm summary component ACTIVE_HOURS_CHIP Profile schedule pills LOCATION_WARNING Missing-coordinates warning banner ONBOARDING First-run wizard DELIVERY_PREVIEW Delivery preview map AREA_MAP Shared area map component REGION_SELECTOR Region picker for geofence submission GEOFENCE_DETAIL Geofence detail view GEOJSON_IMPORT GeoJSON import dialog GYM_PICKER Gym autocomplete POKEMON_SELECTOR Species picker TEMPLATE / TEMPLATE_SELECTOR Notification template picking and preview ADMIN_SETTINGS Admin settings page PAGINATOR Material paginator labels ERROR Error page and interceptor messages COMMON Common labels (Save, Cancel, Delete, etc.)

docs.title: Interpolation
docs.text:
Dynamic values use double-brace syntax: {{variable}}. These must be preserved exactly in translations:

{
  "WELCOME": "Welcome back, {{username}}",
  "AREAS_COUNT": "{{count}} area(s) active"
}

docs.title: HTML in Translations
docs.text:
Some values contain HTML tags (mainly <strong>) for emphasis. These must be preserved in translations and rendered with [innerHTML] binding:

{
  "PAUSED_ALERTS": "Your alerts are <strong>paused</strong>. You will not receive notifications."
}

docs.title: Contributing Translations
docs.text:
To improve or add translations:

  1. Edit the relevant src/assets/i18n/{code}.json file
  2. Ensure all keys from en.json are present (missing keys fall back to English)
  3. Preserve {{placeholders}} and HTML tags exactly
  4. Keep technical terms untranslated: Pokemon, Discord, Poracle, DM, IV, CP, PVP, ATK, DEF, STA
  5. Keep game proper nouns: Mystic, Valor, Instinct, Giovanni, Team Rocket, Dynamax, Gigantamax, PokéStop
  6. Use informal forms (du/tu/tú/je) appropriate for a gaming community

docs.title: Game data names
docs.text:
Pokemon names, their types and their form names are not in the translation files at all. They come from Poracle, which translates them from its own i18n bundle, and this site asks for them in the display language:

GET /api/masterdata/monsters?locale=de
  1_0  -> Bisasam,  types: Gift, Pflanze
 12_0  -> Smettbo,  types: Flug, Käfer

Switching the display language re-fetches them, so an open species picker updates in place. Searching works on the translated names too — typing bi finds Bisasam.

Three things this does not cover:

Move and item names stay English. Poracle serves no translated equivalent for them, so they come from the WatWowMap masterfile as before.

Costume names stay English too, in every interface language. They're not in the endpoint above: the poracle-shaped masterfile carries no costume map, so the costume picker reads the raw WatWowMap file, the same one Poracle downloads for its own costume lookups. Poracle translates costume names internally but exposes no endpoint serving them. A costume too new for that file shows as its number rather than a name.

A Poracle that can't answer (unreachable, or without the endpoint) falls back to the same English masterfile, so the pickers keep working rather than emptying out.

docs.title: Rule summaries follow the alert language
docs.text:
The sentence at the foot of each alarm card describing what the rule does is written by Poracle, not by this site, so it arrives in your alert language while the pills above it follow your display language.

When the two differ, the sentence is hidden rather than shown. A card carrying German chips over an English sentence is worse than a card carrying chips alone, and there is no way to ask Poracle for the summary in a second language. Set the two selectors to the same language to see it.

Poracle ships translations for de, en, es, fr, it, ja, nb-no, pl, ru, sv and zh-cn. Four of this site's languages — nl, pt, pt-BR and da — have no counterpart there, so game data names appear in English while the interface around them is translated.

docs.title: What Is NOT Translated
docs.text:
• move, item and costume names (see above)
  • what admins configure: the site title, logo, custom navigation links, quick-pick names and descriptions
  • what users name: profiles, geofences, saved places, and area names from Koji

The help guide is translated, body and all: the HELP.CONTENT_* values carry the HTML for each section and every locale has its own. The 38 HELP.SECTION_* headings are complete too. Dutch, German and Italian leave one of them reading as English ("Dashboard"), because that is the word in those languages as well.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
ClientApp/
  src/
    assets/i18n/           # Translation JSON files
      en.json              # English (baseline, ~1,900 keys)
      de.json              # German
      fr.json              # French
      ...
    app/
      core/services/
        i18n.service.ts    # Language management service
      app.config.ts        # ngx-translate provider setup

The I18nService:

  • Wraps @ngx-translate/core's TranslateService
  • Manages available languages (filtered by admin allowed_languages setting)
  • Handles browser language detection on first visit, and falls back to Poracle's configured locale when the browser asks for a language this site does not ship
  • Records how the active language was chosen, so a locale arriving from the server after bootstrap replaces a bare English fallback but never a stored or browser-matched choice
  • Provides instant() for synchronous translation in TypeScript code
  • Sets document.documentElement.lang for accessibility

Translation files are loaded lazily via HTTP — only the active language file is fetched. Switching languages fetches the new file and caches it for the session.

docs.title: Linked Accounts
docs.text:
Someone who gets alerts on both Discord and Telegram has two PoracleNG accounts, and PoracleNG treats them as two people. Linking pairs one Discord account with one Telegram account so that PoracleWeb.NET treats them as one person: one list of alarms, the app chosen per alarm, and personal settings saved to both.

Linking never copies or moves alarms, and unlinking deletes nothing. Settings are copied only when the site creates your other account for you (see the settings below). For how the two apps differ and how people register on each, see Discord and Telegram. For how the pair is stored and resolved, see the technical page.

docs.title: Linking
docs.text:
Open Linked accounts from the user menu or under Settings in the sidebar. There's a card for each app, and what it offers depends on how you signed in:

  • Signed in with Telegram. Press Link Discord, approve the sign-in on Discord, and you come back to the page with the link made.
  • Signed in with Discord. Use the Telegram button on the Telegram card and approve it in Telegram.

An app is offered only when its sign-in is set up on the site and switched on. When it isn't, its card says this site doesn't offer that app's sign-in, so it can't be linked here. An account can be in one link at a time, and only personal accounts link: a channel, group, thread or webhook never does. While an admin is viewing the site as you, the page says the link is yours to manage and offers nothing.

docs.title: If a link is refused
docs.text:
The page says why, and what to try next. Dismiss the message with its close button.

Message starts What happened Linking accounts has been switched off on this site An admin turned linking off while you were linking. Nothing was changed You can only link a Discord account to a Telegram account The account isn't a personal Discord or Telegram account, or both sides are the same app That account couldn't be read The id Discord or Telegram sent can't be an account id, or the Telegram login didn't verify That account is already used here as a channel or group That id is registered here as a destination, not a person That account is already linked to someone else Unlink it from the other account first That sign-in took too long A Telegram login is good for ten minutes after you approve it, and a Discord link for ten minutes after you press Link Discord. Start again This site doesn't offer sign-in with that app That app's sign-in isn't set up on this site, or an admin switched it off. Ask the site team if you expected it That account can't sign in to this site The account fails this site's own sign-in rules, such as a required Discord role You cancelled the link You backed out of the Discord approval. Nothing was changed The accounts couldn't be linked Something none of the above covers, or the link was lost part way. Nothing was changed; try again Your other account couldn't be set up The site tried to create the other account and couldn't. Nothing was linked

docs.title: Each side's state
docs.text:
Each card says where that account stands.

State Meaning You're signed in with this account The account you're using now, before anything is linked Not linked No account on this app is linked yet Receiving alerts The account exists and Poracle is sending it alerts Waiting to register The account is linked but Poracle doesn't know it yet. Alerts on that app start once you register there Alerts stopped You stopped alerts on that account. Start them in that app Paused by an admin An admin blocked the account. The card offers Get help when the site has a support link

PoracleWeb.NET never turns a stopped or paused account back on. That's for the person or the admins on that app.

Waiting to register on Telegram. Join the server's Telegram registration group and send /poracle there. If the admins set a registration group link, the card shows a Join the Telegram group button. Press Start in a chat with the bot as well, or it can't DM you.

Waiting to register on Discord. Register the way the site's admins ask, usually by getting a role on the community's Discord server. The card shows Get help when the site has a support link.

docs.title: Where new alarms go
docs.text:
Once both accounts are registered, New alarms go to picks the app for alarms you add. It's a default for new alarms only; existing alarms stay where they are, and every dialog lets you choose differently. An app that isn't receiving alerts is marked "(not receiving alerts)" and can't be picked. If it's already the default, the page says nothing sent there will arrive and suggests the other app. While one side is still waiting to register, the page says the choice comes once both are registered.

Applying any quick pick creates its alarms on the default app, or on the account you're signed in with while the default app isn't registered.

docs.title: Alarms on both apps
docs.text:
Every alarm list shows the alarms of both accounts together. Each card names the app it goes to, with "alerts off" when that app isn't receiving alerts, and Delivered to: All / Discord / Telegram above the list filters by app.

Every add and edit dialog asks Which app gets this alarm? above its tabs. A new alarm starts on the default app. Picking the other app in an edit moves the alarm there when you save.

To move several, tick them in select mode and choose Deliver to… (on a phone it's under More). An app every ticked alarm is already on is greyed out. The result counts what moved, what was already there, and what wasn't moved and why.

docs.title: How a move works
docs.text:
A move creates the alarm on the other account first and deletes the original only once that worked, so an alarm is never lost on the way. If the delete fails, both copies stay and the message says so: "Moved to Telegram, but the Discord copy is still there. Delete it from the list."

A move is refused, with nothing changed, when:

Reason shown What to do Discord and Telegram are on different profiles Switch one app's active profile to match, then move again. The Linked accounts page offers this as a difference to fix The place "Home" isn't saved on Telegram Save that place on the other app first, or match saved places on Linked accounts It's limited to an area Telegram can't use Change the alarm's areas, then move it Telegram already has an alarm like it Telegram has an alarm that differs from this one only in its radius, template or clean setting. Edit or delete one of them, then move again. An identical alarm isn't refused: the move counts it as done and removes this copy Telegram isn't set up yet The other side is still waiting to register Alerts can't be moved while inspecting another account An admin viewing as you can't move your alarms

docs.title: Settings saved to both apps
docs.text:
Saving any of these on the site saves it to both accounts: location, saved places, areas, profiles (names, schedules, areas and location), language, quiet periods, quest summary schedules, and alerts on or off.

The account you signed in with is saved first. If the other app refuses or doesn't answer, what you saved stands on the first app and you see one message naming both, such as "Saved for Discord, but not for Telegram: the alert service didn't answer. Try again in a minute. Review the difference on Linked accounts." Its Review button opens Linked accounts, where the difference is waiting. Nothing is rolled back.

docs.title: When the two accounts differ
docs.text:
Poracle's bot commands change one account only. The site can't stop the two from drifting, so it shows the drift and lets you choose.

A worked example. You're linked, and both apps are set to Old Town. On the bus you send /location with a pin in Riverside to the Telegram bot. Telegram's account now measures distances from Riverside; Discord's still uses Old Town. Next time you open a page on the site, a one-line banner under the toolbar says "Discord and Telegram have different settings." with Review. On Linked accounts the Location line reads "Discord's is in Old Town, Telegram's is in Riverside, 4 km apart." Under Use Discord's it says "Telegram moves to Discord's location."; under Use Telegram's, "Discord moves to Telegram's location." You press Use Telegram's, a message confirms "Discord now has Telegram's location.", and the line goes.

docs.title: What's compared
docs.text:
Line What it names Location Both places at the same level of detail and the distance between them. Never raw coordinates Areas The areas only one app has, in Poracle's spelling Profiles Profiles only one app has, and for shared ones whether the name, schedule or areas differ Active profile The profile each app is using, by name Saved places Places only one app has, and places in different spots

Language, quiet periods and quest summary schedules are saved to both but not compared. Quiet periods, for one, live only in Poracle's memory and vanish when it restarts, so they'd show as different for no reason.

docs.title: Choosing a side
docs.text:
Each line has Use Discord's and Use Telegram's, and under each button what it changes on the other app. Nothing is ever resolved for you.

  • A choice that deletes a profile or saved place from the other app asks first, naming what goes ("Delete Weekend from Telegram").
  • If that deletes the profile the other app is using, the line says that app switches profile, so its areas and location change too.
  • A profile that still holds alarms on the other app isn't deleted, and neither is a saved place that alarms there still use. The message names the app and what to change first.
  • The active profile can only be matched once the other app has that profile, so Profiles comes first in the list.
  • If either app changed since the list was drawn, you're told "That changed in the meantime", nothing is overwritten, and the list shows what differs now.
  • If a choice stops part way, the page says so and the list shows what still differs.

Dismiss on the banner hides it for the rest of the browser session. A new or changed difference shows it again, and the list on Linked accounts always shows everything. The banner appears when a page opens, never in the middle of one, and isn't shown on Linked accounts itself or while an admin is viewing as you.

docs.title: Profile 0
docs.text: Some older accounts have a profile 0. Poracle never gives a new profile that number, so the other account can't have one. The pair leaves profile 0 out: it isn't compared, copied, renamed, switched to or deleted, and its alarms stay on the account that has it. The page says which account has one, for example "Your Discord account has an older profile 0 that Telegram can't have. Its alarms stay on Discord."

docs.title: Unlinking
docs.text:
Press Unlink on the page and confirm. Both accounts and all their alarms stay; they just stop being treated as one person. Admins can do the same from Admin > Users, where a linked account has a chip naming the other app and its row menu has Unlink accounts.

On a site that offers only one app's sign-in, unlinking is one way. You can't link the other app again or reach its alarms from this site afterwards, so the confirm says so: move any alarms you want to keep to the app you're signed in with first. Admin > Server settings > Linked accounts names an app people can't link and why (not set up in .env, or its Enable … login switch is off).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
The settings are under Admin > Server settings > Linked accounts and in Site settings.

Setting Key Default What it does Linked accounts disable_account_linking On Off hides the page and refuses every link route. Each person acts as their single account again. Links are kept for when it's switched back on, and Admin > Users can still unlink them Register the other account when linking link_register_missing Off Off saves the link and the missing side waits.
